SECTION A: Project Foundation, Monorepo
Setup, Environment Configuration, and
Complete Tech Stack
This document provides an exhaustive technical specification for the foundational elements of
the EliTutor platform. It covers the project’s core architecture, monorepo setup using pnpm
workspaces, environment configuration, and the complete technology stack. This guide is
designed for developers who are new to the EliTutor ecosystem, assuming no prior knowledge
of its internal workings. Every file, function, and line of logic is meticulously detailed to ensure a
seamless onboarding and development experience.

1. Project Foundation: EliTutor Platform Overview
EliTutor is a gamified educational web platform designed for Israeli Arab school students across
Grades 1-12. The platform aims to provide a comprehensive learning experience covering all
subjects, including Arabic, Hebrew, English, Math, and Science, strictly adhering to the Koter
curriculum. The platform is browser-only, ensuring accessibility without the need for dedicated
mobile applications.
Key Features:

Gamified Learning: Incorporates game-like elements such as points, badges,
leaderboards, and interactive challenges to enhance student engagement and motivation.
Comprehensive Curriculum Coverage: Aligns with the Koter curriculum for all subjects
and grade levels, ensuring educational relevance and compliance.
Multi-lingual Support: Supports Arabic, Hebrew, and English content, catering to the
diverse linguistic needs of Israeli Arab students.
Interactive Content: Delivers dynamic and engaging learning materials, including quizzes,
exercises, and multimedia resources.
Progress Tracking: Monitors student performance and progress, providing personalized
feedback and adaptive learning paths.
Parent/Teacher Dashboards: Offers insights into student activity and performance for
educators and guardians.

2. Monorepo Setup with pnpm Workspaces
EliTutor utilizes a monorepo structure managed by pnpm workspaces. This approach centralizes
code management, facilitates code sharing between different parts of the application, and
streamlines dependency management. The monorepo will host multiple packages, including the
main NestJS backend application, a React frontend application, shared libraries, and potentially
other utilities.

2.1. Root package.json
The root package.json defines the monorepo’s workspaces and common scripts. It does not
contain direct dependencies for the applications themselves, but rather development tools and
scripts that apply across the entire monorepo.
File Path: /package.json

{
"name": "elitutor-monorepo",
"version": "1.0.0",
"private": true,
"description": "Monorepo for the EliTutor gamified educational web platform.",
"keywords": [
"elitutor",
"education",
"gamification",
"nestjs",
"react",
"typescript",
"monorepo"
],
"scripts": {
"build": "pnpm --filter \"./packages/**\" build",
"start": "pnpm --filter \"./packages/**\" start",
"lint": "eslint \"**/*.{ts,tsx}\"",
"lint:fix": "eslint \"**/*.{ts,tsx}\" --fix",
"format": "prettier --write \"**/*.{ts,tsx,json,md}\"",
"prepare": "husky install"
},
"devDependencies": {
"@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin": "7.13.0",
"@typescript-eslint/parser": "7.13.0",
"eslint": "8.57.0",
"eslint-config-prettier": "9.1.0",
"eslint-plugin-prettier": "5.1.3",
"husky": "9.0.11",
"prettier": "3.3.2",
"typescript": "5.4.5"
},
"pnpm": {
"peerDependencyRules": {
"ignoreMissing": [
"webpack"
]
}
},
"workspaces": [
"packages/*",
"apps/*"
]
}

Explanation:

name , version , private , description , keywords : Standard package metadata.
scripts :
build : Executes the build script in all packages within the packages directory.
start : Executes the start script in all packages within the packages directory.
lint : Runs ESLint across all TypeScript and TSX files in the monorepo.
lint:fix : Runs ESLint with auto-fixing enabled.
format : Formats all TypeScript, TSX, JSON, and Markdown files using Prettier.
prepare : Installs Husky Git hooks, ensuring code quality checks before commits.
devDependencies : Contains development tools used across the monorepo.
@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin , @typescript-eslint/parser , eslint ,
eslint-config-prettier , eslint-plugin-prettier : ESLint and TypeScript

integration for linting.
husky : Git hooks manager.
prettier : Code formatter.
typescript : TypeScript compiler.
pnpm.peerDependencyRules.ignoreMissing : Configures pnpm to ignore missing peer

dependencies for webpack , which might be a peer dependency of some frontend tools but
not directly used in the root.
workspaces : Defines the directories where pnpm will look for packages. In this case,
packages/* for shared libraries and apps/* for applications.

2.5. tsconfig.json for Each Package
Each package within the monorepo will have its own tsconfig.json file, extending a base
configuration for consistency.
2.5.1. Root tsconfig.base.json
This file defines the common TypeScript compiler options for all packages.
File Path: /tsconfig.base.json

{
"compilerOptions": {
"target": "es2021",
"module": "commonjs",
"lib": ["es2021", "dom"],
"declaration": true,
"strict": true,
"esModuleInterop": true,
"skipLibCheck": true,
"forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
"noEmit": true,
// Monorepo path aliases
// "paths": {
//

"@elitutor/dtos": ["./packages/dtos/src"]

// }
},
"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}

Explanation:
compilerOptions :
target : Specifies the ECMAScript target version.
module : Specifies the module code generation.
lib : List of library files to be included in the compilation.
declaration : Generates declaration files ( .d.ts ).
strict : Enables all strict type-checking options.
esModuleInterop : Enables compatibility with CommonJS modules.
skipLibCheck : Skips type checking of all declaration files.
forceConsistentCasingInFileNames : Ensures consistent file casing.
noEmit : Do not emit output (used for base config, actual emission handled by

specific packages).
paths : (Commented out example) Used for monorepo path aliases, allowing

imports like @elitutor/dtos .
exclude : Specifies files and folders to exclude from compilation.

File Path: /apps/api/tsconfig.json

{

compilerOptions :
module , declaration , removeComments , emitDecoratorMetadata ,
experimentalDecorators , allowSyntheticDefaultImports , sourceMap ,
outDir , baseUrl , incremental : Specific options for NestJS compilation.
strictNullChecks , noImplicitAny , strictBindCallApply ,

2.6. ESLint and Prettier Configuration
Consistent code style and quality are enforced using ESLint for linting and Prettier for code
formatting.
2.6.1. Root .eslintrc.js
File Path: /.eslintrc.js

module.exports = {
root: true,
env: {
node: true,
jest: true,
},
parser: '@typescript-eslint/parser',
parserOptions: {
project: 'tsconfig.json',
sourceType: 'module',
},
plugins: ['@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin'],
extends: [
'plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended',
'plugin:prettier/recommended',
],
rules: {
'@typescript-eslint/interface-name-prefix': 'off',
'@typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type': 'off',
'@typescript-eslint/explicit-module-boundary-types': 'off',
'@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any': 'off',
},
};

Explanation:
root : Marks this as the root ESLint configuration.
env : Defines global variables that are predefined.
parser : Specifies the parser to use, @typescript-eslint/parser for TypeScript.
parserOptions : Configuration for the parser, including project for type-aware linting.
plugins : ESLint plugins to use.
extends : Extends recommended configurations from @typescript-eslint and
prettier .
rules : Custom ESLint rules, overriding or adding to the extended configurations.

Common NestJS-related rules are turned off for flexibility.
2.6.2. Root .prettierrc
File Path: /.prettierrc

{
"semi": true,
"trailingComma": "all",
"singleQuote": true,
"printWidth": 120,
"tabWidth": 2,
"useTabs": false
}

Explanation:
semi : Prints semicolons at the end of statements.
trailingComma : Prints trailing commas wherever valid in ES5.
singleQuote : Uses single quotes instead of double quotes.
printWidth : Specifies the line length that Prettier will wrap on.
tabWidth : Specifies the number of spaces per indentation level.
useTabs : Indent with spaces instead of tabs.

2.7. Husky Pre-commit Hooks
Husky is used to manage Git hooks, ensuring that code is linted and formatted before every
commit. This helps maintain code quality and consistency across the development team.
File Path: /.husky/pre-commit

#!/usr/bin/env sh
. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
pnpm lint
pnpm format

Explanation:
This script is executed automatically before a commit is created.
pnpm lint : Runs the lint script defined in the root package.json , which executes

ESLint.
pnpm format : Runs the format script defined in the root package.json , which

executes Prettier.

If either of these commands fails (e.g., due to linting errors or unformatted code), the commit will
be aborted, prompting the developer to fix the issues.

3. Environment Configuration
Environment variables are crucial for configuring the application in different deployment
environments (development, staging, production). A .env.example file provides a template for
all necessary environment variables, along with clear explanations.

3.1. Complete .env.example
File Path: /.env.example

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Core Application Settings
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# The port on which the NestJS backend application will listen.
# Default: 3000
PORT=3000
# The environment in which the application is running (e.g., development,
production, test).
# This affects logging, error handling, and other environment-specific behaviors.
# Default: development
NODE_ENV=development
# The base URL for the frontend application. Used for CORS and potentially for
generating absolute URLs.
# Example: http://localhost:5173 (for local development)
FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:5173
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Database Configuration (PostgreSQL)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# PostgreSQL database host. For Docker Compose, this will be the service name.
# Default: localhost (or 'db' if using Docker Compose)
DATABASE_HOST=db
# PostgreSQL database port.
# Default: 5432
DATABASE_PORT=5432
# PostgreSQL database username.
# Default: postgres
DATABASE_USER=postgres
# PostgreSQL database password.
# Default: postgres
DATABASE_PASSWORD=postgres
# PostgreSQL database name for the application.
# Default: elitutor_db
DATABASE_NAME=elitutor_db
# Whether to synchronize database schema with TypeORM entities on application
startup.
# USE WITH CAUTION IN PRODUCTION. Set to 'true' for development, 'false' for
production.
# Default: false

DATABASE_SYNCHRONIZE=false
# Whether to log SQL queries. Set to 'true' for debugging, 'false' for
production.
# Default: false
DATABASE_LOGGING=false
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Redis Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Redis host. For Docker Compose, this will be the service name.
# Default: localhost (or 'redis' if using Docker Compose)
REDIS_HOST=redis
# Redis port.
# Default: 6379
REDIS_PORT=6379
# Redis password (if any).
# Default: (empty)
REDIS_PASSWORD=
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# MinIO (S3-compatible Storage) Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# MinIO endpoint URL. For Docker Compose, this will be the service name and port.
# Example: http://localhost:9000 (or 'minio:9000' if using Docker Compose)
MINIO_ENDPOINT=minio
# MinIO access key.
# Default: minioadmin
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=minioadmin
# MinIO secret key.
# Default: minioadmin
MINIO_SECRET_KEY=minioadmin
# MinIO bucket name for storing application assets.
# Default: elitutor-assets
MINIO_BUCKET_NAME=elitutor-assets
# Whether to use SSL for MinIO connection. Set to 'false' for local development
with HTTP.
# Default: false
MINIO_USE_SSL=false
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# JWT (JSON Web Token) Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Secret key for signing JWTs. MUST be a strong, random string in production.
# Example: supersecretjwtkey (DO NOT use this in production)
JWT_SECRET=supersecretjwtkey
# Expiration time for access tokens (e.g., '15m', '1h', '7d').
# Default: 1h
JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME=1h
# Expiration time for refresh tokens.
# Default: 7d
JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME=7d
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Rate Limiting Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Maximum number of requests allowed within the time window.
# Default: 100
THROTTLE_LIMIT=100
# Time window in milliseconds for rate limiting.
# Default: 60000 (1 minute)
THROTTLE_TTL=60000
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Other Security Settings
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------# Secret for cookie signing. MUST be a strong, random string in production.
# Example: supersecretcookiekey (DO NOT use this in production)
COOKIE_SECRET=supersecretcookiekey

Explanation:
Each variable is documented with its purpose, default value, and examples where applicable.
This ensures that any developer can quickly understand and configure the application’s
environment.

4. Complete Tech Stack
This section details the core technologies used in EliTutor, focusing on the backend NestJS
application and its foundational setup.

4.1. Docker Compose for Local Development
Docker Compose is used to orchestrate local development services, providing a consistent and
isolated environment for PostgreSQL, Redis, and MinIO.
File Path: /docker-compose.yml

version: '3.8'
services:
db:
image: postgres:16-alpine
restart: always
environment:
POSTGRES_DB: ${DATABASE_NAME:-elitutor_db}
POSTGRES_USER: ${DATABASE_USER:-postgres}
POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD:-postgres}
ports:
- "5432:5432"
volumes:
- db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
healthcheck:
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${DATABASE_USER:-postgres} -d
${DATABASE_NAME:-elitutor_db}"]
interval: 5s
timeout: 5s
retries: 5
redis:
image: redis:7-alpine
restart: always
command: redis-server --appendonly yes --requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
ports:
- "6379:6379"
volumes:
- redis_data:/data
healthcheck:
test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "--raw", "INFO"]
interval: 5s
timeout: 5s
retries: 5
minio:
image: minio/minio
restart: always
ports:
- "9000:9000"
- "9001:9001" # MinIO Console port
environment:
MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ACCESS_KEY:-minioadmin}
MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_SECRET_KEY:-minioadmin}
command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
volumes:
- minio_data:/data
healthcheck:

test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live"]
interval: 30s
timeout: 20s
retries: 3
volumes:
db_data:
redis_data:
minio_data:

Explanation:
db service (PostgreSQL 16):
image: postgres:16-alpine : Uses the official PostgreSQL 16 image (alpine

variant for smaller size).
restart: always : Ensures the container restarts if it crashes.
environment : Sets PostgreSQL environment variables, pulling values from .env or

using defaults.
ports : Maps container port 5432 to host port 5432.
volumes : Persists database data to a named volume db_data .
healthcheck : Defines a health check to ensure the database is ready before the

application connects.
redis service (Redis 7):
image: redis:7-alpine : Uses the official Redis 7 image (alpine variant).
restart: always : Ensures the container restarts if it crashes.
command : Starts Redis with append-only persistence and an optional password.
ports : Maps container port 6379 to host port 6379.
volumes : Persists Redis data to a named volume redis_data .
healthcheck : Checks Redis server status.
minio service (MinIO for S3-compatible storage):
image: minio/minio : Uses the official MinIO image.
restart: always : Ensures the container restarts if it crashes.
ports : Maps container ports 9000 (API) and 9001 (Console) to host ports.
environment : Sets MinIO root user and password, pulling values from .env or

using defaults.

command : Starts the MinIO server and console.
volumes : Persists MinIO data to a named volume minio_data .
healthcheck : Checks MinIO server health.
volumes : Defines named volumes for persistent data storage, ensuring data is not lost

when containers are recreated.

4.2. NestJS Application Bootstrap
The NestJS backend application is the core of the EliTutor platform. This section details its
bootstrap process, including main.ts , app.module.ts , global middleware, CORS, rate
limiting, Helmet security headers, and compression.
4.2.1. main.ts - Application Entry Point
This file is the entry point of the NestJS application, responsible for creating the application
instance, applying global configurations, and starting the server.
File Path: /apps/api/src/main.ts

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';
import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common';
import * as compression from 'compression';
import helmet from 'helmet';
import * as cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
/**
* @function bootstrap
* @description Initializes and starts the NestJS application.
* This function sets up global pipes, middleware, security headers, and starts
the HTTP server.
* @returns {Promise<void>}
*/
async function bootstrap(): Promise<void> {
const logger = new Logger('Bootstrap');
// Create the NestJS application instance
const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
// Retrieve ConfigService to access environment variables
const configService = app.get(ConfigService);
const port = configService.get<number>('PORT') || 3000;
const frontendUrl = configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ||
'http://localhost:5173';
const cookieSecret = configService.get<string>('COOKIE_SECRET') ||
'supersecretcookiekey';
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------// Global Pipes
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------/**
* @description Applies global validation pipe to all incoming requests.
* This pipe automatically validates DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) using classvalidator.
* - `whitelist: true`: Strips properties that are not defined in the DTO.
* - `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`: Throws an error if non-whitelisted
properties are sent.
* - `transform: true`: Automatically transforms incoming payload objects to
DTO instances.
*/
app.useGlobalPipes(
new ValidationPipe({
whitelist: true,
forbidNonWhitelisted: true,

transform: true,
}),
);
logger.log('Global ValidationPipe applied.');
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------// Global Middleware
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------/**
* @description Applies Helmet middleware for securing HTTP headers.
* Helmet helps protect the application from common web vulnerabilities by
setting various HTTP headers.
* It's a collection of 14 smaller middleware functions that set securityrelated HTTP headers.
*/
app.use(helmet());
logger.log('Helmet security middleware applied.');
/**
* @description Applies compression middleware for Gzip compression.
* This middleware compresses response bodies for all requests that traverse
through it,
* potentially speeding up your web application.
*/
app.use(compression());
logger.log('Compression middleware applied.');
/**
* @description Applies cookie-parser middleware.
* This middleware parses Cookie header and populates `req.cookies` with an
object keyed by cookie names.
* It's essential for handling JWTs stored in HTTP-only cookies.
*/
app.use(cookieParser(cookieSecret));
logger.log('CookieParser middleware applied.');
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------// CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) Configuration
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------/**
* @description Configures CORS to allow requests from the frontend
application.
* - `origin`: Specifies the allowed origin(s). In production, this should be
the exact frontend URL.
* - `methods`: Allowed HTTP methods.
* - `credentials`: Allows cookies and authorization headers to be sent with
cross-origin requests.

*/
app.enableCors({
origin: frontendUrl,
methods: 'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE,OPTIONS',
credentials: true,
});
logger.log(`CORS enabled for origin: ${frontendUrl}`);
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------// Application Startup
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------/**
* @description Starts the NestJS application, listening for incoming HTTP
requests.
* The application will listen on the port specified in the environment
variables or default to 3000.
*/
await app.listen(port);
logger.log(`Application is running on: ${await app.getUrl()}`);
logger.log(`Listening on port ${port}`);
}
// Call the bootstrap function to start the application
bootstrap().catch((error) => {
const logger = new Logger('BootstrapError');
logger.error('Application failed to start:', error);
process.exit(1);
});

Explanation:
Imports: Essential modules like NestFactory , AppModule , ValidationPipe ,
compression , helmet , cookieParser , ConfigService , and Logger are imported.
bootstrap() function:
NestFactory.create(AppModule) : Creates an instance of the NestJS application,

passing the root AppModule .
Environment Variables: ConfigService is used to retrieve PORT ,
FRONTEND_URL , and COOKIE_SECRET from environment variables, providing

sensible defaults.
Global Pipes ( ValidationPipe ):
app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe(...)) : Configures a global
ValidationPipe to automatically validate incoming request payloads (DTOs).

whitelist: true : Ensures that only properties defined in the DTO are

accepted, stripping any unknown properties.
forbidNonWhitelisted: true : If whitelist is true, this will throw an error

if non-whitelisted properties are present in the payload.
transform: true : Automatically transforms incoming JSON payloads into

instances of the DTO classes, allowing for class-validator decorators to work
correctly.
Global Middleware:
app.use(helmet()) : Integrates the helmet middleware, which sets various

HTTP headers to enhance security (e.g., X-Content-Type-Options, StrictTransport-Security).
app.use(compression()) : Integrates the compression middleware,

enabling Gzip compression for all outgoing responses, reducing payload size
and improving load times.
app.use(cookieParser(cookieSecret)) : Integrates cookie-parser to

parse incoming cookies. The cookieSecret is used for signing cookies, which
is crucial for security, especially with HTTP-only cookies for authentication.
CORS Configuration ( app.enableCors ):
origin: frontendUrl : Specifies the allowed origin for cross-origin requests.

This should be the URL of the frontend application. Using FRONTEND_URL from
environment variables makes it configurable for different environments.
methods: 'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE,OPTIONS' : Defines the

HTTP methods allowed for cross-origin requests.
credentials: true : Allows the browser to send and receive cookies and

HTTP authentication credentials (like Authorization headers) with crossorigin requests. This is essential for JWT-based authentication where tokens
might be stored in HTTP-only cookies.
Application Startup:
await app.listen(port) : Starts the NestJS HTTP server, making the

application accessible on the configured port.
Logging: Provides informative messages about the application’s status and
URL.
Error Handling: A .catch() block is included to log any errors that occur during the
bootstrap process and gracefully exit the application.

4.2.2. app.module.ts - Root Application Module
The AppModule is the root module of the NestJS application. It aggregates all other modules,
services, controllers, and providers, defining the overall structure of the application.
File Path: /apps/api/src/app.module.ts

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppController } from './app.controller';
import { AppService } from './app.service';
import { ConfigModule } from '@nestjs/config';
import { TypeOrmModule } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
import { ThrottlerModule } from '@nestjs/throttler';
import { AuthModule } from './auth/auth.module';
import { UsersModule } from './users/users.module';
import { DatabaseConfigService } from './config/database-config.service';
import { ThrottlerConfigService } from './config/throttler-config.service';
/**
* @module AppModule
* @description The root module of the EliTutor NestJS application.
* This module imports and configures all other feature modules, global
configurations,
* and services that are essential for the application's operation.
*/
@Module({
imports: [
/**
* @description Configures the global ConfigModule to load environment
variables.
* - `isGlobal: true`: Makes the ConfigService available everywhere without
explicit import.
* - `envFilePath`: Specifies the path to the .env file. In a monorepo, it's
often at the root.
*/
ConfigModule.forRoot({
isGlobal: true,
envFilePath: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test' ? '.env.test' : '.env',
}),
/**
* @description Configures TypeORM for database integration.
* Uses `TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync` to dynamically configure database
settings
* using `DatabaseConfigService`, allowing environment-specific
configurations.
*/
TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync({
useClass: DatabaseConfigService,
}),
/**
* @description Configures the global ThrottlerModule for rate limiting.
* Uses `ThrottlerModule.forRootAsync` to dynamically configure rate limiting
settings
* using `ThrottlerConfigService`, allowing environment-specific
configurations.

*/
ThrottlerModule.forRootAsync({
useClass: ThrottlerConfigService,
}),
// Feature Modules
AuthModule,
UsersModule,
// ... other feature modules (e.g., CoursesModule, GradesModule,
GamificationModule)
],
controllers: [AppController],
providers: [AppService],
})
export class AppModule {}

Explanation:
@Module Decorator: Defines the module and its metadata.
imports :
ConfigModule.forRoot : Configures the @nestjs/config module to load

environment variables. isGlobal: true makes ConfigService available
throughout the application. envFilePath is conditionally set for testing
environments.
TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync : Asynchronously configures TypeORM. It uses
DatabaseConfigService to provide database connection options, allowing for

dynamic configuration based on environment variables.
ThrottlerModule.forRootAsync : Asynchronously configures the rate limiting

module. It uses ThrottlerConfigService to provide rate limiting options
(TTL and limit), also dynamically configurable.
Feature Modules: AuthModule , UsersModule , and other future feature
modules are imported here, making their controllers and providers available
within the application context.
controllers : Declares the controllers belonging to this module (e.g.,
AppController ).
providers : Declares the services and other providers belonging to this module

(e.g., AppService ).
4.2.3. database-config.service.ts - TypeORM Configuration
This service provides the dynamic configuration for TypeORM, pulling database credentials and
settings from environment variables.

File Path: /apps/api/src/config/database-config.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { TypeOrmOptionsFactory, TypeOrmModuleOptions } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
/**
* @class DatabaseConfigService
* @implements {TypeOrmOptionsFactory}
* @description Provides TypeORM configuration options dynamically based on
environment variables.
* This allows for flexible database connection settings across different
environments (development, production, test).
*/
@Injectable()
export class DatabaseConfigService implements TypeOrmOptionsFactory {
constructor(private configService: ConfigService) {}
/**
* @method createTypeOrmOptions
* @description Creates and returns TypeORM module options.
* It retrieves database connection details from the ConfigService.
* @returns {TypeOrmModuleOptions}
*/
createTypeOrmOptions(): TypeOrmModuleOptions {
const synchronize = this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_SYNCHRONIZE')
=== 'true';
const logging = this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_LOGGING') ===
'true';
return {
type: 'postgres',
host: this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_HOST'),
port: this.configService.get<number>('DATABASE_PORT'),
username: this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_USER'),
password: this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_PASSWORD'),
database: this.configService.get<string>('DATABASE_NAME'),
entities: [__dirname + '/../**/*.entity{.ts,.js}'], // Path to your TypeORM
entities
synchronize: synchronize, // WARNING: Set to false in production!
logging: logging,
autoLoadEntities: true,
};
}
}

Explanation:

@Injectable() : Marks the class as a provider that can be injected into other classes.
TypeOrmOptionsFactory : Implements this interface to provide TypeORM options

asynchronously.
Constructor: Injects ConfigService to access environment variables.
createTypeOrmOptions() method:

Retrieves database host, port, user, password, and name from ConfigService .
entities : Specifies the glob pattern for finding TypeORM entity files. This ensures

all entities are registered with the ORM.
synchronize : CRITICAL WARNING: synchronize: true automatically creates

database tables based on entities. This is convenient for development but extremely
dangerous in production as it can lead to data loss. It should always be false in
production environments.
logging : Enables or disables SQL query logging, useful for debugging.
autoLoadEntities : Automatically loads entities registered with TypeORM.

4.2.4. throttler-config.service.ts - Rate Limiting Configuration
This service provides the dynamic configuration for the @nestjs/throttler module, pulling
rate limiting settings from environment variables.
File Path: /apps/api/src/config/throttler-config.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { ThrottlerOptionsFactory, ThrottlerModuleOptions } from
'@nestjs/throttler';
/**
* @class ThrottlerConfigService
* @implements {ThrottlerOptionsFactory}
* @description Provides ThrottlerModule configuration options dynamically based
on environment variables.
* This allows for flexible rate limiting settings across different environments.
*/
@Injectable()
export class ThrottlerConfigService implements ThrottlerOptionsFactory {
constructor(private configService: ConfigService) {}
/**
* @method createThrottlerOptions
* @description Creates and returns ThrottlerModule options.
* It retrieves rate limiting details (TTL and limit) from the ConfigService.
* @returns {ThrottlerModuleOptions}
*/
createThrottlerOptions(): ThrottlerModuleOptions {
const ttl = this.configService.get<number>('THROTTLE_TTL') || 60000; //
Default to 1 minute
const limit = this.configService.get<number>('THROTTLE_LIMIT') || 100; //
Default to 100 requests
return [
{
ttl: ttl,
limit: limit,
},
];
}
}

Explanation:
@Injectable() : Marks the class as a provider.
ThrottlerOptionsFactory : Implements this interface to provide Throttler options

asynchronously.
Constructor: Injects ConfigService to access environment variables.
createThrottlerOptions() method:

Retrieves THROTTLE_TTL (time to live for records in milliseconds) and
THROTTLE_LIMIT (maximum requests within the TTL) from ConfigService ,

providing sensible defaults.
Returns an array of ThrottlerModuleOptions , allowing for multiple rate limiting
policies if needed.

To apply rate limiting globally, the ThrottlerGuard is registered as a global guard in main.ts
or provided at the application level.

While

is

configured

in

AppModule ,

the

File Path: /apps/api/src/app.module.ts (Modified providers section)

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppController } from './app.controller';
import { AppService } from './app.service';
import { ConfigModule } from '@nestjs/config';
import { TypeOrmModule } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
import { ThrottlerModule, ThrottlerGuard } from '@nestjs/throttler';
import { AuthModule } from './auth/auth.module';
import { UsersModule } from './users/users.module';
import { DatabaseConfigService } from './config/database-config.service';
import { ThrottlerConfigService } from './config/throttler-config.service';
import { APP_GUARD } from '@nestjs/core'; // Import APP_GUARD
@Module({
imports: [
ConfigModule.forRoot({
isGlobal: true,
envFilePath: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test' ? '.env.test' : '.env',
}),
TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync({
useClass: DatabaseConfigService,
}),
ThrottlerModule.forRootAsync({
useClass: ThrottlerConfigService,
}),
AuthModule,
UsersModule,
],
controllers: [AppController],
providers: [
AppService,
/**
* @description Registers ThrottlerGuard as a global guard.
* This applies rate limiting to all routes in the application.
* The `APP_GUARD` token is used to register global guards that are part of

*/
{

},
],

By providing ThrottlerGuard with the APP_GUARD token, NestJS automatically applies
this guard to all routes throughout the application. This ensures that the rate limiting
configured in ThrottlerConfigService is enforced globally.

4.2.6. Global Exception Filter (Example)
While not explicitly requested, a global exception filter is a crucial part of a robust NestJS
application for consistent error handling and logging. Here’s an example.
File Path: /apps/api/src/common/filters/all-exceptions.filter.ts

import {
Catch,
ArgumentsHost,
HttpException,
HttpStatus,
Logger,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import { BaseExceptionFilter } from '@nestjs/core';
/**
* @class AllExceptionsFilter
* @extends {BaseExceptionFilter}
* @description A global exception filter to catch all unhandled exceptions
across the application.
* It logs errors and sends a standardized error response to the client.
*/
@Catch()
export class AllExceptionsFilter extends BaseExceptionFilter {
private readonly logger = new Logger(AllExceptionsFilter.name);
/**
* @method catch
* @description Catches an exception and processes it.
* @param {unknown} exception The caught exception.
* @param {ArgumentsHost} host Provides access to the arguments of the original
request.
*/
catch(exception: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost) {
const ctx = host.switchToHttp();
const response = ctx.getResponse();
const request = ctx.getRequest();
const status =
exception instanceof HttpException
? exception.getStatus()
: HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
const message =
exception instanceof HttpException
? exception.getResponse()
: 'Internal server error';
const errorResponse = {
statusCode: status,
timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
path: request.url,
message: typeof message === 'object' ? (message as any).message || message
: message,

// Include stack trace only in development environment
stack: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' ? (exception as any).stack :
undefined,
};
this.logger.error(
`HTTP Status: ${status} Error Message: ${JSON.stringify(errorResponse)}`,
(exception as any).stack,
);
response.status(status).json(errorResponse);
}
}

Explanation:
@Catch() : Decorator indicates that this is an exception filter and, when empty, catches all

exceptions.
extends BaseExceptionFilter : Extends NestJS’s base exception filter for easier

implementation.
catch(exception, host) method:

Extracts response and request objects from the ArgumentsHost .
Determines the HTTP status code: HttpException instances provide their status;
otherwise, it defaults to HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR .
Extracts the error message, handling both HttpException responses and generic
errors.
Constructs a standardized errorResponse object, including statusCode ,
timestamp , path , and message . The stack trace is conditionally included based

on NODE_ENV for security in production.
Logs the error using NestJS’s Logger .
Sends the errorResponse back to the client with the appropriate HTTP status.
To apply this global filter, it needs to be registered in main.ts .
File Path: /apps/api/src/main.ts (Modified bootstrap function)

import { NestFactory, HttpAdapterHost } from '@nestjs/core'; // Import
HttpAdapterHost
import { AppModule } from './app.module';
import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common';
import * as compression from 'compression';
import helmet from 'helmet';
import * as cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AllExceptionsFilter } from './common/filters/all-exceptions.filter'; //
Import the filter
async function bootstrap(): Promise<void> {
const logger = new Logger('Bootstrap');
const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
const configService = app.get(ConfigService);
const port = configService.get<number>('PORT') || 3000;
const frontendUrl = configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ||
'http://localhost:5173';
const cookieSecret = configService.get<string>('COOKIE_SECRET') ||
'supersecretcookiekey';
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------// Global Exception Filter
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------/**
* @description Registers a global exception filter to catch and handle all
unhandled exceptions.
* This ensures consistent error responses and logging across the application.
* It must be instantiated using `app.get(HttpAdapterHost)` to correctly bind
to the HTTP adapter.
*/
const { httpAdapter } = app.get(HttpAdapterHost);
app.useGlobalFilters(new AllExceptionsFilter(httpAdapter));
logger.log('Global AllExceptionsFilter applied.');
// ... rest of main.ts (Global Pipes, Middleware, CORS, etc.)
app.useGlobalPipes(
new ValidationPipe({
whitelist: true,
forbidNonWhitelisted: true,
transform: true,
}),
);

logger.log('Global ValidationPipe applied.');
app.use(helmet());
logger.log('Helmet security middleware applied.');
app.use(compression());
logger.log('Compression middleware applied.');
app.use(cookieParser(cookieSecret));
logger.log('CookieParser middleware applied.');
app.enableCors({
origin: frontendUrl,
methods: 'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE,OPTIONS',
credentials: true,
});
logger.log(`CORS enabled for origin: ${frontendUrl}`);
await app.listen(port);
logger.log(`Application is running on: ${await app.getUrl()}`);
logger.log(`Listening on port ${port}`);
}
bootstrap().catch((error) => {
const logger = new Logger('BootstrapError');
logger.error('Application failed to start:', error);
process.exit(1);
});

Explanation:
HttpAdapterHost is injected to correctly bind the AllExceptionsFilter to the

underlying HTTP server (Express in this case). This ensures that the filter can intercept
exceptions before they are handled by the default Express error handler.

6. Prisma Schema Snippets (Example for User Entity)
While TypeORM is used for database interaction, it’s beneficial to also define the database
schema using a tool like Prisma for clear schema definition and potential future migrations or
client generation. Here’s an example for a User entity.
File Path: /apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma (This file would be part of a separate prisma
package or directly in api if Prisma is used for migrations/client)
generator client {
provider = "prisma-client-js"
}
datasource db {
provider = "postgresql"
url

= env("DATABASE_URL") // DATABASE_URL should be defined in .env

}
model User {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

email

String

@unique

password

String

firstName String?
lastName

String?

isActive

Boolean

@default(true)

createdAt DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt DateTime

@updatedAt

roles

@default(["STUDENT"]) // Example: STUDENT, TEACHER, ADMIN

String[]

@@map("users") // Maps the model to a 'users' table in the database
}

Explanation:
generator client : Configures the Prisma Client generator.
datasource db : Defines the database connection. url pulls from DATABASE_URL

environment variable, which would be constructed from the individual DATABASE_HOST ,
DATABASE_PORT , etc., variables.

model User : Defines the User database table structure.
id : Unique identifier, generated as a UUID.
email : User’s email, must be unique.
password : Hashed password.
firstName , lastName : Optional first and last names.
isActive : Boolean flag for account status.
createdAt , updatedAt : Timestamps for record creation and last update.
roles : An array of strings to define user roles (e.g., STUDENT , TEACHER , ADMIN ).
@@map("users") : Explicitly maps the User model to a database table named
users .

This comprehensive section lays the groundwork for the EliTutor platform, providing all
necessary details for developers to understand and begin working on the project’s foundation.
The emphasis on clear documentation, consistent tooling, and robust configuration ensures a
scalable and maintainable codebase.

SECTION B: Complete PostgreSQL Database Schema using
Prisma ORM

SECTION B: Complete PostgreSQL Database
Schema using Prisma ORM
This section provides an exhaustive definition of the EliTutor platform’s PostgreSQL database
schema, implemented using Prisma ORM. It covers every single model, detailing their fields,
data types, relationships, indexes, and enums. Furthermore, it includes the complete seed script
for populating sample data and all necessary Prisma migration commands. This document is
designed to be the sole reference for developers working on the database layer, assuming no
prior knowledge of the system.

1. Database Models Definition
1.1. User Model
The User model serves as the foundational entity for authentication and authorization within the
EliTutor platform. It stores core user information, including credentials and basic profile details.
This model is central to linking various user-specific data across the application.
File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model User {
id

String

@id @default(auto())

email

String

@unique

passwordHash

String

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

role

UserRole

@default(STUDENT)

isVerified

Boolean

@default(false)

lastLogin

DateTime? // Optional: Stores the last login timestamp

// Relations
accounts

Account[]

sessions

Session[]

studentProfile

StudentProfile? // One-to-one relation with StudentProfile

parentProfile

ParentProfile?

achievements

UserAchievement[]

// One-to-one relation with ParentProfile

weeklyXpRecords WeeklyXpRecord[]
notifications

Notification[]

leagueGroupMembers LeagueGroupMember[]
@@map("users") // Map to a custom table name
}
enum UserRole {
STUDENT
PARENT
ADMIN
TEACHER
}

Field Descriptions:
id : A unique identifier for the user. Generated automatically by Prisma.

Type: String
Constraints: Primary Key, Auto-generated ( @id @default(auto()) )

email : The user’s email address. Must be unique across all users and is used for login.

Type: String
Constraints: Unique ( @unique )
passwordHash : The hashed password for the user. Stores a secure, one-way hash of the

user’s password, never the plain text.
Type: String
createdAt : Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Default to current timestamp ( @default(now()) )
updatedAt : Timestamp indicating the last time the user account was updated.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Automatically updated on record change ( @updatedAt )
role : The role of the user within the platform (e.g., STUDENT, PARENT, ADMIN,

TEACHER). Defaults to STUDENT .
Type: UserRole (Enum)
Constraints: Default to STUDENT
isVerified : A boolean flag indicating whether the user’s email address has been

verified.
Type: Boolean
Constraints: Default to false
lastLogin : An optional timestamp recording the user’s last successful login.

Type: DateTime? (Nullable)
Relationships:
accounts : One-to-many relationship with the Account model, representing external

accounts linked to the user (e.g., OAuth accounts).
sessions : One-to-many relationship with the Session model, tracking active user

sessions.
studentProfile : One-to-one optional relationship with StudentProfile . A User can

have at most one StudentProfile .
parentProfile : One-to-one optional relationship with ParentProfile . A User can

have at most one ParentProfile .

achievements : One-to-many relationship with UserAchievement , tracking achievements

earned by the user.
weeklyXpRecords : One-to-many relationship with WeeklyXpRecord , tracking weekly

experience points.
notifications : One-to-many relationship with Notification , storing notifications for

the user.
leagueGroupMembers : One-to-many relationship with LeagueGroupMember , linking users

to their league groups.
Enums:
enum UserRole {
STUDENT
PARENT
ADMIN
TEACHER
}

UserRole : Defines the possible roles a user can have in the system.
STUDENT : A student user, primarily focused on learning activities.
PARENT : A parent user, responsible for monitoring student progress and managing

settings.
ADMIN : An administrative user with full system access.
TEACHER : A teacher user, responsible for managing courses and students.

Indexes:
No specific indexes are defined on the User model beyond the primary key and unique email
constraint, as Prisma automatically handles these. Additional indexes can be added if specific
query patterns require them for performance optimization.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Duplicate Email: Attempting to create a new user with an email that already exists will
result in a P2002 (Unique constraint failed) error from Prisma. The application layer must
handle this by informing the user that the email is already registered.
Invalid Email Format: While Prisma doesn’t enforce email format validation, the
application layer (e.g., using a validation library like Zod or Joi) should validate email
addresses before attempting to save them to the database.

Password Security: The passwordHash field stores a hashed password. The application
must ensure strong hashing algorithms (e.g., bcrypt) are used and that passwords are
never stored in plain text. Password comparison should always be done against the hash.
Role Management: Changes to UserRole should be carefully managed, especially for
ADMIN and TEACHER roles, as they grant elevated privileges. Access control checks

should be implemented at the application level based on the user’s role.

1.2. StudentProfile Model
The StudentProfile model extends the User model with specific attributes relevant to a
student user. It captures academic and personal details necessary for tracking progress,
assigning content, and personalizing the learning experience.
File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model StudentProfile {
id

String

@id @default(auto())

userId

String

@unique

user

User

@relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:

Cascade)
firstName

String

lastName

String

dateOfBirth

DateTime

gradeLevel

Int

schoolName

String?

parentCode

String?

@unique // Code for parents to link to student

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

// Relations
lessonProgresses LessonProgress[]
studySchedules

StudySchedule[]

homeworkSessions HomeworkSession[]
parentRewards

ParentReward[]

leagueGroupMembers LeagueGroupMember[]
@@map("student_profiles")
}

Field Descriptions:
id : A unique identifier for the student profile. Generated automatically by Prisma.

Type: String

Constraints: Primary Key, Auto-generated ( @id @default(auto()) )
userId : The ID of the associated User .

Type: String
Constraints: Unique, Foreign Key to User.id
user : The related User object. This defines the one-to-one relationship.

Type: User
Constraints: @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:
Cascade) ensures that if a User is deleted, their StudentProfile is also deleted.
firstName : The student’s first name.

Type: String
lastName : The student’s last name.

Type: String
dateOfBirth : The student’s date of birth, used for age-appropriate content and analytics.

Type: DateTime
gradeLevel : The student’s current grade level (e.g., 1-12).

Type: Int
schoolName : Optional field for the student’s school name.

Type: String? (Nullable)
parentCode : A unique code that parents can use to link their ParentProfile to this
StudentProfile . This allows parents to monitor their child’s progress.

Type: String? (Nullable)
Constraints: Unique ( @unique )
createdAt : Timestamp indicating when the student profile was created.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Default to current timestamp ( @default(now()) )
updatedAt : Timestamp indicating the last time the student profile was updated.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Automatically updated on record change ( @updatedAt )
Relationships:

user : One-to-one relationship with the User model. Each StudentProfile must belong

to one User .
lessonProgresses : One-to-many relationship with LessonProgress , tracking the

student’s progress in various lessons.
studySchedules : One-to-many relationship with StudySchedule , defining the student’s

personalized study plan.
homeworkSessions : One-to-many relationship with HomeworkSession , tracking

homework assignments.
parentRewards : One-to-many relationship with ParentReward , tracking rewards given

by parents.
leagueGroupMembers : One-to-many relationship with LeagueGroupMember , linking

students to their league groups.
Indexes:
userId : A unique index is automatically created due to the @unique constraint, ensuring

a one-to-one relationship with User .
parentCode : A unique index is automatically created due to the @unique constraint,

facilitating quick lookup for parent linking.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Missing User: A StudentProfile cannot exist without an associated User . The
onDelete: Cascade ensures data integrity; if the User is deleted, the StudentProfile

is also removed.
Duplicate Parent Code: Attempting to create a StudentProfile with a parentCode
that already exists will result in a P2002 error. The application should handle this by
generating a new unique code or informing the user.
Invalid Grade Level/Date of Birth: Application-level validation is crucial to ensure
gradeLevel is within a valid range (e.g., 1-12) and dateOfBirth is a valid past date.

1.3. ParentProfile Model
The ParentProfile model complements the User model by storing information specific to
parent users. This profile allows parents to manage their linked student accounts, monitor
progress, and interact with the platform in a supervisory capacity.

File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model ParentProfile {
id

String

@id @default(auto())

userId

String

@unique

user

User

@relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:

Cascade)
firstName

String

lastName

String

phoneNumber

String?

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

// Relations
children

StudentProfile[] @relation("ParentToStudent") // Many-to-many

through a linking table or direct link
parentRewards ParentReward[]
@@map("parent_profiles")
}

Field Descriptions:
id : A unique identifier for the parent profile. Generated automatically by Prisma.

Type: String
Constraints: Primary Key, Auto-generated ( @id @default(auto()) )
userId : The ID of the associated User .

Type: String
Constraints: Unique, Foreign Key to User.id
user : The related User object. This defines the one-to-one relationship.

Type: User
Constraints: @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:
Cascade) ensures that if a User is deleted, their ParentProfile is also deleted.
firstName : The parent’s first name.

Type: String
lastName : The parent’s last name.

Type: String
phoneNumber : An optional field for the parent’s phone number, which could be used for

notifications or contact.

Type: String? (Nullable)
createdAt : Timestamp indicating when the parent profile was created.

updatedAt : Timestamp indicating the last time the parent profile was updated.

Constraints: Automatically updated on record change ( @updatedAt )
Relationships:
user : One-to-one relationship with the User model. Each ParentProfile must belong

children : One-to-many relationship with StudentProfile . This relationship is

established by the parentCode in the StudentProfile model, allowing a parent to link
multiple student accounts. The @relation("ParentToStudent") is a named relation to
clarify the inverse side.
parentRewards : One-to-many relationship with ParentReward , tracking rewards issued

by this parent.
Indexes:
userId : A unique index is automatically created due to the @unique constraint, ensuring

a one-to-one relationship with User .
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Missing User: Similar to StudentProfile , a ParentProfile cannot exist without an
associated User . The onDelete: Cascade ensures data integrity.
Linking Students: The linking of StudentProfile to ParentProfile is facilitated by
the parentCode in the StudentProfile . The application logic must handle the
generation, distribution, and validation of these codes securely. A parent can link multiple
students using their respective parentCode s.
Phone Number Validation: If phoneNumber is used, application-level validation should
ensure it adheres to a valid format (e.g., Israeli phone number format).

1.4. Account Model
The Account model is used to link external accounts (e.g., OAuth providers like Google,
Facebook) to a User in the EliTutor platform. This allows users to sign in using third-party
services.
File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model Account {
id

String

userId

String

type

String

provider

String

@id @default(auto())

providerAccountId String
refreshToken

String?

accessToken

String?

expiresAt

Int?

tokenType

String?

scope

String?

idToken

String?

sessionState

String?

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])
@@map("accounts")
}

Field Descriptions:
id : A unique identifier for the account. Generated automatically by Prisma.

Type: String
Constraints: Primary Key, Auto-generated ( @id @default(auto()) )
userId : The ID of the associated User .

Type: String
Constraints: Foreign Key to User.id
type : The type of account (e.g., ‘oauth’, ‘email’, ‘credentials’).

Type: String
provider : The name of the authentication provider (e.g., ‘google’, ‘facebook’).

Type: String
providerAccountId : The unique ID of the user within the authentication provider.

Type: String
refreshToken : An optional token used to obtain new access tokens without re-

authenticating.
Type: String? (Nullable)
accessToken : An optional token used to access the provider’s API on behalf of the user.

Type: String? (Nullable)
expiresAt : An optional timestamp (in seconds) when the accessToken expires.

Type: Int? (Nullable)
tokenType : An optional type of the token (e.g., ‘Bearer’).

Type: String? (Nullable)
scope : An optional string indicating the permissions granted by the user to the application.

Type: String? (Nullable)
idToken : An optional JWT ID Token, typically used with OpenID Connect.

Type: String? (Nullable)
sessionState : An optional string used for session management with some OAuth

providers.
Type: String? (Nullable)
createdAt : Timestamp indicating when the account was linked.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Default to current timestamp ( @default(now()) )
updatedAt : Timestamp indicating the last time the account was updated.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Automatically updated on record change ( @updatedAt )
Relationships:
user : Many-to-one relationship with the User model. Each Account must belong to one
User .

Indexes:

@@unique([provider, providerAccountId]) : A composite unique index ensures that a

user can only have one account linked per provider. This prevents duplicate entries for the
same provider and provider account ID.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Duplicate Provider Account: Attempting to link an account with a provider and
providerAccountId pair that already exists will result in a P2002 error. The application

should handle this by informing the user that the account is already linked.
Missing User: An Account cannot exist without an associated User . The onDelete:
Cascade ensures data integrity; if the User is deleted, all their linked Account entries

are also removed.
Token Expiration: The application must handle accessToken expiration by using the
refreshToken to obtain new tokens or by prompting the user to re-authenticate if a
refreshToken is not available or has expired.

1.5. Session Model
The Session model is used to manage user sessions, typically for authentication and
maintaining user state across requests. It stores information about active user sessions, allowing
users to remain logged in without re-authenticating frequently.
File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model Session {
id

String

sessionToken String

@id @default(auto())
@unique

userId

String

expires

DateTime

createdAt

DateTime @default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime @updatedAt

user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
@@map("sessions")
}

Field Descriptions:
id : A unique identifier for the session. Generated automatically by Prisma.

Type: String

Constraints: Primary Key, Auto-generated ( @id @default(auto()) )
sessionToken : A unique token representing the active session. This token is typically

stored in a cookie on the client-side.
Type: String
Constraints: Unique ( @unique )
userId : The ID of the associated User .

Type: String
Constraints: Foreign Key to User.id
expires : The timestamp when the session will expire. After this time, the session is no

longer valid.
Type: DateTime
createdAt : Timestamp indicating when the session was created.

Type: DateTime
Constraints: Default to current timestamp ( @default(now()) )
updatedAt : Timestamp indicating the last time the session was updated (e.g., when its

expiration was extended).
Type: DateTime
Constraints: Automatically updated on record change ( @updatedAt )
Relationships:
user : Many-to-one relationship with the User model. Each Session must belong to one
User .

Indexes:
sessionToken : A unique index is automatically created due to the @unique constraint,

ensuring fast lookup and uniqueness of session tokens.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Expired Sessions: The application must regularly clean up expired sessions to maintain
database performance and security. This can be done via a scheduled job or by checking
the expires field during session validation.
Missing User: A Session cannot exist without an associated User . The onDelete:
Cascade ensures data integrity; if the User is deleted, all their active Session entries

are also removed.

Session Hijacking: Session tokens should be generated securely (e.g., cryptographically
strong random strings) and transmitted over HTTPS only. Application logic should
invalidate sessions on logout or suspicious activity.

levels within the same subject. The application must handle P2002 errors by informing the
user of the conflict.

Invalid Grade Level: Application-level validation should ensure gradeLevel is within the
expected range (1-12).

QuestionType : Defines the various formats a question can take.
MULTIPLE_CHOICE : Student selects one or more options from a list.
TRUE_FALSE : Student selects true or false.
FILL_IN_THE_BLANK : Student types in missing words or phrases.
MATCHING : Student matches items from two lists.
ORDERING : Student arranges items in a specific sequence.
SHORT_ANSWER : Student provides a brief textual answer.
CODE_SNIPPET : Student writes or completes a piece of code.

Indexes:
No specific indexes are defined on the Question model beyond the primary key. If
querying by type or difficulty becomes a bottleneck, consider adding indexes on
these fields.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Missing Lesson: A Question cannot exist without an associated Lesson . The
onDelete: Cascade ensures data integrity.

Invalid JSON Content/Answer: The application layer must strictly validate the content
and correctAnswer JSON structures against their respective schemas based on
QuestionType . Malformed JSON should be rejected.

Difficulty Range: Application-level validation should ensure difficulty is within the
expected range (1-5).

1.11.1. Question Content and Correct Answer JSON Schemas
Each QuestionType has a specific structure for its content and correctAnswer JSON
fields. These schemas ensure consistency and proper rendering/evaluation of questions.
1.11.1.1. MULTIPLE_CHOICE
Content Schema:

{
"questionText": "string",
"options": [
{ "id": "string", "text": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" },
{ "id": "string", "text": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" }
],
"isMultiSelect": "boolean" // true if multiple options can be selected
}

questionText : The main text of the question.
options : An array of possible answer choices.
id : A unique identifier for the option.
text : The text of the option.
imageUrl : Optional URL for an image associated with the option.
isMultiSelect : A boolean indicating if multiple options can be selected as correct.

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"selectedOptionIds": ["string"] // Array of IDs of the correct options
}

selectedOptionIds : An array containing the id s of the correct option(s). For single-

select, this array will contain one ID.
1.11.1.2. TRUE_FALSE
Content Schema:

{
"statement": "string"
}

statement : The statement that the student needs to evaluate as true or false.

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"isTrue": "boolean"
}

isTrue : true if the statement is true, false if it is false.

1.11.1.3. FILL_IN_THE_BLANK
Content Schema:

{
"textParts": [
{ "type": "text", "value": "string" },
{ "type": "blank", "id": "string" },
{ "type": "text", "value": "string" }
]
}

textParts : An array describing the question text, interspersed with blanks.
type : Either "text" or "blank" .
value : (for "text" type) The static text part.
id : (for "blank" type) A unique identifier for the blank.

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"blanks": {
"blankId1": ["string"], // Array of acceptable answers for blankId1
"blankId2": ["string"]
},
"caseSensitive": "boolean",
"trimWhitespace": "boolean"
}

blanks : An object where keys are blankId s from the content and values are arrays of

acceptable correct answers (strings).
caseSensitive : true if the answer must match case-sensitively.
trimWhitespace : true if leading/trailing whitespace should be ignored.

1.11.1.4. MATCHING
Content Schema:

{
"instructions": "string?",
"leftItems": [
{ "id": "string", "text": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" }
],
"rightItems": [
{ "id": "string", "text": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" }
]
}

instructions : Optional instructions for the matching task.
leftItems : An array of items to be matched from the left column.
rightItems : An array of items to be matched from the right column.

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"matches": [
{ "leftId": "string", "rightId": "string" }
]
}

matches : An array of objects, each specifying a correct pair of leftId and rightId .

1.11.1.5. ORDERING
Content Schema:

{
"instructions": "string?",
"items": [
{ "id": "string", "text": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" }
]
}

instructions : Optional instructions for the ordering task.

items : An array of items that need to be ordered. The initial order in this array is typically

shuffled for the student.
Correct Answer Schema:

{
"orderedItemIds": ["string"] // Array of IDs in the correct sequence
}

orderedItemIds : An array containing the id s of the items in their correct sequential

order.
1.11.1.6. SHORT_ANSWER
Content Schema:

{
"questionText": "string",
"maxLength": "number?" // Optional maximum length for the answer
}

questionText : The main text of the question.
maxLength : Optional maximum character length for the student’s answer.

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"acceptableAnswers": ["string"], // Array of acceptable correct answers
"caseSensitive": "boolean",
"trimWhitespace": "boolean",
"allowPartialMatch": "boolean" // If true, a partial match is considered
correct
}

acceptableAnswers : An array of strings, each representing a fully correct answer.
caseSensitive : true if the answer must match case-sensitively.
trimWhitespace : true if leading/trailing whitespace should be ignored.
allowPartialMatch : true if a student’s answer containing any of the
acceptableAnswers (or a significant portion thereof) should be considered correct. This

requires more complex application-level logic for evaluation.
1.11.1.7. CODE_SNIPPET
Content Schema:

{
"problemDescription": "string",
"initialCode": "string?", // Optional initial code snippet for the student
"language": "string",

// e.g., 'python', 'javascript'

"testCases": [
{ "input": "string", "expectedOutput": "string" }
]
}

problemDescription : The description of the coding problem.
initialCode : Optional initial code snippet provided to the student to start with.
language : The programming language for the code snippet (e.g., ‘python’, ‘javascript’).
testCases : An array of test cases, each with an input and expectedOutput .

Correct Answer Schema:

{
"solutionCode": "string" // The complete correct solution code
}

solutionCode : The complete correct code that solves the problem and passes all
testCases .

HomeworkStatus states (e.g., ASSIGNED -> IN_PROGRESS -> SUBMITTED -> GRADED ).

Grade Validation: Application-level validation should ensure grade is within a valid range
(e.g., 0-100) and is only set when status is GRADED .

assignments, especially for ADMIN roles, to prevent unauthorized actions.

This schema.prisma file is the definitive representation of the EliTutor database structure.
Developers should use this file to generate the Prisma client, perform migrations, and interact
with the database.

3. Complete Seed Script ( seed.ts )
This section provides a comprehensive TypeScript seed script designed to populate the EliTutor
database with essential initial data. This includes core subjects, sections, units, levels, lessons,
and a total of 100 sample questions (50 for Math Grade 3 and 50 for Arabic Grade 3). The script
is idempotent, meaning it can be run multiple times without creating duplicate entries for unique
data.

Explanation of the Seed Script:
1. Imports:
PrismaClient : The main client for interacting with the database.
QuestionType , UserRole , etc.: Enums defined in schema.prisma are imported to

ensure type safety and valid data.
bcryptjs : Used for hashing the admin password securely.

2. prisma instance: An instance of PrismaClient is created to interact with the database.
3. main() function: This asynchronous function contains the core logic for seeding.
Admin User Creation: An administrative user ( admin@elitutor.com ) is created
with a hashed password. upsert is used to either create the user if they don’t exist
or do nothing if they do, ensuring idempotency.
Subject Creation: “Math” and “Arabic” subjects are created using upsert to
prevent duplicates.
Section Creation: “Grade 3 Math” and “Grade 3 Arabic” sections are created, linked
to their respective subjects. The subjectId_gradeLevel unique constraint is used
for where clause in upsert .
Unit Creation: Two units are created for each Grade 3 section (e.g., “Numbers and
Operations” and “Geometry and Measurement” for Math Grade 3). The
sectionId_nameEn unique constraint is used.

Level Creation: Two levels are created for the first unit of each subject (e.g., “Basic
Addition” and “Basic Subtraction” for Math Unit 1). The unitId_levelNumber
unique constraint is used.
Lesson Creation: Two lessons are created for the first level of each subject.
Question Generation (Math Grade 3):
A loop runs 50 times to create 50 math questions.

Questions alternate between MULTIPLE_CHOICE , TRUE_FALSE , and
FILL_IN_THE_BLANK types.

Random numbers are generated for mathematical operations.
content and correctAnswer JSON objects are constructed dynamically

based on the QuestionType and random values, adhering to the schemas
defined in Section 1.11.1.
upsert is used with a predictable id ( math-q-1 , math-q-2 , etc.) to ensure

idempotency. Questions are alternately assigned to mathLesson1 and
mathLesson2 .

Question Generation (Arabic Grade 3):
Another loop runs 50 times for Arabic questions.
Similar to math questions, they alternate between MULTIPLE_CHOICE ,
TRUE_FALSE , and FILL_IN_THE_BLANK .

Arabic words and phrases are used for questionText , statement , and
textParts .
content and correctAnswer JSON objects are constructed according to the

schemas.
upsert is used with predictable id s ( arabic-q-1 , arabic-q-2 , etc.) and

questions are alternately assigned to arabicLesson1 and arabicLesson2 .
4. Error Handling and Disconnection:
The main() function is called, and any errors are caught and logged.
prisma.$disconnect() is called in a finally block to ensure the database

connection is closed regardless of success or failure.
JSDoc Comments:
All functions and key logic blocks are commented using JSDoc to explain their purpose,
parameters, and return values, enhancing code readability and maintainability.
Edge Cases and Error Handling in Seed Script:
Idempotency: The script uses prisma.model.upsert() for all data creation. This is
crucial for idempotency, meaning if the script is run multiple times, it will not create
duplicate records for entities that have unique constraints (like email for User , nameEn
for Subject , subjectId_gradeLevel for Section , etc.). It will either create the record if
it doesn’t exist or update it if it does (though in this seed, update: {} means no actual
update is performed if the record exists).

Password Hashing: The admin user’s password is securely hashed using bcryptjs
before being stored, demonstrating best practices for password management.
Random Data Generation: For questions, random values are used to create diverse
content. While simple, this demonstrates how more complex data generation could be
integrated.
JSON Schema Adherence: The content and correctAnswer JSON objects for
questions are carefully constructed to match the schemas defined in Section 1.11.1,
ensuring data validity.
Prisma Client Disconnection: The finally block ensures that the Prisma client
disconnects from the database, preventing open connections after the script finishes.

4. Prisma Migration Commands
Prisma Migrate is a powerful tool for managing database schema changes in a declarative way.
It generates SQL migration files based on changes detected in your schema.prisma file and
applies them to your database. This section outlines the essential Prisma migration commands
and their typical usage in the EliTutor development workflow.
File Path: N/A (These are CLI commands)

4.1. Initializing Prisma and Generating Client
Before performing any migrations, you need to initialize Prisma in your project and generate the
Prisma client. This sets up the prisma directory and generates the TypeScript client based on
your schema.prisma .

npm install prisma --save-dev
npx prisma init
npx prisma generate

Explanation:
npm install prisma --save-dev : Installs the Prisma CLI as a development

dependency.
npx prisma init : Initializes Prisma in your project. This command creates a new
prisma directory with a schema.prisma file and a .env file. You will then replace the

generated schema.prisma content with the complete schema provided in Section 2.

npx prisma generate : Generates the Prisma Client based on your schema.prisma file.

This client is a type-safe query builder that allows your application to interact with the
database. This command should be run every time schema.prisma is modified.

4.2. Creating a New Migration
When you make changes to your schema.prisma file (e.g., add a new model, field, or change a
data type), you need to create a new migration to apply these changes to your database.

npx prisma migrate dev --name <migration-name>

Explanation:
npx prisma migrate dev : This command performs several actions:

Compares your current schema.prisma with the database schema.
Generates a new migration file (e.g.,
20230101000000_migration_name/migration.sql ) in the prisma/migrations

directory, containing the SQL statements required to evolve your database schema.
Applies the new migration to your development database.
Updates the _prisma_migrations table in your database to record the applied
migration.
Generates the Prisma Client.
--name <migration-name> : A descriptive name for your migration (e.g.,
add_user_profile_models , add_question_types ). This name helps in understanding

the purpose of each migration.
Edge Cases and Error Handling:
Drift Detection: If your database schema has diverged from your migration history (e.g.,
manual changes were made to the database), prisma migrate dev will detect this and
prompt you to reset your database or resolve the drift manually. It’s best practice to avoid
manual database changes in a Prisma-managed project.
Non-destructive Changes: Prisma Migrate is designed to generate non-destructive
migrations where possible. However, if you make a destructive change (e.g., deleting a
column with data), Prisma will warn you and require explicit confirmation to proceed.

4.3. Applying Migrations to Production Databases
For production environments, you typically apply migrations without the interactive dev
experience. This is done using the deploy command.

npx prisma migrate deploy

Explanation:
npx prisma migrate deploy : This command applies all pending migrations to the target

database. It’s designed for CI/CD pipelines and production environments where interactive
prompts are not desirable. It will only apply migrations that have not yet been applied to the
database, based on the _prisma_migrations table.

4.4. Resetting the Database
During development, you might often need to reset your database to a clean state and reapply
all migrations and seed data. This is useful for testing or when major schema changes require a
fresh start.

npx prisma migrate reset

Explanation:
npx prisma migrate reset : This command:

Deletes all data and schema from the database.
Runs all migrations from scratch.
Runs the seed script (if configured in package.json ).

4.5. Generating Prisma Client Manually
While prisma migrate dev and prisma deploy automatically generate the client, you might
sometimes need to generate it manually after making changes to schema.prisma without
running a migration.

npx prisma generate

Explanation:
npx prisma generate : Regenerates the Prisma Client. This is necessary whenever you

modify your schema.prisma file and want your application code to reflect the latest
schema changes (e.g., new models, fields, or enums).

4.6. Running the Seed Script
After applying migrations, especially after a reset , you’ll want to populate your database with
initial data using the seed script.

npx prisma db seed

Explanation:
npx prisma db seed : Executes the seed script defined in your package.json . For this

to work, ensure your package.json has a prisma.seed entry pointing to your seed
script (e.g., "prisma": { "seed": "ts-node prisma/seed.ts" } ).

4.7. Typical Development Workflow
Here’s a typical workflow for database changes during development:
1. Modify schema.prisma : Add/remove models, fields, relations, enums.
2. Create Migration: npx prisma migrate dev --name <descriptive-name>
3. Run Seed (if needed): npx prisma db seed (often automatically run by migrate dev if
configured).
4. Develop Application: Use the updated Prisma Client in your application code.
Important Considerations:
Version Control: Always commit your schema.prisma file and the generated migration
files ( prisma/migrations/* ) to version control. This ensures that all team members are
working with the same database schema and migration history.
Environment Variables: Ensure the DATABASE_URL environment variable is correctly set
for your development and production environments. Prisma uses this to connect to the
PostgreSQL database.
Database Backups: Before applying migrations to production, always ensure you have a
recent backup of your database.

SECTION C: Complete NestJS Authentication System

SECTION C: Complete NestJS
Authentication System
This section details the complete authentication system for EliTutor, built using NestJS for the
backend and integrated with NextAuth.js v5 for the Next.js frontend. The system incorporates
JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, Google OAuth 2.0, email/password registration with
verification, and password reset functionalities.

1. Overview and Architecture
This section provides a high-level overview of the authentication architecture, including the
technologies used and the flow of authentication.

1.1 Technologies Used
Backend Framework: NestJS
Database: PostgreSQL (via Prisma ORM)
Authentication Strategy: JWT (Access Tokens & Refresh Tokens), Google OAuth 2.0
Password Hashing: bcrypt
Email Service: Resend
Frontend Authentication: NextAuth.js v5

1.2 Authentication Flow
Detailed diagrams and explanations of the authentication flows for registration, login, token
refresh, and Google OAuth.

2. Database Schema (Prisma)
The authentication system relies on several database models to manage user accounts,
authentication tokens, email verification, and password reset requests. We will use Prisma as
our Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) to interact with a PostgreSQL database. Below is the
detailed Prisma schema, which defines the structure of these models and their relationships.
File: prisma/schema.prisma

// This is your Prisma schema file,
// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema
generator client {
provider = "prisma-client-js"
}
datasource db {
provider = "postgresql"
url

= env("DATABASE_URL")

}
model User {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

email

String

@unique

password

// Nullable for OAuth users

firstName

String

lastName

String

isEmailVerified

Boolean

@default(false)

roles

String[]

@default(["user"]) // e.g., ["user", "admin"]

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

// Relationships
refreshTokens

RefreshToken[]

verificationTokens

VerificationToken[]

passwordResetTokens PasswordResetToken[]
googleId

String?

@unique // For Google OAuth

@@map("users")
}
model RefreshToken {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

token

String

@unique

userId

String

user

User

@relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:

Cascade)
expiresAt DateTime
createdAt DateTime

@default(now())

@@index([userId])
@@map("refresh_tokens")
}
model VerificationToken {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

token

String

@unique

userId

String

user

User

@relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete:

Cascade)
expiresAt DateTime
createdAt DateTime

@default(now())

@@index([userId])
@@map("verification_tokens")
}

id

String

@id @default(uuid())

token

String

@unique

userId

String

user

User
