@@index([userId])
@@map("password_reset_tokens")
}

2.1 Model Explanations
User Model

This model represents a user account in the system. It stores essential user information and
links to other authentication-related tokens.
id : A unique identifier for the user, generated as a UUID.
email : The user’s email address, which must be unique across all users. Used for login

and communication.
password : The hashed password for users who register with email/password. This field is

nullable to accommodate users who register via OAuth providers (e.g., Google) and may
not have a direct password set in our system.
firstName : The user’s first name.
lastName : The user’s last name.
isEmailVerified : A boolean flag indicating whether the user’s email address has been

verified. Defaults to false .
roles : An array of strings representing the user’s roles (e.g., ["user", "admin"] ).

Defaults to ["user"] .
createdAt : Timestamp for when the user account was created.

updatedAt : Timestamp for the last update to the user account.
refreshTokens : A relation to the RefreshToken model, indicating all refresh tokens

associated with this user.
verificationTokens : A relation to the VerificationToken model, for email verification

purposes.
passwordResetTokens : A relation to the PasswordResetToken model, for password

reset requests.
googleId : A unique identifier provided by Google for users who sign up or log in via

Google OAuth. This field is nullable.
@@map("users") : Maps the User model to a table named users in the database.
RefreshToken Model

This model stores refresh tokens, which are used to obtain new access tokens without requiring
the user to re-authenticate frequently. These tokens have a longer expiry time and are stored
securely.
id : Unique identifier for the refresh token.
token : The actual refresh token string, which must be unique.
userId : Foreign key linking to the User model, indicating which user this token belongs

to.
user : Relation to the User model.
expiresAt : Timestamp indicating when the refresh token expires.
createdAt : Timestamp for when the refresh token was issued.
@@index([userId]) : Creates an index on userId for faster lookups.
@@map("refresh_tokens") : Maps the RefreshToken model to a table named
refresh_tokens .
VerificationToken Model

This model stores tokens used for email verification during the registration process.
id : Unique identifier for the verification token.
token : The actual verification token string, which must be unique.
userId : Foreign key linking to the User model.
user : Relation to the User model.

expiresAt : Timestamp indicating when the verification token expires.
createdAt : Timestamp for when the verification token was issued.
@@index([userId]) : Creates an index on userId for faster lookups.
@@map("verification_tokens") : Maps the VerificationToken model to a table

named verification_tokens .
PasswordResetToken Model

This model stores tokens used for the password reset flow, allowing users to set a new
password if they forget their old one.
id : Unique identifier for the password reset token.
token : The actual password reset token string, which must be unique.
userId : Foreign key linking to the User model.
user : Relation to the User model.
expiresAt : Timestamp indicating when the password reset token expires.
createdAt : Timestamp for when the password reset token was issued.
@@index([userId]) : Creates an index on userId for faster lookups.
@@map("password_reset_tokens") : Maps the PasswordResetToken model to a table

named password_reset_tokens .

2.2 Database Migrations
After defining the Prisma schema, you will need to generate and apply database migrations to
create these tables in your PostgreSQL database. This is typically done using the Prisma CLI:

npx prisma migrate dev --name init_auth_models

This command will:
1. Create a new migration file in the prisma/migrations directory.
2. Apply the migration to your database, creating the users , refresh_tokens ,
verification_tokens , and password_reset_tokens tables.

Remember to run npx prisma generate after any schema changes to update the Prisma
Client.

3. Configuration
Proper configuration is crucial for the security and functionality of the authentication system. This
section outlines the necessary environment variables and NestJS module configurations for
JWT, Google OAuth, and the email service (Resend).

3.1 Environment Variables
All sensitive information and configurable parameters should be stored as environment
variables. This ensures that credentials are not hardcoded and can be easily managed across
different deployment environments. Create a .env file in the root of your NestJS project and
populate it with the following variables:
File: .env
# Database
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/elitutor_db?schema=public"
# JWT Configuration
JWT_SECRET="supersecretjwtkeythatshouldbechangedinproduction"
JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME="15m" # 15 minutes
JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME="7d" # 7 days
# Google OAuth 2.0 Configuration
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="YOUR_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID"
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="YOUR_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"
GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL="http://localhost:3000/auth/google/callback" # Backend callback
URL
# Resend Email Service Configuration
RESEND_API_KEY="YOUR_RESEND_API_KEY"
EMAIL_FROM="noreply@elitutor.com"
VERIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECT="Verify your EliTutor account"
PASSWORD_RESET_EMAIL_SUBJECT="Reset your EliTutor password"
# Frontend URL (for email links)
FRONTEND_URL="http://localhost:3001"

Explanation of Environment Variables:
DATABASE_URL : Connection string for your PostgreSQL database. Prisma uses this to

connect to the database.
JWT_SECRET : A strong, secret key used to sign and verify JWTs. Crucially, this must be a

long, randomly generated string in production environments.

JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME : The expiration time for access tokens (e.g., 15m

for 15 minutes). Access tokens are short-lived for security.
JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME : The expiration time for refresh tokens (e.g., 7d

for 7 days). Refresh tokens are longer-lived but are handled with more care (e.g., HTTPonly cookies).
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID : Your Google OAuth 2.0 client ID, obtained from the Google Cloud

Console.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET : Your Google OAuth 2.0 client secret, also from the Google

Cloud Console.
GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL : The URL where Google will redirect the user after authentication.

This should point to your NestJS backend’s Google OAuth callback endpoint.
RESEND_API_KEY : Your API key for the Resend email service.
EMAIL_FROM : The sender email address for all outgoing emails (e.g., verification,

password reset).
VERIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECT : Subject line for email verification emails.
PASSWORD_RESET_EMAIL_SUBJECT : Subject line for password reset emails.
FRONTEND_URL : The base URL of your Next.js frontend. Used to construct verification and

password reset links that redirect users back to the frontend.

3.2 NestJS Module Configurations
NestJS uses modules to organize application parts. We will configure the ConfigModule ,
JwtModule , and integrate with PassportModule for authentication strategies.

3.2.1 ConfigModule
The ConfigModule from @nestjs/config package is used to load environment variables into
the application. It makes environment variables accessible throughout your application via the
ConfigService .

File: src/app.module.ts

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigModule } from '@nestjs/config';
import { AppController } from './app.controller';
import { AppService } from './app.service';
import { AuthModule } from './auth/auth.module';
import { PrismaModule } from './prisma/prisma.module';
@Module({
imports: [
ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }), // Loads .env file and makes
variables globally available
AuthModule,
PrismaModule,
],
controllers: [AppController],
providers: [AppService],
})
export class AppModule {}

Explanation:
ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }) : This line imports and configures the
ConfigModule . Setting isGlobal: true makes the ConfigService available

throughout the application without needing to import ConfigModule in every feature
module. This is convenient for accessing environment variables like JWT_SECRET or
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID .

3.2.2 JwtModule
The JwtModule from @nestjs/jwt is essential for signing and verifying JSON Web Tokens. It
needs to be configured with a secret key and default sign options.
File: src/auth/auth.module.ts

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtModule } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import { PassportModule } from '@nestjs/passport';
import { AuthService } from './auth.service';
import { AuthController } from './auth.controller';
import { PrismaModule } from '../prisma/prisma.module';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { JwtStrategy } from './strategies/jwt.strategy';
import { GoogleStrategy } from './strategies/google.strategy';
import { EmailService } from '../email/email.service';
@Module({
imports: [
PassportModule.register({ defaultStrategy: 'jwt' }), // Default strategy for
Passport
JwtModule.registerAsync({
imports: [ConfigModule],
useFactory: async (configService: ConfigService) => ({
secret: configService.get<string>('JWT_SECRET'),
signOptions: {
expiresIn: configService.get<string>
('JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME'),
},
}),
inject: [ConfigService],
}),
PrismaModule,
],
controllers: [AuthController],
providers: [AuthService, JwtStrategy, GoogleStrategy, EmailService],
exports: [AuthService, JwtModule, PassportModule],
})
export class AuthModule {}

Explanation:
PassportModule.register({ defaultStrategy: 'jwt' }) : This registers the
PassportModule and sets jwt as the default authentication strategy. This simplifies the

use of @UseGuards(AuthGuard()) later on.
JwtModule.registerAsync(...) : This asynchronously configures the JwtModule .

Using registerAsync allows us to inject ConfigService to retrieve JWT_SECRET and
JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME from environment variables.
secret : The secret key used to sign JWTs. Retrieved from JWT_SECRET .

signOptions.expiresIn : The default expiration time for access tokens when they

are signed. Retrieved from JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME .
3.2.3 PassportModule
PassportModule is integrated into AuthModule as shown above. It provides the necessary

infrastructure for authentication strategies.

5. Authentication Service (AuthService)
The AuthService is the core of our authentication system. It encapsulates all business logic
related to user management, authentication, token generation, and interaction with the database
and email service. It is responsible for hashing passwords, creating and validating JWTs,
managing refresh tokens, handling email verification, password resets, and integrating with
Google OAuth.
File: src/auth/auth.service.ts

import { ConflictException, Injectable, UnauthorizedException,
BadRequestException, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtService } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import * as bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import { PrismaService } from '../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RegisterUserDto } from './dto/register-user.dto';
import { LoginUserDto } from './dto/login-user.dto';
import { AuthResponseDto } from './dto/auth-response.dto';
import { EmailService } from '../email/email.service';
import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid';
import { add } from 'date-fns';
/**
* @description Service responsible for all authentication-related business
logic.
*/
@Injectable()
export class AuthService {
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly jwtService: JwtService,
private readonly configService: ConfigService,
private readonly emailService: EmailService,
) {}
/**
* @description Registers a new user with email and password.
* Hashes the password, creates a user in the database, and initiates email
verification.
* @param {RegisterUserDto} registerUserDto - The DTO containing user
registration details.
* @returns {Promise<AuthResponseDto>} - The authentication response containing
user details and access token.
* @throws {ConflictException} If a user with the given email already exists.
*/
async register(registerUserDto: RegisterUserDto): Promise<AuthResponseDto> {
const { email, password, firstName, lastName } = registerUserDto;
// 1. Check if user already exists
const existingUser = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
if (existingUser) {
throw new ConflictException('‫ ;)'البريد الإلكتروني مستخدم بالفعل‬// Email already
in use
}
// 2. Hash password
const hashedPassword = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);

// 3. Create user in database
const user = await this.prisma.user.create({
data: {
email,
password: hashedPassword,
firstName,
lastName,
},
});
// 4. Generate verification token and send email
const verificationToken = await this.generateVerificationToken(user.id);
const verificationLink = `${this.configService.get<string>
('FRONTEND_URL')}/verify-email?token=${verificationToken.token}`;
try {
await this.emailService.sendVerificationEmail(user.email, user.firstName,
verificationLink);
} catch (error) {
console.error(`Failed to send verification email to ${user.email}:`,
error);
// Log the error but do not prevent user registration, as email sending can
be retried or handled separately.
// A more robust system might queue this email for a retry mechanism.
}
// 5. Generate JWT tokens
const { accessToken, refreshToken } = await this.generateTokens(user.id,
user.email, user.roles);
// 6. Store refresh token in DB
await this.storeRefreshToken(user.id, refreshToken);
return {
id: user.id,
email: user.email,
firstName: user.firstName,
lastName: user.lastName,
isEmailVerified: user.isEmailVerified,
roles: user.roles,
accessToken,
};
}
/**
* @description Logs in a user with email and password.
* Validates credentials, checks email verification status, and generates JWT
tokens.
* @param {LoginUserDto} loginUserDto - The DTO containing user login details.

* @returns {Promise<AuthResponseDto>} - The authentication response containing
user details and access token.
* @throws {UnauthorizedException} If credentials are invalid or email is not
verified.
*/
async login(loginUserDto: LoginUserDto): Promise<AuthResponseDto> {
const { email, password } = loginUserDto;
// 1. Find user by email
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
if (!user || !user.password) {
throw new UnauthorizedException('‫ ;)'بيانات الاعتماد غير صالحة‬// Invalid
credentials
}
// 2. Compare passwords
const isPasswordValid = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password);
if (!isPasswordValid) {
throw new UnauthorizedException('‫ ;)'بيانات الاعتماد غير صالحة‬// Invalid
credentials
}
// 3. Check if email is verified
if (!user.isEmailVerified) {

throw new UnauthorizedException('‫ يرجى التحقق من بريدك‬.‫البريد الإلكتروني غير مؤكد‬

‫الوارد‬.'); // Email not verified
}
// 4. Generate JWT tokens

const { accessToken, refreshToken } = await this.generateTokens(user.id,
user.email, user.roles);
// 5. Store refresh token in DB (and invalidate old ones if any)
await this.storeRefreshToken(user.id, refreshToken);
return {
id: user.id,
email: user.email,
firstName: user.firstName,
lastName: user.lastName,
isEmailVerified: user.isEmailVerified,
roles: user.roles,
accessToken,
};
}
/**
* @description Handles Google OAuth login/registration.
* If the user exists, logs them in. If not, registers them.

* @param {string} email - The user's email from Google.
* @param {string} firstName - The user's first name from Google.
* @param {string} lastName - The user's last name from Google.
* @param {string} googleId - The user's Google ID.
* @returns {Promise<AuthResponseDto>} - The authentication response.
*/
async googleLogin(email: string, firstName: string, lastName: string, googleId:
string): Promise<AuthResponseDto> {
let user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
if (!user) {
// If user doesn't exist, create a new one
user = await this.prisma.user.create({
data: {
email,
firstName,
lastName,
isEmailVerified: true, // Google users are considered verified
googleId,
},
});
} else if (!user.googleId) {
// If user exists but not linked to Google, link it
user = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: user.id },
data: { googleId, isEmailVerified: true },
});
}
// Generate JWT tokens
const { accessToken, refreshToken } = await this.generateTokens(user.id,
user.email, user.roles);
// Store refresh token in DB
await this.storeRefreshToken(user.id, refreshToken);
return {
id: user.id,
email: user.email,
firstName: user.firstName,
lastName: user.lastName,
isEmailVerified: user.isEmailVerified,
roles: user.roles,
accessToken,
};
}
/**
* @description Generates a new access token and refresh token.

* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user.
* @param {string} email - The email of the user.
* @param {string[]} roles - The roles of the user.
* @returns {Promise<{ accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }>} - An
object containing the access and refresh tokens.
*/
private async generateTokens(userId: string, email: string, roles: string[]):
Promise<{ accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }> {
const payload = { sub: userId, email, roles };
const accessToken = this.jwtService.sign(payload, {
expiresIn: this.configService.get<string>
('JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME'),
});
const refreshToken = this.jwtService.sign(payload, {
expiresIn: this.configService.get<string>
('JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME'),
secret: this.configService.get<string>('JWT_SECRET') + '-refresh', // Use a
different secret for refresh tokens
});
return { accessToken, refreshToken };
}
/**
* @description Stores a refresh token in the database, invalidating any old
ones for the same user.
* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user.
* @param {string} token - The refresh token string.
*/
private async storeRefreshToken(userId: string, token: string): Promise<void> {
const expiresAt = add(new Date(), { days: 7 }); // 7 days expiry for refresh
token
// Invalidate all existing refresh tokens for this user for security (onetime use refresh tokens)
await this.prisma.refreshToken.deleteMany({ where: { userId } });
await this.prisma.refreshToken.create({
data: {
userId,
token,
expiresAt,
},
});
}
/**
* @description Refreshes access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh
token.
* Invalidates the old refresh token and issues new ones.

* @param {string} oldRefreshToken - The expired refresh token.
* @returns {Promise<{ accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }>} - New
access and refresh tokens.
* @throws {UnauthorizedException} If the refresh token is invalid or expired.
*/
async refreshTokens(oldRefreshToken: string): Promise<{ accessToken: string;
refreshToken: string }> {
try {
// 1. Verify the old refresh token
const decoded = this.jwtService.verify(oldRefreshToken, {
secret: this.configService.get<string>('JWT_SECRET') + '-refresh',
});
// 2. Check if the refresh token exists in DB and is not expired
const storedToken = await this.prisma.refreshToken.findUnique({
where: { token: oldRefreshToken },
include: { user: true },
});
if (!storedToken || storedToken.expiresAt < new Date()) {

throw new UnauthorizedException('‫ ;)'رمز التحديث غير صالح أو منتهي الصالحية‬//

Invalid or expired refresh token
}
// 3. Invalidate the old refresh token (one-time use)
await this.prisma.refreshToken.delete({ where: { id: storedToken.id } });
// 4. Generate new tokens
const { accessToken, refreshToken } = await this.generateTokens(
storedToken.user.id,
storedToken.user.email,
storedToken.user.roles,
);
// 5. Store the new refresh token
await this.storeRefreshToken(storedToken.user.id, refreshToken);
return { accessToken, refreshToken };
} catch (error) {
throw new UnauthorizedException('‫ ;)'رمز التحديث غير صالح أو منتهي الصالحية‬//
Invalid or expired refresh token
}
}
/**
* @description Generates a unique email verification token and stores it in
the database.
* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user.
* @returns {Promise<VerificationToken>} - The created verification token.

*/
private async generateVerificationToken(userId: string) {
const token = uuidv4();
const expiresAt = add(new Date(), { hours: 24 }); // Token valid for 24 hours
return this.prisma.verificationToken.create({
data: {
userId,
token,
expiresAt,
},
});
}
/**
* @description Verifies a user's email using a verification token.
* @param {string} token - The verification token.
* @returns {Promise<void>} - Resolves on successful verification.
* @throws {BadRequestException} If the token is invalid or expired.
*/
async verifyEmail(token: string): Promise<void> {
const verificationRecord = await this.prisma.verificationToken.findUnique({
where: { token },
include: { user: true },
});
if (!verificationRecord || verificationRecord.expiresAt < new Date()) {
throw new BadRequestException('‫ ;)'رمز التحقق غير صالح أو منتهي الصالحية‬//

Invalid or expired verification token
}
await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: verificationRecord.userId },
data: { isEmailVerified: true },
});
await this.prisma.verificationToken.delete({ where: { id:
verificationRecord.id } });
}
/**
* @description Initiates the password reset flow by generating a token and
sending a reset email.
* @param {string} email - The email of the user requesting a password reset.
* @returns {Promise<void>} - Resolves on successful initiation.
* @throws {NotFoundException} If no user is found with the given email.
*/
async forgotPassword(email: string): Promise<void> {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });

if (!user) {
// For security, do not reveal if the email exists or not.
// Just return success, but log the attempt.
console.warn(`Password reset requested for non-existent email: ${email}`);
return;
}
// Invalidate any existing password reset tokens for this user
await this.prisma.passwordResetToken.deleteMany({ where: { userId: user.id }
});
const resetToken = uuidv4();
const expiresAt = add(new Date(), { hours: 1 }); // Token valid for 1 hour
await this.prisma.passwordResetToken.create({
data: {
userId: user.id,
token: resetToken,
expiresAt,
},
});
const resetLink = `${this.configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL')}/resetpassword?token=${resetToken}`;
try {
await this.emailService.sendPasswordResetEmail(user.email, user.firstName,
resetLink);
} catch (error) {
console.error(`Failed to send password reset email to ${user.email}:`,
error);
// Log the error but do not prevent token generation.
}
}
/**
* @description Resets a user's password using a valid reset token.
* @param {string} token - The password reset token.
* @param {string} newPassword - The new password.
* @returns {Promise<void>} - Resolves on successful password reset.
* @throws {BadRequestException} If the token is invalid or expired.
*/
async resetPassword(token: string, newPassword: string): Promise<void> {
const resetRecord = await this.prisma.passwordResetToken.findUnique({
where: { token },
include: { user: true },
});
if (!resetRecord || resetRecord.expiresAt < new Date()) {
throw new BadRequestException('‫رمز إعادة تعيين كلمة المرور غير صالح أو منتهي‬

‫ ;)'الصالحية‬// Invalid or expired reset token
}
const hashedPassword = await bcrypt.hash(newPassword, 10);
await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: resetRecord.userId },
data: { password: hashedPassword },
});
await this.prisma.passwordResetToken.delete({ where: { id: resetRecord.id }
});
}
/**
* @description Invalidates all refresh tokens for a given user.
* Used during logout or when a user's security is compromised.
* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user.
* @returns {Promise<void>} - Resolves on successful invalidation.
*/
async invalidateAllRefreshTokens(userId: string): Promise<void> {
await this.prisma.refreshToken.deleteMany({ where: { userId } });
}
/**
* @description Validates a JWT payload (used by JwtStrategy).
* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user from the JWT payload.
* @returns {Promise<User | null>} - The user object if valid, otherwise null.
*/
async validateUserById(userId: string): Promise<any> {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
if (!user) {
return null;
}
// Ensure sensitive data like password is not returned
const { password, ...result } = user;
return result;
}
}

Explanation of AuthService Methods:
constructor : Injects PrismaService , JwtService , ConfigService , and
EmailService for database interaction, JWT operations, configuration access, and email

sending, respectively.
register(registerUserDto) : Handles new user registration. It first checks for existing

users with the same email to prevent ConflictException . It then hashes the provided

password using bcrypt (salt rounds are implicitly handled by bcrypt.hash with 10
rounds). A new user record is created in the database. An email verification token is
generated, stored, and a verification email is sent to the user. Finally, it generates and
stores JWT access and refresh tokens, returning the user details and access token.
login(loginUserDto) : Authenticates an existing user. It retrieves the user by email and

compares the provided password with the stored hashed password using
bcrypt.compare . It also checks if the user’s email is verified. If credentials are valid and

the email is verified, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated, the refresh token
is stored, and the authentication response is returned.
googleLogin(email, firstName, lastName, googleId) : Manages user

login/registration via Google OAuth. It checks if a user with the given email already exists.
If not, a new user account is created, marked as email verified, and linked with the
googleId . If a user exists but doesn’t have a googleId linked, it updates the existing

user to link the Google account. Finally, it generates and stores JWT tokens.
generateTokens(userId, email, roles) : A private helper method to create both JWT

access and refresh tokens. Access tokens are short-lived (15 minutes) and signed with
JWT_SECRET . Refresh tokens are longer-lived (7 days) and signed with a different secret

( JWT_SECRET + '-refresh' ) for enhanced security. This separation prevents an attacker
from using a compromised access token to forge a refresh token.
storeRefreshToken(userId, token) : A private helper method to store the generated

refresh token in the database. For security, it invalidates all previously issued refresh

SECTION D: Complete NestJS Curriculum & Learning Path
System

SECTION D: Complete NestJS Curriculum &
Learning Path System
This section details the complete implementation of the Curriculum & Learning Path System for
EliTutor, a gamified educational web platform. It covers the core components, including the
CurriculumController ,

CurriculumService ,

LearningPathService ,

and

PlacementTestService , along with their respective functionalities, data structures, and error

handling. The system is designed to manage educational content, track user progress, and

provide adaptive learning experiences for Israeli Arab school students (Grades 1-12) across
various subjects based on the Koter curriculum.

1. Prisma Schema Definition
The data model for the Curriculum & Learning Path System is defined using Prisma, an opensource ORM. The schema outlines the relationships between Curriculum , Subject , Grade ,
Lesson ,

LearningPathNode ,

UserProgress , and

PlacementTest

entities. This robust

schema ensures data integrity and provides a clear structure for content management and user
interaction.

1.1. Curriculum Model
Represents the overall educational curriculum, which can be Koter or any other standard.
// prisma/schema.prisma
model Curriculum {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

name

String

@unique

description String?
subjects

Subject[]

createdAt DateTime @default(now())
updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

1.2. Subject Model
Defines the academic subjects offered within a curriculum (e.g., Arabic, Hebrew, English, Math,
Science).

// prisma/schema.prisma
model Subject {
id

String

name

String

@id @default(uuid())

curriculumId String
curriculum

Curriculum @relation(fields: [curriculumId], references: [id])

grades

Grade[]

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

@@unique([name, curriculumId])
}

1.3. Grade Model
Represents the academic grade levels (e.g., Grade 1, Grade 2, …, Grade 12).
// prisma/schema.prisma
model Grade {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

level

Int

@unique // e.g., 1, 2, ..., 12

subjectId String
subject

Subject

lessons

Lesson[]

@relation(fields: [subjectId], references: [id])

createdAt DateTime @default(now())
updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
@@unique([level, subjectId])
}

1.4. Lesson Model
Defines individual lessons within a subject and grade. Each lesson has content and can be part
of a learning path.

// prisma/schema.prisma
enum LessonType {
REGULAR
PLACEMENT_TEST
}
model Lesson {
id

String

title

String

String?

content

String

@id @default(uuid())

@db.Text // Markdown or HTML content for the

lesson
gradeId

String

grade

Grade

@relation(fields: [gradeId], references: [id])

order

Int

// Order within the grade/subject

type

LessonType

@default(REGULAR)

learningPathNodes LearningPathNode[]
userProgress

UserProgress[]

createdAt

DateTime

@default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime

@updatedAt

@@unique([gradeId, order])
}

Represents a node in the learning path, linking lessons in a specific sequence. This forms the
“snake path” structure.

model LearningPathNode {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

lessonId

String

@unique

lesson

Lesson

@relation(fields: [lessonId], references: [id])

nextLessonId String?

@unique

nextLesson

@relation("NextLesson", fields: [nextLessonId], references:

Lesson?

[id])
prevLessonId String?

@unique

prevLesson

@relation("PrevLesson", fields: [prevLessonId], references:

Lesson?

[id])
// This field will store the calculated snake path order for quick retrieval

@unique

createdAt

DateTime @default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime @updatedAt

}

1.6. UserProgress Model
Tracks a user’s progress through lessons, including completion status, scores, and last access.

@updatedAt

Records attempts at placement tests, including questions, answers, and adaptive difficulty

model PlacementTestAttempt {
id

String

String

String

Lesson

Json

Json

Int?

@@unique([userId, lessonId])

2. Core Data Transfer Objects (DTOs)
DTOs are essential for defining the structure of data exchanged between the client and the
server. They ensure type safety and clear communication within the NestJS application. These
DTOs will be used for request payloads and API responses.

2.1. Curriculum DTOs
CurriculumDto

Represents the basic structure of a curriculum.

// src/curriculum/dto/curriculum.dto.ts

@ApiProperty({ description: 'Unique identifier of the curriculum', example:
'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-1234-567890abcdef' })
id: string;
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Name of the curriculum', example: 'Koter
Curriculum' })
name: string;
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Description of the curriculum', example: 'The
official Koter curriculum for Israeli Arab schools.', required: false })
description?: string;
}

2.2. Learning Path DTOs
LearningPathNodeDto

Represents a node in the learning path, including its associated lesson and user progress.

// src/learning-path/dto/learning-path-node.dto.ts
import { ApiProperty } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { LessonDto } from '../../curriculum/dto/lesson.dto';
import { ProgressStatus } from '@prisma/client';
export class LearningPathNodeDto {
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Unique identifier of the learning path node',
example: 'node-123-abc' })
id: string;

@ApiProperty({ description: 'The order of this lesson in the snake path',

@ApiProperty({ description: 'Status of the user\'s progress for this lesson',
enum: ProgressStatus, example: ProgressStatus.UNLOCKED })
status: ProgressStatus;
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Score achieved by the user for this lesson, if
completed', example: 95, required: false })
score?: number;
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Indicates if the lesson is currently unlocked for

isUnlocked: boolean;
@ApiProperty({ description: 'Indicates if the lesson is the next one the user
should attempt', example: true })
isCurrent: boolean;
}

import { ApiProperty } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { LearningPathNodeDto } from './learning-path-node.dto';

async findAllSubjects(): Promise<SubjectDto[]> {

5. LearningPathService Implementation
The

LearningPathService

is responsible for constructing and managing the user’s

personalized learning path. This includes determining the order of lessons (snake path),
calculating the status of each lesson based on user progress, and implementing unlock logic.
File Path: src/learning-path/learning-path.service.ts

// src/learning-path/learning-path.service.ts
import { Injectable, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../prisma/prisma.service';
import { LearningPathDto, LearningPathNodeDto } from './dto/learning-path.dto';
import { LessonDto } from '../curriculum/dto/lesson.dto';
import { ProgressStatus, Lesson, UserProgress, LearningPathNode } from
'@prisma/client';
@Injectable()
export class LearningPathService {
constructor(private prisma: PrismaService) {}
/**
* @summary Fetches the complete learning path for a user in a specific subject
and grade.
* @param {string} userId The ID of the user.
* @param {string} subjectId The ID of the subject.
* @param {number} gradeLevel The grade level.
* @returns {Promise<LearningPathDto>} The user's personalized learning path.
* @throws {NotFoundException} If the subject or grade is not found.
*/
async fetchLearningPath(
userId: string,
subjectId: string,
gradeLevel: number,
): Promise<LearningPathDto> {
const grade = await this.prisma.grade.findUnique({
where: {
level_subjectId: { level: gradeLevel, subjectId: subjectId },
},
include: {
lessons: {
orderBy: { order: 'asc' },
include: {
learningPathNodes: true, // Include learning path nodes to get
snakePathOrder
},
},
subject: true,
},
});
if (!grade) {
throw new NotFoundException(`Grade ${gradeLevel} for subject ${subjectId}
not found.`);
}
const userProgress = await this.prisma.userProgress.findMany({

where: { userId, lessonId: { in: grade.lessons.map(lesson => lesson.id) }
},
});
const userProgressMap = new Map<string, UserProgress>();
userProgress.forEach(progress => userProgressMap.set(progress.lessonId,
progress));
// Ensure all lessons have a LearningPathNode and snakePathOrder. If not,
create them.
await this.ensureLearningPathNodes(grade.lessons);
// Re-fetch lessons with guaranteed learningPathNodes and snakePathOrder
const lessonsWithNodes = await this.prisma.lesson.findMany({
where: { gradeId: grade.id },
include: {
learningPathNodes: true,
},
orderBy: { learningPathNodes: { snakePathOrder: 'asc' } }, // Order by
snake path
});
let currentLessonIndex = -1;
let foundCurrent = false;
const nodes: LearningPathNodeDto[] = lessonsWithNodes.map((lesson, index) =>
{
const progress = userProgressMap.get(lesson.id);
const lessonDto: LessonDto = {
id: lesson.id,
title: lesson.title,
description: lesson.description,
content: lesson.content,
gradeId: lesson.gradeId,
order: lesson.order,
type: lesson.type,
};
const nodeStatus = this.calculateNodeStatus(lesson, progress,
lessonsWithNodes, index, userProgressMap);
if (nodeStatus.isCurrent && !foundCurrent) {
currentLessonIndex = index;
foundCurrent = true;
}
return {
id: lesson.learningPathNodes[0]?.id || `node-${lesson.id}`, // Assuming
one node per lesson for simplicity

lesson: lessonDto,
snakePathOrder: lesson.learningPathNodes[0]?.snakePathOrder ||
lesson.order, // Fallback to lesson order if snakePathOrder is missing
status: nodeStatus.status,
score: progress?.score || null,
isUnlocked: nodeStatus.isUnlocked,
isCurrent: nodeStatus.isCurrent,
};
});
// If no current lesson was explicitly found (e.g., all completed or all
locked), determine the first unlocked/locked lesson as current
if (!foundCurrent && nodes.length > 0) {
const firstUnlocked = nodes.find(node => node.isUnlocked && node.status !==
ProgressStatus.COMPLETED);
if (firstUnlocked) {
firstUnlocked.isCurrent = true;
} else if (nodes.every(node => node.status === ProgressStatus.COMPLETED) &&
nodes.length > 0) {
// If all lessons are completed, the last lesson can be considered
'current' for review purposes
nodes[nodes.length - 1].isCurrent = true;
} else if (nodes.length > 0) {
// If no unlocked lessons, the first locked lesson is the 'current'
target
const firstLocked = nodes.find(node => node.status ===
ProgressStatus.LOCKED);
if (firstLocked) {
firstLocked.isCurrent = true;
}
}
}
return {
id: `${subjectId}-${gradeLevel}-path`,
subjectName: grade.subject.name,
gradeLevel: grade.level,
nodes,
};
}
/**
* @summary Ensures that all lessons have an associated LearningPathNode with a
snakePathOrder.
* If a lesson does not have a node, one is created and the snake path order is
assigned.
* This method implements the snake path ordering algorithm.
* @param {Lesson[]} lessons The list of lessons to process.
*/

private async ensureLearningPathNodes(lessons: Lesson[]): Promise<void> {
// Sort lessons by their natural order to establish a base sequence
const sortedLessons = [...lessons].sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
for (let i = 0; i < sortedLessons.length; i++) {
const lesson = sortedLessons[i];
let learningPathNode = await this.prisma.learningPathNode.findUnique({
where: { lessonId: lesson.id },
});
if (!learningPathNode) {
// Create a new node if it doesn't exist
learningPathNode = await this.prisma.learningPathNode.create({
data: {
lessonId: lesson.id,
snakePathOrder: i + 1, // Assign sequential order based on sorted
lessons
},
});
} else if (learningPathNode.snakePathOrder === null) {
// If node exists but snakePathOrder is null, update it
learningPathNode = await this.prisma.learningPathNode.update({
where: { id: learningPathNode.id },
data: { snakePathOrder: i + 1 },
});
}
}
}
/**
* @summary Calculates the status of a single learning path node (lesson) for a
user.
* This includes determining if it's locked, unlocked, in progress, completed,
or the current lesson.
* @param {Lesson} lesson The lesson object.
* @param {UserProgress | undefined} userProgress The user's progress for this
lesson, if any.
* @param {Lesson[]} allLessonsInPath All lessons in the current learning path,
ordered by snake path.
* @param {number} lessonIndex The index of the current lesson in the
`allLessonsInPath` array.
* @param {Map<string, UserProgress>} userProgressMap A map of user progress
for quick lookups.
* @returns {{ status: ProgressStatus; isUnlocked: boolean; isCurrent: boolean
}} The calculated status and flags.
*/
private calculateNodeStatus(
lesson: Lesson,
userProgress: UserProgress | undefined,

allLessonsInPath: Lesson[],
lessonIndex: number,
userProgressMap: Map<string, UserProgress>,
): { status: ProgressStatus; isUnlocked: boolean; isCurrent: boolean } {
let status: ProgressStatus = ProgressStatus.LOCKED;
let isUnlocked = false;
let isCurrent = false;
if (userProgress) {
status = userProgress.status;
if (status === ProgressStatus.COMPLETED || status ===
ProgressStatus.IN_PROGRESS) {
isUnlocked = true;
}
}
// Unlock logic: A lesson is unlocked if the previous lesson is completed, or
if it's the very first lesson.
// A lesson is also unlocked if it's a placement test and the previous
regular lesson is completed.
const previousLesson = allLessonsInPath[lessonIndex - 1];
const previousLessonProgress = previousLesson ?
userProgressMap.get(previousLesson.id) : undefined;
if (lessonIndex === 0) {
// The very first lesson is always unlocked.
isUnlocked = true;
if (!userProgress) {
status = ProgressStatus.UNLOCKED;
}
} else if (previousLessonProgress?.status === ProgressStatus.COMPLETED) {
// If the previous lesson is completed, the current one is unlocked.
isUnlocked = true;
if (!userProgress) {
status = ProgressStatus.UNLOCKED;
}
} else if (lesson.type === 'PLACEMENT_TEST') {
// Special handling for placement tests: they can be unlocked if the *last
regular lesson before them* is completed.
// Find the most recent regular lesson before this placement test.
let lastRegularLessonCompleted = false;
for (let i = lessonIndex - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
const prev = allLessonsInPath[i];
if (prev.type === 'REGULAR') {
const prevProgress = userProgressMap.get(prev.id);
if (prevProgress?.status === ProgressStatus.COMPLETED) {
lastRegularLessonCompleted = true;
break;
}

}
}
if (lastRegularLessonCompleted) {
isUnlocked = true;
if (!userProgress) {
status = ProgressStatus.UNLOCKED;
}
}
}
// Determine if it's the current lesson
// The current lesson is the first unlocked lesson that is not yet completed.
// If all lessons are completed, the last lesson is considered current for
review.
if (isUnlocked && status !== ProgressStatus.COMPLETED) {
// Check if any previous lesson is not completed or in progress
const hasIncompletePrevious = allLessonsInPath.slice(0,
lessonIndex).some(prev => {
const prevProg = userProgressMap.get(prev.id);
return !prevProg || (prevProg.status !== ProgressStatus.COMPLETED &&
prevProg.status !== ProgressStatus.IN_PROGRESS);
});
if (!hasIncompletePrevious) {
isCurrent = true;
}
}
// Edge case: If all lessons are completed, the last one is current
if (allLessonsInPath.every(l => userProgressMap.get(l.id)?.status ===
ProgressStatus.COMPLETED) && lessonIndex === allLessonsInPath.length - 1) {
isCurrent = true;
}
return { status, isUnlocked, isCurrent };
}
/**
* @summary Updates the user's progress for a specific lesson.
* @param {string} userId The ID of the user.
* @param {string} lessonId The ID of the lesson.
* @param {ProgressStatus} status The new progress status.
* @param {number} [score] The score achieved for the lesson (optional).
* @returns {Promise<UserProgress>} The updated user progress record.
*/
async updateUserProgress(
userId: string,
lessonId: string,
status: ProgressStatus,

score?: number,
): Promise<UserProgress> {
return this.prisma.userProgress.upsert({
where: { userId_lessonId: { userId, lessonId } },
update: { status, score, completedAt: status === ProgressStatus.COMPLETED ?
new Date() : undefined },
create: { userId, lessonId, status, score, completedAt: status ===
ProgressStatus.COMPLETED ? new Date() : undefined },
});
}
}

6. PlacementTestService Implementation
The PlacementTestService manages the adaptive difficulty logic for placement tests. It tracks
user answers, adjusts difficulty, and determines when a test is completed based on consecutive
wrong answers.
File Path: src/placement-test/placement-test.service.ts

import { Injectable, NotFoundException, BadRequestException } from
'@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../prisma/prisma.service';
import { PlacementTestAttemptDto, PlacementTestQuestionDto,
PlacementTestResultDto } from './dto/placement-test.dto';
import { SubmitPlacementTestAnswerDto } from './dto/submit-placement-testanswer.dto';
import { LessonType, PlacementTestAttempt } from '@prisma/client';
@Injectable()
export class PlacementTestService {
private readonly MAX_CONSECUTIVE_WRONG = 3;
private readonly INITIAL_DIFFICULTY = 1;
private readonly MAX_DIFFICULTY = 5; // Assuming 5 difficulty levels
constructor(private prisma: PrismaService) {}
/**
* @summary Starts a new placement test attempt for a user.
* @param {string} userId The ID of the user.
* @param {string} lessonId The ID of the lesson configured as a placement
test.
* @returns {Promise<PlacementTestAttemptDto>} The newly created placement test
attempt.
* @throws {NotFoundException} If the lesson is not found or is not a placement
test.
* @throws {BadRequestException} If an active placement test already exists for
the user and lesson.
*/
async startPlacementTest(
userId: string,
lessonId: string,
): Promise<PlacementTestAttemptDto> {
const lesson = await this.prisma.lesson.findUnique({
where: { id: lessonId, type: LessonType.PLACEMENT_TEST },
});
if (!lesson) {
throw new NotFoundException(`Placement test lesson with ID ${lessonId} not
found.`);
}
// Check for existing active attempt
const existingAttempt = await this.prisma.placementTestAttempt.findUnique({
where: { userId_lessonId: { userId, lessonId } },
});

if (existingAttempt && !existingAttempt.isCompleted) {
throw new BadRequestException('An active placement test attempt already
exists for this user and lesson.');
}
// For simplicity, let's assume questions are part of the lesson content or
fetched from a question bank.
// Here, we'll mock fetching the first question based on initial difficulty.
const initialQuestion = await
this.fetchQuestionByDifficulty(this.INITIAL_DIFFICULTY);
if (!initialQuestion) {
throw new NotFoundException('No questions available for the initial
difficulty level.');
}
const newAttempt = await this.prisma.placementTestAttempt.create({
data: {
userId,
lessonId,
difficultyLevel: this.INITIAL_DIFFICULTY,
consecutiveWrong: 0,
questions: [initialQuestion] as Prisma.JsonArray,
answers: [] as Prisma.JsonArray,
results: [] as Prisma.JsonArray,
isCompleted: false,
},
});
return this.mapToPlacementTestAttemptDto(newAttempt);
}
/**
* @summary Submits an answer to a placement test question and applies adaptive
difficulty logic.
* @param {string} userId The ID of the user.
* @param {SubmitPlacementTestAnswerDto} submitAnswerDto The DTO containing
attempt ID, question ID, and answer.
* @returns {Promise<PlacementTestResultDto>} The result of the submission,
including the next question or test completion status.
* @throws {NotFoundException} If the attempt or question is not found.
* @throws {BadRequestException} If the test is already completed or the
question is not part of the current attempt.
*/
async submitAnswer(
userId: string,
submitAnswerDto: SubmitPlacementTestAnswerDto,
): Promise<PlacementTestResultDto> {
const { attemptId, questionId, answer } = submitAnswerDto;

let attempt = await this.prisma.placementTestAttempt.findUnique({
where: { id: attemptId, userId },
});
if (!attempt) {
throw new NotFoundException(`Placement test attempt with ID ${attemptId}
not found for user ${userId}.`);
}
if (attempt.isCompleted) {
throw new BadRequestException('This placement test attempt is already
completed.');
}
const questions = attempt.questions as unknown as PlacementTestQuestionDto[];
const currentQuestion = questions.find(q => q.id === questionId);
if (!currentQuestion) {
throw new BadRequestException(`Question with ID ${questionId} not found in
this attempt.`);
}
// Simulate checking the answer (in a real scenario, this would involve a
question bank lookup)
const isCorrect = this.checkAnswer(currentQuestion, answer);
const updatedAnswers = [...(attempt.answers as Prisma.JsonArray), answer];
const updatedResults = [...(attempt.results as Prisma.JsonArray), isCorrect];
let newDifficultyLevel = attempt.difficultyLevel;
let newConsecutiveWrong = isCorrect ? 0 : attempt.consecutiveWrong + 1;
let isTestCompleted = false;
let finalScore: number | null = null;
let nextQuestion: PlacementTestQuestionDto | null = null;
if (isCorrect) {
// Increase difficulty on correct answer, up to MAX_DIFFICULTY
newDifficultyLevel = Math.min(newDifficultyLevel + 1, this.MAX_DIFFICULTY);
} else {
// Decrease difficulty on wrong answer, down to INITIAL_DIFFICULTY
newDifficultyLevel = Math.max(newDifficultyLevel - 1,
this.INITIAL_DIFFICULTY);
}
// Check for test completion condition (3 consecutive wrong answers)
if (newConsecutiveWrong >= this.MAX_CONSECUTIVE_WRONG) {
isTestCompleted = true;
finalScore = this.calculateFinalScore(updatedResults as boolean[]);
} else {

// Fetch the next question based on the new difficulty level
nextQuestion = await this.fetchQuestionByDifficulty(newDifficultyLevel);
if (!nextQuestion) {
// If no more questions at this difficulty, consider test completed or
move to next available difficulty
isTestCompleted = true;
finalScore = this.calculateFinalScore(updatedResults as boolean[]);
}
}
// Update the attempt record
attempt = await this.prisma.placementTestAttempt.update({
where: { id: attemptId },
data: {
difficultyLevel: newDifficultyLevel,
consecutiveWrong: newConsecutiveWrong,
questions: nextQuestion ? [...questions, nextQuestion] as
Prisma.JsonArray : questions,
answers: updatedAnswers,
results: updatedResults,
isCompleted: isTestCompleted,
score: finalScore,
},
});
return {
attemptId: attempt.id,
isCorrect,
nextQuestion: nextQuestion || undefined,
isCompleted: isTestCompleted,
finalScore: finalScore || undefined,
};
}
/**
* @summary Simulates checking if the provided answer is correct.
* In a real application, this would involve a more complex logic, potentially
querying a question bank.
* @param {PlacementTestQuestionDto} question The question object.
* @param {string} userAnswer The user's answer.

*/
private checkAnswer(question: PlacementTestQuestionDto, userAnswer: string):
boolean {
// This is a placeholder. In a real system, this would compare against a
stored correct answer.
return question.correctAnswer === userAnswer;
}

/**

private calculateFinalScore(results: boolean[]): number {
if (results.length === 0) return 0;

// src/learning-path/dto/learning-path.dto.ts

SECTION E: Complete NestJS Gamification System

SECTION E: Complete NestJS Gamification
System
This section provides an exhaustive architectural and implementation guide for the EliTutor
platform’s gamification system, built on NestJS. It details the core services responsible for
managing user engagement through game mechanics such as hearts, streaks, experience
points (XP), gems, leagues, and achievements. Each service is described with extreme
precision, including file paths, complete TypeScript code blocks, JSDoc comments, error
handling, Redis key naming conventions with TTLs, and relevant Prisma schema snippets.

1. HeartsService
The HeartsService manages the user’s “hearts” or “lives” system, a common gamification
mechanic that limits activity and encourages focused learning. Users lose a heart for incorrect
answers and regenerate hearts over time. This service ensures a balanced and engaging
learning pace.

1.1. Prisma Schema Definition
First, we define the User model in prisma/schema.prisma to include fields relevant to the
Hearts system. This includes hearts , lastHeartRegenerationAt , and maxHearts .
File: prisma/schema.prisma

// prisma/schema.prisma
model User {
id

String

@id @default(uuid())

email

String

@unique

username

String

@unique

password

String

hearts

Int

@default(5) // Current number of hearts

maxHearts

Int

@default(5) // Maximum hearts a user can have

lastHeartRegenerationAt DateTime

@default(now()) // Timestamp of the last heart

regeneration
// Other user fields...
@@map("users")
}
// Other models...

Explanation:
hearts : An integer representing the current number of hearts a user has. Defaults to 5.
maxHearts : An integer representing the maximum hearts a user can accumulate. Defaults

to 5. This can be upgraded through in-app purchases or achievements.
lastHeartRegenerationAt : A DateTime field storing the timestamp when the user’s

hearts were last regenerated or when a heart was spent. This is crucial for calculating the
next regeneration time.

1.2. Configuration
Gamification parameters, such as heart regeneration rates, should be configurable. We’ll use a
config module for this.

File: src/config/gamification.config.ts

// src/config/gamification.config.ts
export const GamificationConfig = {
hearts: {
initialHearts: 5,
maxHearts: 5,
regenerationTimeMinutes: 30, // Time in minutes to regenerate one heart
regenerationIntervalMs: 30 * 60 * 1000, // Regeneration interval in
milliseconds
},
// Other gamification configs...
};

Explanation:
initialHearts : The number of hearts a new user starts with.
maxHearts : The default maximum number of hearts.
regenerationTimeMinutes : The duration, in minutes, it takes for one heart to

regenerate.
regenerationIntervalMs : The regeneration interval in milliseconds, derived from
regenerationTimeMinutes .

1.3. HeartsModule
The HeartsModule will encapsulate all components related to the Hearts system.
File: src/gamification/hearts/hearts.module.ts

// src/gamification/hearts/hearts.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { HeartsService } from './hearts.service';
import { HeartsController } from './hearts.controller';

@Module({

providers: [HeartsService],
controllers: [HeartsController],

})

Explanation:
PrismaModule : Provides access to the Prisma client for database interactions.
RedisModule : Provides access to the Redis client for caching and real-time updates.
HeartsService : The core service logic.

1.4. HeartsService
This service contains the core logic for heart management, including depletion, regeneration,
and retrieval of heart status.
File: src/gamification/hearts/hearts.service.ts

// src/gamification/hearts/hearts.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RedisService } from '../../redis/redis.service';
import { GamificationConfig } from '../../config/gamification.config';
import { User } from '@prisma/client';
@Injectable()
export class HeartsService implements OnModuleInit {
private readonly logger = new Logger(HeartsService.name);
private readonly HEART_REGENERATION_INTERVAL_MS =
GamificationConfig.hearts.regenerationIntervalMs;
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly redis: RedisService,
) {}
async onModuleInit() {
// Optional: Initialize any Redis keys or perform checks on startup
this.logger.log('HeartsService initialized.');
}
/**
* Redis Key Naming Convention:
* `user:{{userId}}:hearts` - Stores the current number of hearts for a user.
Used for quick reads.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "3")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change, kept in sync with DB.

*
* `user:{{userId}}:last_heart_regen` - Stores the timestamp of the last heart
regeneration or depletion.
*

Type: String

*

Value: ISO 8601 string (e.g., "2023-10-27T10:00:00.000Z")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change, kept in sync with DB.

*/
private getUserHeartsRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:hearts`;
}
private getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:last_heart_regen`;
}
/**
* Retrieves the current hearts and maximum hearts for a user.

* It first attempts to fetch from Redis for performance, then falls back to
the database.
* It also triggers heart regeneration if necessary.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns An object containing current hearts and max hearts.
*/
async getHearts(userId: string): Promise<{ hearts: number; maxHearts: number;
nextRegenerationAt: Date | null }> {
try {
// Attempt to get hearts from Redis
const cachedHearts = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserHeartsRedisKey(userId));
const cachedLastRegen = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(userId));
let user: User | null;
if (cachedHearts !== null && cachedLastRegen !== null) {
// If cached data exists, create a mock user object for regeneration
logic
user = {
id: userId,
hearts: parseInt(cachedHearts, 10),
maxHearts: GamificationConfig.hearts.maxHearts, // Assume default
maxHearts for cached user, or fetch from DB if needed
lastHeartRegenerationAt: new Date(cachedLastRegen),
// Other user fields are not needed for heart logic here
} as User; // Type assertion as we only need specific fields
this.logger.debug(`Hearts for user ${userId} retrieved from Redis.`);
} else {
// Fallback to database if not in Redis or incomplete
user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { id: true, hearts: true, maxHearts: true,
lastHeartRegenerationAt: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
// Cache to Redis if fetched from DB
await this.redis.set(this.getUserHeartsRedisKey(userId),
user.hearts.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(userId),
user.lastHeartRegenerationAt.toISOString());
this.logger.debug(`Hearts for user ${userId} retrieved from DB and
cached.`);
}

// Regenerate hearts if applicable
const updatedUser = await this.regenerateHearts(user);
const nextRegenerationAt = updatedUser.hearts < updatedUser.maxHearts
? new Date(updatedUser.lastHeartRegenerationAt.getTime() +
this.HEART_REGENERATION_INTERVAL_MS)
: null;
return { hearts: updatedUser.hearts, maxHearts: updatedUser.maxHearts,
nextRegenerationAt };
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get hearts for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not retrieve hearts information.');
}
}
/**
* Depletes one heart from the user's current count.
* This is typically called when a user answers a question incorrectly.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns The updated number of hearts.
* @throws Error if the user has no hearts left or user not found.
*/
async depleteHeart(userId: string): Promise<number> {
try {
// Ensure hearts are up-to-date before depletion
const { hearts, maxHearts } = await this.getHearts(userId);
if (hearts <= 0) {
throw new Error('User has no hearts left to deplete.');
}
const newHearts = hearts - 1;
const now = new Date();
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
hearts: newHearts,
lastHeartRegenerationAt: newHearts < maxHearts ? now : undefined, //
Update regen time only if not full
},
select: { hearts: true, maxHearts: true, lastHeartRegenerationAt: true },
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserHeartsRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.hearts.toString());

if (updatedUser.lastHeartRegenerationAt) {
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.lastHeartRegenerationAt.toISOString());
}
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} depleted a heart. Remaining:
${updatedUser.hearts}`);
return updatedUser.hearts;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to deplete heart for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw error; // Re-throw to be handled by controller or global exception
filter
}
}
/**
* Regenerates hearts for a user based on elapsed time since last regeneration.
* This method is called internally by `getHearts` to ensure hearts are always
up-to-date.
* It calculates how many hearts should have regenerated and updates the user's
record.
* @param user The user object (partial, containing id, hearts, maxHearts,
lastHeartRegenerationAt).
* @returns The updated user object with regenerated hearts.
*/
private async regenerateHearts(user: Pick<User, 'id' | 'hearts' | 'maxHearts' |
'lastHeartRegenerationAt'>): Promise<Pick<User, 'id' | 'hearts' | 'maxHearts' |
'lastHeartRegenerationAt'>> {
if (user.hearts >= user.maxHearts) {
return user; // No regeneration needed if hearts are full
}
const now = new Date();
const timeElapsedMs = now.getTime() - user.lastHeartRegenerationAt.getTime();
const heartsToRegenerate = Math.floor(timeElapsedMs /
this.HEART_REGENERATION_INTERVAL_MS);
if (heartsToRegenerate <= 0) {
return user; // No hearts to regenerate yet
}
const newHearts = Math.min(user.hearts + heartsToRegenerate, user.maxHearts);
let newLastHeartRegenerationAt = user.lastHeartRegenerationAt;
if (newHearts < user.maxHearts) {
// If hearts are not yet full, update lastRegen time to reflect the
regenerated hearts

newLastHeartRegenerationAt = new
Date(user.lastHeartRegenerationAt.getTime() + (heartsToRegenerate *
this.HEART_REGENERATION_INTERVAL_MS));
} else {
// If hearts are full, set lastRegen time to now (or keep as is, as it
won't be used until a heart is depleted)
newLastHeartRegenerationAt = now;
}
try {
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: user.id },
data: {
hearts: newHearts,
lastHeartRegenerationAt: newLastHeartRegenerationAt,
},
select: { id: true, hearts: true, maxHearts: true,
lastHeartRegenerationAt: true },
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserHeartsRedisKey(user.id),
updatedUser.hearts.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(user.id),
updatedUser.lastHeartRegenerationAt.toISOString());
this.logger.log(`User ${user.id} regenerated ${heartsToRegenerate} hearts.
Total: ${updatedUser.hearts}`);
return updatedUser;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to regenerate hearts for user ${user.id}:
${error.message}`);
// If DB update fails, return the original user object to avoid breaking
the flow,
// but log the error. The next request will try again.
return user;
}
}
/**
* Refills a user's hearts to maximum.
* This can be triggered by an in-app purchase, an achievement, or an admin
action.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns The updated number of hearts.
*/
async refillHearts(userId: string): Promise<number> {
try {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({

where: { id: userId },
select: { maxHearts: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
const now = new Date();
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
hearts: user.maxHearts,
lastHeartRegenerationAt: now, // Reset regen time as hearts are full
},
select: { hearts: true },
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserHeartsRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.hearts.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLastHeartRegenRedisKey(userId),
now.toISOString());
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} hearts refilled to max
(${updatedUser.hearts}).`);
return updatedUser.hearts;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to refill hearts for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not refill hearts.');
}
}
}

Explanation:
Redis Caching: The service heavily utilizes Redis to cache the current heart count and
the last regeneration timestamp. This significantly reduces database load for frequent read
operations (e.g., checking hearts before starting a lesson).
Regeneration Logic: The regenerateHearts method calculates the number of hearts to
add based on the time elapsed since lastHeartRegenerationAt . It updates the
database and Redis cache accordingly. This is called lazily within getHearts to ensure
the user always sees their up-to-date heart count without needing a background cron job
constantly updating every user.

Depletion Logic: depleteHeart reduces the heart count by one. If the user was
previously at max hearts, it sets lastHeartRegenerationAt to the current time, starting
the regeneration timer.
Refill Logic: refillHearts sets the heart count to maxHearts and resets the
regeneration timer.

2. StreakService
The StreakService tracks consecutive days of user activity. A streak is maintained if the user
completes at least one lesson or activity per day. It also handles “streak freezes,” which allow a
user to miss a day without losing their streak.

2.1. Prisma Schema Definition
We need to add fields to the User model to track streaks and streak freezes.
File: prisma/schema.prisma
// prisma/schema.prisma
model User {
// ... previous fields (id, email, hearts, etc.)
currentStreak

Int

@default(0) // Current consecutive days active

longestStreak

Int

@default(0) // Longest streak achieved

lastActivityDate

DateTime? // Date of the last activity that counted

towards the streak
streakFreezes

Int

@default(0) // Number of streak freezes

available
// ... other fields
}

Explanation:
currentStreak : The number of consecutive days the user has been active.
longestStreak : The user’s all-time highest streak.
lastActivityDate : The date (ignoring time) of the user’s last qualifying activity. This is

crucial for determining if a streak is maintained, broken, or needs a freeze applied.
streakFreezes : The number of “streak freeze” items the user owns.

2.2. Configuration
File: src/config/gamification.config.ts

// ... hearts config

freezeCostGems: 200, // Cost in gems to buy a streak freeze
maxFreezes: 2, // Maximum number of streak freezes a user can hold
},
};

2.4. StreakService
This service handles the logic for updating streaks based on daily activity and applying streak
freezes.
File: src/gamification/streaks/streaks.service.ts

// src/gamification/streaks/streaks.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RedisService } from '../../redis/redis.service';
import { User } from '@prisma/client';
import * as dayjs from 'dayjs';
import * as utc from 'dayjs/plugin/utc';
import * as timezone from 'dayjs/plugin/timezone';
dayjs.extend(utc);
dayjs.extend(timezone);
@Injectable()
export class StreaksService {
private readonly logger = new Logger(StreaksService.name);
// Assuming platform operates on a specific timezone for "daily" resets, e.g.,
Asia/Jerusalem
private readonly PLATFORM_TIMEZONE = 'Asia/Jerusalem';
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly redis: RedisService,
) {}
/**
* Redis Key Naming Convention:
* `user:{{userId}}:streak` - Stores the current streak count.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "15")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*
* `user:{{userId}}:last_activity_date` - Stores the date string of last
activity.
*

Type: String

*

Value: YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g., "2023-10-27")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*/
private getUserStreakRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:streak`;
}
private getUserLastActivityDateRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:last_activity_date`;
}
/**
* Gets the current date in the platform's timezone as a YYYY-MM-DD string.

*/
private getCurrentPlatformDateString(): string {
return dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).format('YYYY-MM-DD');
}
/**
* Records a user's activity for the day and updates their streak.
* This should be called when a user completes a lesson or significant action.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns An object containing the updated streak information.
*/
async recordActivity(userId: string): Promise<{ currentStreak: number;
longestStreak: number; streakMaintained: boolean }> {
try {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { id: true, currentStreak: true, longestStreak: true,
lastActivityDate: true, streakFreezes: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
const todayStr = this.getCurrentPlatformDateString();
const todayDate = dayjs.tz(todayStr,
this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).startOf('day');
let lastActivityDateStr = null;
let lastActivityDate = null;
if (user.lastActivityDate) {
lastActivityDateStr =
dayjs(user.lastActivityDate).tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).format('YYYY-MM-DD');
lastActivityDate = dayjs.tz(lastActivityDateStr,
this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).startOf('day');
}
// If activity was already recorded today, do nothing
if (lastActivityDateStr === todayStr) {
return {
currentStreak: user.currentStreak,
longestStreak: user.longestStreak,
streakMaintained: true,
};
}
let newCurrentStreak = user.currentStreak;
let newLongestStreak = user.longestStreak;

let newStreakFreezes = user.streakFreezes;
let streakMaintained = false;
if (!lastActivityDate) {
// First ever activity
newCurrentStreak = 1;
streakMaintained = true;
} else {
const daysDifference = todayDate.diff(lastActivityDate, 'day');
if (daysDifference === 1) {
// Consecutive day activity
newCurrentStreak += 1;
streakMaintained = true;
} else if (daysDifference > 1) {
// Missed one or more days. Check for streak freezes.
const missedDays = daysDifference - 1;
if (user.streakFreezes >= missedDays) {
// User has enough freezes to cover the missed days
newStreakFreezes -= missedDays;
newCurrentStreak += 1; // Increment streak as if they didn't miss
streakMaintained = true;
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} used ${missedDays} streak freeze(s).
Remaining: ${newStreakFreezes}`);
} else {
// Not enough freezes, streak is broken
newCurrentStreak = 1; // Reset to 1 for today's activity
streakMaintained = false;
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} streak broken. Reset to 1.`);
}
}
}
// Update longest streak if necessary
if (newCurrentStreak > newLongestStreak) {
newLongestStreak = newCurrentStreak;
}
// Update database
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
currentStreak: newCurrentStreak,
longestStreak: newLongestStreak,
lastActivityDate: todayDate.toDate(), // Store as UTC Date object in DB
streakFreezes: newStreakFreezes,
},
select: { currentStreak: true, longestStreak: true },

});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserStreakRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.currentStreak.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLastActivityDateRedisKey(userId),
todayStr);
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} activity recorded. Current streak:
${updatedUser.currentStreak}`);
return {
currentStreak: updatedUser.currentStreak,
longestStreak: updatedUser.longestStreak,
streakMaintained,
};
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to record activity for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not record activity and update streak.');
}
}
/**
* Retrieves the user's current streak information.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns The current streak count.
*/
async getStreak(userId: string): Promise<number> {
try {
const cachedStreak = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserStreakRedisKey(userId));
if (cachedStreak !== null) {
return parseInt(cachedStreak, 10);
}
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { currentStreak: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
await this.redis.set(this.getUserStreakRedisKey(userId),
user.currentStreak.toString());
return user.currentStreak;
} catch (error) {

this.logger.error(`Failed to get streak for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not retrieve streak information.');
}
}
}

Explanation:
Timezone Handling: Streaks are highly dependent on timezones. The service uses
dayjs with timezone support to ensure “daily” resets happen at midnight according to the

platform’s configured timezone (e.g., Asia/Jerusalem ), regardless of the server’s UTC
time.
Activity Recording: The recordActivity method calculates the difference in days
between the current date and the lastActivityDate .
If daysDifference === 1 , the streak increments.
If daysDifference > 1 , it checks if the user has enough streakFreezes to cover
the missed days. If so, freezes are consumed, and the streak continues. If not, the
streak resets to 1.
Redis Caching: The current streak and last activity date string are cached in Redis for fast
retrieval.

2.5. Streak Milestone Detection (Optional)
To detect streak milestones (e.g., 7-day streak, 30-day streak), you can extend the
recordActivity method or create a separate event listener. For simplicity, we will outline the

logic here.

// Inside recordActivity, after updating newCurrentStreak:
// Example: Check for 7-day streak milestone
if (newCurrentStreak === 7) {
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} achieved a 7-day streak milestone!`);
// Trigger achievement, grant gems, etc.
// await this.achievementsService.grantAchievement(userId, 'SEVEN_DAY_STREAK');
}
// Example: Check for 30-day streak milestone
if (newCurrentStreak === 30) {
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} achieved a 30-day streak milestone!`);
// Trigger achievement, grant gems, etc.
// await this.achievementsService.grantAchievement(userId,
'THIRTY_DAY_STREAK');
}

3. XPService
The XPService manages the user’s Experience Points (XP), which are crucial for progression
and leveling up within the EliTutor platform. XP is earned through various activities, and this
service tracks both total XP and weekly XP for leaderboards.

3.1. Prisma Schema Definition
We need to add fields to the User model for XP tracking.
File: prisma/schema.prisma
// prisma/schema.prisma
model User {
// ... previous fields (id, email, hearts, streak, etc.)
totalXp

Int

@default(0) // Total accumulated XP

weeklyXp

Int

@default(0) // XP earned this week for weekly

DateTime

@default(now()) // Timestamp of the last weekly

Int

@default(1) // Current user level

leaderboards
lastWeeklyXpReset
XP reset
level
// ... other fields
}

Explanation:

totalXp : The cumulative experience points a user has earned throughout their journey.

This determines their overall level.
weeklyXp : XP earned within the current week. This is used for weekly leaderboards and

resets periodically.
lastWeeklyXpReset : The timestamp of the last time weeklyXp was reset. Used to

determine if a reset is due.
level : The user’s current level, derived from totalXp .

Explanation:

xpPerCorrectAnswer : XP awarded for each correct answer in a quiz or exercise.
xpPerLessonCompletion : XP awarded upon completing an entire lesson.
xpPerQuizCompletion : XP awarded upon completing a quiz.
xpPerDailyLogin : Bonus XP for logging in daily.
xpPerAchievement : Base XP awarded when an achievement is unlocked.
xpPerStreakMilestone : Additional XP awarded for reaching specific streak milestones.
levelingCurve : An array defining the cumulative XP required to reach each subsequent

level. levelingCurve[0] is for Level 1, levelingCurve[1] for Level 2, and so on. The
index i corresponds to the XP needed to reach level i+1 .
