3.4. XPService
This service handles the logic for awarding XP, tracking total and weekly XP, and managing user
levels.
File: src/gamification/xp/xp.service.ts

// src/gamification/xp/xp.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RedisService } from '../../redis/redis.service';
import { GamificationConfig } from '../../config/gamification.config';
import { User } from '@prisma/client';
import * as dayjs from 'dayjs';
import * as utc from 'dayjs/plugin/utc';
import * as weekOfYear from 'dayjs/plugin/weekOfYear';
import * as timezone from 'dayjs/plugin/timezone';
dayjs.extend(utc);
dayjs.extend(weekOfYear);
dayjs.extend(timezone);
@Injectable()
export class XpService {
private readonly logger = new Logger(XpService.name);
private readonly PLATFORM_TIMEZONE = 'Asia/Jerusalem'; // Consistent with
StreakService
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly redis: RedisService,
) {}
/**
* Redis Key Naming Convention:
* `user:{{userId}}:total_xp` - Stores the user's total XP.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "1250")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*
* `user:{{userId}}:weekly_xp` - Stores the user's weekly XP.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "300")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change, reset by cron.

*
* `user:{{userId}}:level` - Stores the user's current level.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "5")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*/
private getUserTotalXpRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:total_xp`;
}

private getUserWeeklyXpRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:weekly_xp`;
}
private getUserLevelRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:level`;
}
/**
* Calculates the user's level based on their total XP and the leveling curve.
* @param totalXp The user's total XP.
* @returns The calculated level.
*/
private calculateLevel(totalXp: number): number {
const levelingCurve = GamificationConfig.xp.levelingCurve;
for (let i = levelingCurve.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
if (totalXp >= levelingCurve[i]) {
return i + 1; // Level is index + 1
}
}
return 1; // Default to level 1 if no XP or below first threshold
}
/**
* Awards XP to a user for a specific action.
* This method updates total XP, weekly XP, and potentially the user's level.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @param xpAmount The amount of XP to award.
* @returns An object containing the updated total XP, weekly XP, and new
level.
*/
async awardXp(userId: string, xpAmount: number): Promise<{ totalXp: number;
weeklyXp: number; level: number; levelUp: boolean }> {
if (xpAmount <= 0) {
this.logger.warn(`Attempted to award non-positive XP amount (${xpAmount})
to user ${userId}. Skipping.`);
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { totalXp: true, weeklyXp: true, level: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
return { totalXp: user.totalXp, weeklyXp: user.weeklyXp, level: user.level,
levelUp: false };
}
try {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({

where: { id: userId },
select: { id: true, totalXp: true, weeklyXp: true, lastWeeklyXpReset:
true, level: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
let currentTotalXp = user.totalXp;
let currentWeeklyXp = user.weeklyXp;
let currentLevel = user.level;
let levelUp = false;
// Check for weekly XP reset
const now = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
const lastReset = dayjs(user.lastWeeklyXpReset).tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
// Weekly reset happens on Monday at 00:00 in the platform timezone
const startOfCurrentWeek = now.startOf('week'); // dayjs week starts on
Sunday by default, adjust if needed
// For ISO week (Monday start), use .startOf('isoWeek')
// Assuming week starts on Sunday for simplicity here, adjust based on
Koter curriculum week definition
if (lastReset.isBefore(startOfCurrentWeek)) {
this.logger.log(`Weekly XP reset for user ${userId}. Previous weekly XP:
${currentWeeklyXp}`);
currentWeeklyXp = 0;
// Update lastWeeklyXpReset to now to prevent immediate re-reset
// This will be updated in the DB later
}
currentTotalXp += xpAmount;
currentWeeklyXp += xpAmount;
const newLevel = this.calculateLevel(currentTotalXp);
if (newLevel > currentLevel) {
levelUp = true;
currentLevel = newLevel;
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} leveled up to Level ${currentLevel}!`);
// Potentially trigger achievement for leveling up
// await this.achievementsService.grantAchievement(userId,
`LEVEL_${currentLevel}`);
}
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {

totalXp: currentTotalXp,
weeklyXp: currentWeeklyXp,
level: currentLevel,
lastWeeklyXpReset: lastReset.isBefore(startOfCurrentWeek) ?
now.toDate() : user.lastWeeklyXpReset, // Only update if reset occurred
},
select: { totalXp: true, weeklyXp: true, level: true },
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserTotalXpRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.totalXp.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserWeeklyXpRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.weeklyXp.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLevelRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.level.toString());
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} awarded ${xpAmount} XP. Total XP:
${updatedUser.totalXp}, Weekly XP: ${updatedUser.weeklyXp}, Level:
${updatedUser.level}`);
return { totalXp: updatedUser.totalXp, weeklyXp: updatedUser.weeklyXp,
level: updatedUser.level, levelUp };
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to award XP to user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not award XP.');
}
}
/**
* Retrieves the user's current XP and level information.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns An object containing total XP, weekly XP, and level.
*/
async getUserXpInfo(userId: string): Promise<{ totalXp: number; weeklyXp:
number; level: number }> {
try {
const cachedTotalXp = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserTotalXpRedisKey(userId));
const cachedWeeklyXp = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserWeeklyXpRedisKey(userId));
const cachedLevel = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserLevelRedisKey(userId));
if (cachedTotalXp !== null && cachedWeeklyXp !== null && cachedLevel !==
null) {
return {
totalXp: parseInt(cachedTotalXp, 10),

weeklyXp: parseInt(cachedWeeklyXp, 10),
level: parseInt(cachedLevel, 10),
};
}
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { totalXp: true, weeklyXp: true, level: true, lastWeeklyXpReset:
true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
// Perform a check for weekly XP reset even on read, to ensure data
consistency
const now = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
const lastReset = dayjs(user.lastWeeklyXpReset).tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
const startOfCurrentWeek = now.startOf('week');
let currentWeeklyXp = user.weeklyXp;
if (lastReset.isBefore(startOfCurrentWeek)) {
this.logger.log(`Weekly XP reset detected on read for user ${userId}.
Resetting weekly XP.`);
currentWeeklyXp = 0;
// Update DB to reflect the reset, but don't wait for it to return
current info
this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: { weeklyXp: 0, lastWeeklyXpReset: now.toDate() },
}).catch(e => this.logger.error(`Failed to update weekly XP reset on read
for user ${userId}: ${e.message}`));
}
// Cache to Redis
await this.redis.set(this.getUserTotalXpRedisKey(userId),
user.totalXp.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserWeeklyXpRedisKey(userId),
currentWeeklyXp.toString());
await this.redis.set(this.getUserLevelRedisKey(userId),
user.level.toString());
return { totalXp: user.totalXp, weeklyXp: currentWeeklyXp, level:
user.level };
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get XP info for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not retrieve XP information.');

}
}
/**
* Resets weekly XP for a specific user. This method is primarily for internal
use
* or by a scheduled cron job.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
*/
async resetWeeklyXp(userId: string): Promise<void> {
try {
const now = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
weeklyXp: 0,
lastWeeklyXpReset: now.toDate(),
},
});
await this.redis.set(this.getUserWeeklyXpRedisKey(userId), '0');
this.logger.log(`Weekly XP reset for user ${userId} via explicit call.`);
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to reset weekly XP for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not reset weekly XP.');
}
}
}

Explanation:
XP Earning Rules: GamificationConfig.xp defines various XP amounts for different
actions, making the system highly configurable.
Leveling Curve: The levelingCurve array in the config allows for a flexible and easily
adjustable progression system. calculateLevel determines the user’s current level
based on their totalXp .
Weekly XP Reset: weeklyXp is tracked for weekly leaderboards. The awardXp and
getUserXpInfo methods include logic to check if a new week has started (based on
PLATFORM_TIMEZONE and startOf('week') ) and reset weeklyXp if necessary. This

ensures that weekly leaderboards are always up-to-date.
Redis Caching: totalXp , weeklyXp , and level are cached in Redis to minimize
database reads for frequently accessed user data.
resetWeeklyXp : A dedicated method for cron jobs or administrative actions to explicitly

reset weekly XP. The awardXp and getUserXpInfo methods handle implicit resets when

a new week begins.

File: src/gamification/gems/gems.service.ts

// src/gamification/gems/gems.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RedisService } from '../../redis/redis.service';
import { GamificationConfig } from '../../config/gamification.config';
@Injectable()
export class GemsService {
private readonly logger = new Logger(GemsService.name);
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly redis: RedisService,
) {}
/**
* Redis Key Naming Convention:
* `user:{{userId}}:gems` - Stores the user's current gem balance.
*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "500")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*/
private getUserGemsRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:gems`;
}
/**
* Awards gems to a user for a specific action.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @param amount The amount of gems to award.
* @returns The user's new gem balance.
*/
async awardGems(userId: string, amount: number): Promise<number> {
if (amount <= 0) {
this.logger.warn(`Attempted to award non-positive gem amount (${amount}) to
user ${userId}. Skipping.`);
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { gems: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
return user.gems;
}
try {

const updatedUser = await this.prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
gems: {
increment: amount,
},
},
select: { gems: true },
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserGemsRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.gems.toString());
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} awarded ${amount} gems. New balance:
${updatedUser.gems}`);
return updatedUser.gems;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to award gems to user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not award gems.');
}
}
/**
* Deducts gems from a user's balance for a purchase or action.
* Ensures the user has sufficient gems before deducting.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @param amount The amount of gems to deduct.
* @returns The user's new gem balance.
* @throws Error if the user has insufficient gems or user not found.
*/
async spendGems(userId: string, amount: number): Promise<number> {
if (amount <= 0) {
this.logger.warn(`Attempted to spend non-positive gem amount (${amount})
for user ${userId}. Skipping.`);
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { gems: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
return user.gems;
}
try {
// Use a transaction to ensure atomicity: check balance and then update
const updatedUser = await this.prisma.$transaction(async (prisma) => {

const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { gems: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
if (user.gems < amount) {
throw new Error(`Insufficient gems. User has ${user.gems}, needs
${amount}.`);
}
return prisma.user.update({
where: { id: userId },
data: {
gems: {
decrement: amount,
},
},
select: { gems: true },
});
});
// Update Redis cache
await this.redis.set(this.getUserGemsRedisKey(userId),
updatedUser.gems.toString());
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} spent ${amount} gems. New balance:
${updatedUser.gems}`);
return updatedUser.gems;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to spend gems for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw error; // Re-throw to be handled by controller or global exception
filter
}
}
/**
* Retrieves the user's current gem balance.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns The user's current gem balance.
*/
async getGems(userId: string): Promise<number> {
try {
const cachedGems = await this.redis.get(this.getUserGemsRedisKey(userId));
if (cachedGems !== null) {

return parseInt(cachedGems, 10);
}
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { gems: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
await this.redis.set(this.getUserGemsRedisKey(userId),
user.gems.toString());
return user.gems;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get gems for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not retrieve gem balance.');
}
}
}

Explanation:
Awarding Gems: The awardGems method simply increments the user’s gem count in the
database and updates the Redis cache.
Spending Gems (Atomic Transaction): The spendGems method is critical. It uses a
Prisma transaction ( this.prisma.$transaction ) to ensure that checking the user’s
balance and deducting gems are performed atomically. This prevents race conditions
where a user might try to spend more gems than they have if multiple requests are
processed simultaneously.
Redis Caching: The user’s gem balance is cached in Redis for quick retrieval.

5. LeagueService
The LeagueService implements a competitive league system where users are grouped weekly
based on their performance (XP earned). Users are promoted or demoted based on their rank
within their league. This system uses Redis Sorted Sets for efficient leaderboard management.

5.1. Prisma Schema Definition
We need to add fields to the User model to track league information.
File: prisma/schema.prisma
// prisma/schema.prisma
model User {
// ... previous fields (id, email, hearts, streak, xp, gems, etc.)
league

String

@default("Bronze") // Current league name (e.g.,

Int

@default(0) // User's rank within their current

Bronze, Silver, Gold)
leagueRank
league (0-indexed)
// ... other fields
}

Explanation:
league : The name of the league the user is currently in. Defaults to “Bronze”.
leagueRank : The user’s rank within their current league. This is dynamic and updated

weekly.

5.2. Configuration
File: src/config/gamification.config.ts

// src/config/gamification.config.ts
export const GamificationConfig = {
// ... hearts, streaks, xp, gems config
leagues: {
leagueTiers: ["Bronze", "Silver", "Gold", "Platinum", "Diamond", "Master"],
// Ordered list of league tiers
leagueSize: 50, // Number of users per league group
promotionThreshold: 0.2, // Top 20% get promoted
demotionThreshold: 0.3, // Bottom 30% get demoted
// Day of the week for league reset (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ..., 6 =
Saturday)
// Assuming weekly reset on Sunday evening after activity for the week has
concluded.
resetDayOfWeek: 0, // Sunday
resetHour: 23, // 11 PM
resetMinute: 59, // 59 minutes
},
};

Explanation:
leagueTiers : An ordered array of league names, from lowest to highest. This defines the

progression path.
leagueSize : The number of users that will be grouped into a single league. This impacts

the competitiveness and group formation algorithm.
promotionThreshold : A percentage (e.g., 0.2 for 20%) indicating the top portion of a

league that will be promoted to the next tier.
demotionThreshold : A percentage (e.g., 0.3 for 30%) indicating the bottom portion of a

league that will be demoted to the previous tier.
resetDayOfWeek , resetHour , resetMinute : Define when the weekly league reset cron

job should run, based on the platform’s timezone.

5.4. LeagueService
This service orchestrates the weekly league cycle: group formation, promotion/demotion, and
leaderboard management using Redis Sorted Sets.
File: src/gamification/leagues/leagues.service.ts

// src/gamification/leagues/leagues.service.ts
import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaService } from '../../prisma/prisma.service';
import { RedisService } from '../../redis/redis.service';
import { GamificationConfig } from '../../config/gamification.config';
import { User } from '@prisma/client';
import { XpService } from '../xp/xp.service';
import * as dayjs from 'dayjs';
import * as utc from 'dayjs/plugin/utc';
import * as timezone from 'dayjs/plugin/timezone';
dayjs.extend(utc);
dayjs.extend(timezone);
@Injectable()
export class LeagueService {
private readonly logger = new Logger(LeagueService.name);
private readonly PLATFORM_TIMEZONE = 'Asia/Jerusalem';
private readonly LEAGUE_TIERS = GamificationConfig.leagues.leagueTiers;
private readonly LEAGUE_SIZE = GamificationConfig.leagues.leagueSize;
private readonly PROMOTION_THRESHOLD =
GamificationConfig.leagues.promotionThreshold;
private readonly DEMOTION_THRESHOLD =
GamificationConfig.leagues.demotionThreshold;
constructor(
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
private readonly redis: RedisService,
private readonly xpService: XpService,
) {}
/**
* Redis Key Naming Conventions:
* `league:{{leagueName}}:{{weekOfYear}}:{{year}}` - Redis Sorted Set for a
specific league in a given week/year.
*

Type: ZSET (Sorted Set)

*

Score: User's weekly XP

*

Member: userId

*

TTL: 2 weeks (to allow for historical data viewing for a short period)

*
* `user:{{userId}}:current_league` - Stores the user's current league name.
*

Type: String

*

Value: League Name (e.g., "Gold")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*
* `user:{{userId}}:current_league_rank` - Stores the user's current rank
within their league.

*

Type: String

*

Value: Integer (e.g., "5")

*

TTL: No TTL, updated on change.

*/
private getLeagueZSetKey(leagueName: string, week: number, year: number):
string {
return `league:${leagueName}:${week}:${year}`;
}
private getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:current_league`;
}
private getUserCurrentLeagueRankRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:current_league_rank`;
}
/**
* Retrieves the current week and year based on the platform's timezone.
* @returns An object containing the week number and year.
*/
private getCurrentWeekAndYear(): { week: number; year: number } {
const now = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE);
return {
week: now.week(), // dayjs().week() returns week of year (1-52/53)
year: now.year(),
};
}
/**
* Assigns new users to the lowest league tier or re-assigns users whose league
data is missing.
* This ensures every active user is part of a league.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
*/
async assignUserToDefaultLeague(userId: string): Promise<void> {
try {
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { id: true, league: true },
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found.`);
}
if (!user.league || !this.LEAGUE_TIERS.includes(user.league)) {
const defaultLeague = this.LEAGUE_TIERS[0]; // Bronze
await this.prisma.user.update({

where: { id: userId },
data: { league: defaultLeague },
});
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(userId),
defaultLeague);
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} assigned to default league:
${defaultLeague}`);
}
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to assign user ${userId} to default league:
${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not assign user to default league.');
}
}
/**
* Updates a user's weekly XP in their current league's Redis Sorted Set.
* This should be called whenever a user earns XP.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @param weeklyXp The user's current weekly XP.
* @param leagueName The user's current league name.
*/
async updateLeagueXp(userId: string, weeklyXp: number, leagueName: string):
Promise<void> {
try {
const { week, year } = this.getCurrentWeekAndYear();
const leagueKey = this.getLeagueZSetKey(leagueName, week, year);
// Add or update user's score in the sorted set
await this.redis.zadd(leagueKey, weeklyXp, userId);
// Set TTL for the sorted set to expire after 2 weeks
await this.redis.expire(leagueKey, 2 * 7 * 24 * 60 * 60); // 2 weeks in
seconds
this.logger.debug(`User ${userId} weekly XP (${weeklyXp}) updated in league
${leagueName} (Redis key: ${leagueKey}).`);
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to update league XP for user ${userId} in league
${leagueName}: ${error.message}`);
throw new Error('Could not update league XP.');
}
}
/**
* Retrieves the leaderboard for a specific league.
* @param leagueName The name of the league.
* @returns An array of objects, each containing userId and score (weekly XP).
*/
async getLeagueLeaderboard(leagueName: string): Promise<{ userId: string; xp:

number }[]> {
try {
const { week, year } = this.getCurrentWeekAndYear();
const leagueKey = this.getLeagueZSetKey(leagueName, week, year);
// ZREVRANGE returns members in descending order by score (XP)
const leaderboard = await this.redis.zrevrange(leagueKey, 0, -1,
'WITHSCORES');
const result: { userId: string; xp: number }[] = [];
for (let i = 0; i < leaderboard.length; i += 2) {
result.push({
userId: leaderboard[i],
xp: parseInt(leaderboard[i + 1], 10),
});
}
return result;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get leaderboard for league ${leagueName}:
${error.message}`);
return []; // Return empty array on error
}
}
/**
* Retrieves a user's current league and rank.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns An object containing league name and rank, or null if not found.
*/
async getUserLeagueInfo(userId: string): Promise<{ league: string; rank: number
} | null> {
try {
const cachedLeague = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(userId));
const cachedRank = await
this.redis.get(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRankRedisKey(userId));
if (cachedLeague !== null && cachedRank !== null) {
return { league: cachedLeague, rank: parseInt(cachedRank, 10) };
}
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: { league: true },
});
if (!user || !user.league) {
return null;
}

const { week, year } = this.getCurrentWeekAndYear();
const leagueKey = this.getLeagueZSetKey(user.league, week, year);
// ZREVRANK returns the rank (0-indexed) of a member in a sorted set, with
scores ordered from high to low
const rank = await this.redis.zrevrank(leagueKey, userId);
if (rank === null) {
// User might not be in the current week's leaderboard yet, or data
inconsistency
this.logger.warn(`User ${userId} not found in Redis leaderboard for
league ${user.league}.`);
// Attempt to re-add user to the leaderboard with their current weekly XP
const userXpInfo = await this.xpService.getUserXpInfo(userId);
if (userXpInfo) {
await this.updateLeagueXp(userId, userXpInfo.weeklyXp, user.league);
const reRank = await this.redis.zrevrank(leagueKey, userId);
if (reRank !== null) {
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(userId),
user.league);
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRankRedisKey(userId),
reRank.toString());
return { league: user.league, rank: reRank };
}
}
return { league: user.league, rank: -1 }; // Indicate not ranked yet or
error
}
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(userId),
user.league);
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRankRedisKey(userId),
rank.toString());
return { league: user.league, rank: rank };
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get user league info for ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
return null;
}
}
/**
* **CRON JOB ENTRY POINT:**
* This method is designed to be executed as a weekly cron job.
* It performs the league reset, including group formation, promotion, and
demotion.
* This should run once a week, e.g., Sunday 23:59 in the platform's timezone.

*/
async runWeeklyLeagueReset(): Promise<void> {
this.logger.log('Starting weekly league reset cron job...');
try {
const { week: currentWeek, year: currentYear } =
this.getCurrentWeekAndYear();
const previousWeek = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).subtract(1,
'week').week();
const previousYear = dayjs().tz(this.PLATFORM_TIMEZONE).subtract(1,
'week').year();
// 1. Get all users and their current league
const allUsers = await this.prisma.user.findMany({
select: { id: true, league: true, totalXp: true }, // totalXp for new
user placement if needed
});
// Group users by their current league
const usersByLeague: { [leagueName: string]: User[] } = {};
for (const user of allUsers) {
if (!usersByLeague[user.league]) {
usersByLeague[user.league] = [];
}
usersByLeague[user.league].push(user);
}
const userUpdates: { userId: string; newLeague: string; newRank: number }[]
= [];
// Process each league tier
for (let i = 0; i < this.LEAGUE_TIERS.length; i++) {
const currentLeagueName = this.LEAGUE_TIERS[i];
const nextLeagueName = this.LEAGUE_TIERS[i + 1];
const prevLeagueName = this.LEAGUE_TIERS[i - 1];
const leagueUsers = usersByLeague[currentLeagueName] || [];
if (leagueUsers.length === 0) {
this.logger.log(`No users in league ${currentLeagueName} for
processing.`);
continue;
}
// Get previous week's leaderboard for this league
const previousLeaderboard = await
this.getLeagueLeaderboard(currentLeagueName); // This will fetch from Redis
// Sort users by their XP from the previous week (descending)
previousLeaderboard.sort((a, b) => b.xp - a.xp);

const numUsersInLeague = previousLeaderboard.length;
const numToPromote = Math.floor(numUsersInLeague *
this.PROMOTION_THRESHOLD);
const numToDemote = Math.floor(numUsersInLeague *
this.DEMOTION_THRESHOLD);
this.logger.log(`Processing league ${currentLeagueName}:
${numUsersInLeague} users. Promote: ${numToPromote}, Demote: ${numToDemote}`);
for (let j = 0; j < numUsersInLeague; j++) {
const userInLeaderboard = previousLeaderboard[j];
let newLeague = currentLeagueName;
if (j < numToPromote && nextLeagueName) {
// Promote user
newLeague = nextLeagueName;
this.logger.log(`User ${userInLeaderboard.userId} promoted from
${currentLeagueName} to ${newLeague}`);
} else if (j >= numUsersInLeague - numToDemote && prevLeagueName !==
undefined) {
// Demote user (ensure not trying to demote from the lowest tier)
newLeague = prevLeagueName;
this.logger.log(`User ${userInLeaderboard.userId} demoted from
${currentLeagueName} to ${newLeague}`);
}
userUpdates.push({
userId: userInLeaderboard.userId,
newLeague: newLeague,
newRank: j, // Their rank in the previous week's leaderboard
});
}
}
// Apply all updates in a single transaction for efficiency and consistency
await this.prisma.$transaction(async (prisma) => {
for (const update of userUpdates) {
await prisma.user.update({
where: { id: update.userId },
data: {
league: update.newLeague,
leagueRank: update.newRank,
},
});
// Update Redis cache for user's current league and rank
await this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRedisKey(update.userId),
update.newLeague);
await

this.redis.set(this.getUserCurrentLeagueRankRedisKey(update.userId),
update.newRank.toString());
}
});
// After processing, reset weekly XP for all users for the new week
// This is crucial for the next week's leaderboard calculation
for (const user of allUsers) {
await this.xpService.resetWeeklyXp(user.id);
}
this.logger.log('Weekly league reset cron job completed successfully.');
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Weekly league reset failed: ${error.message}`);
// Depending on severity, might need to alert admins or retry
}
}

}
}
// Now, for each formed group, initialize their Redis Sorted Set for the new
week
for (const leagueName of Object.keys(leagueGroups)) {
for (const group of leagueGroups[leagueName]) {

// This allows for multiple groups per tier if total users > LEAGUE_SIZE

// If true group formation is needed, the leagueKey needs to include a
groupId.

## 6. AchievementsService
The `AchievementsService` is responsible for defining, tracking, and awarding
achievements to users based on various in-app conditions. It features a flexible
condition evaluation engine to support different types of achievements.
### 6.1. Prisma Schema Definition
We need a new model for `Achievement` and a many-to-many relationship with `User`
to track unlocked achievements.
**File:** `prisma/schema.prisma`
```prisma

id

String

@id @default(uuid())

name

String

@unique

description String
iconUrl

String?

points

Int

@default(0) // XP or other points awarded for achievement

gems

Int

@default(0) // Gems awarded for achievement

type

String

// e.g., "STREAK", "XP_MILESTONE", "LESSON_COUNT",

"CUSTOM"

condition

Json

// JSON object defining the conditions for unlocking

users

UserAchievement[]

@@map("achievements")
}

id

String

String

@id @default(uuid())

unlockedAt

DateTime

@default(now())

user

User

@relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

achievement

@@unique([userId, achievementId]) // A user can unlock an achievement only once

Explanation:
Achievement model:
name : Unique name of the achievement (e.g., “First Lesson”, “7-Day Streak”).
description : Human-readable description.
iconUrl : URL to the achievement icon.
points , gems : Rewards for unlocking the achievement.
type : Categorizes the achievement (e.g., STREAK , XP_MILESTONE ). This helps the

evaluation engine know which data to check.
condition : A JSON field that stores the specific criteria for unlocking the

achievement. This is the heart of the flexible evaluation engine.
UserAchievement model: A join table for the many-to-many relationship between User

and Achievement , tracking when an achievement was unlocked.

The condition field in the Achievement model will store JSON objects. Here are examples of

Example 2: XP Milestone Achievement

}

Value: JSON string of Achievement object

*

TTL: 1 hour (refreshable cache)

*/
private getUserUnlockedAchievementsRedisKey(userId: string): string {
return `user:${userId}:unlocked_achievements`;
}

private getAchievementDetailsRedisKey(achievementId: string): string {
return `achievement:${achievementId}`;
}
/**
* Retrieves all defined achievements from the database, caching them in Redis.
* @returns A promise that resolves to an array of Achievement objects.
*/
private async getAllAchievements(): Promise<Achievement[]> {
// In a real system, this might be cached more aggressively or loaded once on
startup
// For simplicity, we'll fetch from DB and cache for a short period.
const cachedAchievements = await this.redis.get('all_achievements');
if (cachedAchievements) {
return JSON.parse(cachedAchievements);
}
const achievements = await this.prisma.achievement.findMany();
await this.redis.set('all_achievements', JSON.stringify(achievements), 'EX',
3600); // Cache for 1 hour
return achievements;
}
/**
* Grants an achievement to a user if the conditions are met and it hasn't been
unlocked yet.
* This is the primary entry point for checking and awarding achievements.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @param achievementName The name of the achievement to check/grant.
* @returns A boolean indicating if the achievement was newly unlocked.
*/
async grantAchievement(userId: string, achievementName: string):
Promise<boolean> {
try {
const achievement = await this.prisma.achievement.findUnique({
where: { name: achievementName },
});
if (!achievement) {
this.logger.warn(`Achievement with name ${achievementName} not found.`);
return false;
}
// Check if already unlocked
const alreadyUnlocked = await this.prisma.userAchievement.count({
where: { userId, achievementId: achievement.id },
}) > 0;

if (alreadyUnlocked) {
this.logger.debug(`User ${userId} already unlocked achievement
${achievementName}.`);
return false;
}
// Evaluate condition
const userProgress = await
this.getUserProgressForAchievementEvaluation(userId);
const conditionMet = this.evaluateCondition(achievement.condition as
unknown as AchievementCondition, userProgress);
if (conditionMet) {
await this.prisma.$transaction(async (prisma) => {
// Record achievement unlock
await prisma.userAchievement.create({
data: {
userId,
achievementId: achievement.id,
},
});
// Award XP and Gems
if (achievement.points > 0) {
await this.xpService.awardXp(userId, achievement.points);
}
if (achievement.gems > 0) {
await this.gemsService.awardGems(userId, achievement.gems);
}
// Add to Redis Set of unlocked achievements
await this.redis.sadd(this.getUserUnlockedAchievementsRedisKey(userId),
achievement.id);
});
this.logger.log(`User ${userId} newly unlocked achievement:
${achievementName}. Awarded ${achievement.points} XP and ${achievement.gems}
gems.`);
return true;
}
return false;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to grant achievement ${achievementName} to user
${userId}: ${error.message}`);
throw new Error(`Could not grant achievement ${achievementName}.`);
}
}

/**
* Retrieves all achievements unlocked by a specific user.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns A promise that resolves to an array of Achievement objects unlocked
by the user.
*/
async getUserUnlockedAchievements(userId: string): Promise<Achievement[]> {
try {
const cachedUnlockedIds = await
this.redis.smembers(this.getUserUnlockedAchievementsRedisKey(userId));
if (cachedUnlockedIds && cachedUnlockedIds.length > 0) {
const allAchievements = await this.getAllAchievements();
return allAchievements.filter(ach => cachedUnlockedIds.includes(ach.id));
}
const userAchievements = await this.prisma.userAchievement.findMany({
where: { userId },
include: { achievement: true },
});
const unlockedAchievementIds = userAchievements.map(ua =>
ua.achievementId);
if (unlockedAchievementIds.length > 0) {
await this.redis.sadd(this.getUserUnlockedAchievementsRedisKey(userId),
...unlockedAchievementIds);
}
return userAchievements.map(ua => ua.achievement);
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to get unlocked achievements for user ${userId}:
${error.message}`);
return [];
}
}
/**
* Gathers all necessary user progress data required for achievement condition
evaluation.
* This method centralizes data fetching to optimize performance.
* @param userId The ID of the user.
* @returns An object containing various user progress metrics.
*/
private async getUserProgressForAchievementEvaluation(userId: string):
Promise<any> {
// Fetch user data from DB (or cache if available)
const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
where: { id: userId },
select: {

currentStreak: true,
totalXp: true,
// Add other relevant fields here, e.g., lessonsCompletedCount,
correctAnswersCount
// For example, if you have a separate LessonCompletion model:
// _count: {
//

select: { lessonCompletions: true, correctAnswers: true },

// },
},
});
if (!user) {
throw new Error(`User with ID ${userId} not found for achievement
evaluation.`);
}
// Placeholder for other progress data. In a real system, you'd fetch these
// from dedicated services or aggregate them here.
const lessonsCompletedCount = await this.prisma.lessonCompletion.count({
where: { userId } }); // Assuming a LessonCompletion model
const correctAnswersCount = await this.prisma.userAnswer.count({ where: {
userId, isCorrect: true } }); // Assuming a UserAnswer model
return {
currentStreak: user.currentStreak,
totalXp: user.totalXp,
lessonsCompleted: lessonsCompletedCount,
correctAnswers: correctAnswersCount,
// ... other progress metrics
};
}
/**
* Evaluates if a user's progress meets the conditions for a given achievement.
* This is the core of the achievement engine.
* @param condition The JSON condition object from the Achievement model.
* @param userProgress An object containing the user's current progress
metrics.
* @returns True if the condition is met, false otherwise.
*/
private evaluateCondition(condition: AchievementCondition, userProgress: any):
boolean {
switch (condition.type) {
case 'STREAK':
const streakCondition = condition as StreakCondition;
return userProgress.currentStreak >= streakCondition.minStreak;
case 'XP_MILESTONE':
const xpCondition = condition as XpMilestoneCondition;

return userProgress.totalXp >= xpCondition.minTotalXp;
case 'LESSON_COUNT':
const lessonCondition = condition as LessonCountCondition;
// If subjectId is specified, you'd need to filter lessonsCompleted by
subject
// For now, assuming total lessons completed.
return userProgress.lessonsCompleted >=
lessonCondition.minLessonsCompleted;
case 'CORRECT_ANSWERS':
const correctAnswersCondition = condition as CorrectAnswersCondition;
return userProgress.correctAnswers >=
correctAnswersCondition.minCorrectAnswers;
default:
this.logger.warn(`Unknown achievement condition type:
${condition.type}`);
return false;
}
}
}

Explanation:
Achievement and UserAchievement Models: These Prisma models define the structure

for achievements and track which users have unlocked them.
Flexible Condition Json Field: The condition field in the Achievement model is a
Json type, allowing for highly flexible and extensible achievement conditions without

requiring schema migrations for every new achievement type. The
AchievementCondition TypeScript types provide strong typing for these JSON

structures.
getAllAchievements : Retrieves and caches all achievement definitions, reducing

database load.
grantAchievement : This is the central method. It first checks if the achievement exists

and if the user has already unlocked it. Then, it calls
getUserProgressForAchievementEvaluation to gather all relevant user data and
evaluateCondition to check if the criteria are met. If unlocked, it records the

achievement, awards XP and gems, and updates the Redis cache.
getUserProgressForAchievementEvaluation : This crucial helper method is

responsible for fetching all necessary user data (streak, XP, lesson counts, correct

answers, etc.) required by the evaluateCondition engine. This centralizes data access
and can be optimized with caching or batching.
evaluateCondition : This is the core of the achievement engine. It takes an
AchievementCondition object and the userProgress data, then uses a switch

statement to evaluate the specific condition type. This design makes it easy to add new
achievement types by simply adding a new case to the switch statement and defining a
new condition interface.
Redis Caching: Unlocked achievement IDs are stored in a Redis Set ( user:
{{userId}}:unlocked_achievements ) for quick lookups. Achievement definitions

themselves are also cached.
This comprehensive guide covers the design and implementation of the core gamification
services for the EliTutor platform, providing a robust foundation for engaging user experiences.
Each service is designed with scalability, performance, and maintainability in mind, leveraging
NestJS, Prisma, and Redis for optimal operation.

SECTION F: Complete NestJS AI Integration System

SECTION F: Complete NestJS AI Integration
System
F.1 Introduction
This section details the complete Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration system within the EliTutor
platform, built using NestJS. This system is designed to enhance the educational experience for
Israeli Arab school students (Grades 1-12) by providing intelligent explanations, transcribing
audio, and processing homework submissions across all subjects (Arabic, Hebrew, English,
Math, Science) based on the Koter curriculum. The AI integration leverages various OpenAI
models, including GPT-4o-mini for explanations, Whisper for audio transcription, and GPT-4o
Vision for homework parsing. Robust error handling, caching mechanisms, and asynchronous
processing are critical components to ensure reliability, performance, and a seamless user
experience.
This document serves as the definitive guide for developers, providing exhaustive detail on
every file, function, and line of logic. It includes complete TypeScript code blocks, exact file

paths, comprehensive JSDoc comments, thorough error handling strategies, and relevant
SQL/Prisma schema snippets. The aim is to equip developers with all necessary information to
understand, implement, and maintain this complex AI integration system, assuming no prior
knowledge of the specific system architecture.

F.2 Core Concepts and Technologies
Before diving into the specifics of each AI service, it’s crucial to understand the foundational
technologies and concepts underpinning this integration.

F.2.1 NestJS
NestJS is a progressive Node.js framework for building efficient, reliable, and scalable serverside applications. It uses modern JavaScript, is built with TypeScript, and combines elements of
OOP (Object Oriented Programming), FP (Functional Programming), and FRP (Functional
Reactive Programming). NestJS provides a robust architecture that facilitates the creation of
highly maintainable and testable applications, making it an ideal choice for complex systems like
EliTutor.

F.2.2 OpenAI API
The OpenAI API provides access to powerful AI models. For EliTutor, we utilize three key
models:
GPT-4o-mini: A highly capable and cost-effective language model used for generating
clear, concise, and contextually relevant explanations for educational concepts. It excels at
understanding complex queries and synthesizing information into digestible formats
suitable for students.
Whisper: An advanced speech-to-text model capable of transcribing audio into text with
high accuracy. Its multilingual capabilities are crucial for handling Arabic, Hebrew, and
English audio inputs from students.
GPT-4o Vision: A multimodal model that can process both images and text. This is
instrumental for parsing homework submissions, which often involve images of handwritten
or printed assignments, allowing the system to understand and extract relevant
information.

F.2.3 Redis
Redis is an open-source, in-memory data structure store, used as a database, cache, and
message broker. In our AI integration, Redis serves as a high-performance caching layer for the
ExplanationService . This significantly reduces latency and API costs by storing frequently

requested explanations, preventing redundant calls to the OpenAI API.

F.2.4 AWS S3
Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is an object storage service offering industry-leading
scalability, data availability, security, and performance. It is used in the HomeworkService for
securely storing images of homework submissions before they are processed by the GPT-4o
Vision model. This ensures data persistence and provides a reliable source for image retrieval
during asynchronous processing.

F.2.5 Prisma & PostgreSQL
Prisma is an open-source ORM (Object-Relational Mapper) that simplifies database access and
management. It provides a type-safe API for interacting with our PostgreSQL database.
PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source object-relational database system known for its
reliability, feature robustness, and performance. These technologies are used to store and
manage application data, including user information, educational content, homework statuses,
and pre-written explanations.

F.3 ExplanationService
F.3.1 Overview
The ExplanationService is responsible for generating clear and concise explanations for
various educational concepts. It leverages the GPT-4o-mini model to provide dynamic, AIgenerated content. To optimize performance and reduce API costs, it incorporates a robust
caching mechanism using Redis. Furthermore, it includes a fallback system to deliver pre-written
explanations in cases where the OpenAI API is unavailable or fails, ensuring continuous service
availability.

F.3.2 Dependencies
To implement the ExplanationService , the following key dependencies are required:
@nestjs/common : Core NestJS utilities.

@nestjs/config : For managing environment variables and configuration.
openai : The official OpenAI Node.js client library.
ioredis : A robust, high-performance Redis client for Node.js.
@prisma/client : Prisma client for database interactions.

These dependencies should be installed via npm or yarn :

npm install @nestjs/common @nestjs/config openai ioredis @prisma/client

F.3.3 explanation.service.ts
This is the core service that orchestrates the explanation generation process, including OpenAI
API calls, caching, and fallback logic.

import { Injectable, Logger, InternalServerErrorException,
ServiceUnavailableException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import Redis from 'ioredis';
import { PrismaService } from '../prisma/prisma.service';
/**
* @interface ExplanationResponse
* @description Defines the structure for an explanation response.
* @property {string} explanation - The generated or retrieved explanation text.
* @property {boolean} fromCache - Indicates if the explanation was retrieved
from cache.
* @property {boolean} fromFallback - Indicates if the explanation was retrieved
from fallback.
*/
interface ExplanationResponse {
explanation: string;
fromCache: boolean;
fromFallback: boolean;
}
@Injectable()
export class ExplanationService {
private readonly openai: OpenAI;
private readonly redisClient: Redis;
private readonly logger = new Logger(ExplanationService.name);
private readonly REDIS_TTL_SECONDS: number = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60; // 30 days in
seconds
constructor(
private readonly configService: ConfigService,
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
) {
// Initialize OpenAI client with API key from configuration
const openaiApiKey = this.configService.get<string>('OPENAI_API_KEY');
if (!openaiApiKey) {
this.logger.error('OPENAI_API_KEY is not defined in environment
variables.');
throw new InternalServerErrorException('OpenAI API key is missing.');
}
this.openai = new OpenAI({
apiKey: openaiApiKey,
});
// Initialize Redis client with configuration from environment variables
const redisUrl = this.configService.get<string>('REDIS_URL');
if (!redisUrl) {

this.logger.error('REDIS_URL is not defined in environment variables.');
throw new InternalServerErrorException('Redis URL is missing.');
}
this.redisClient = new Redis(redisUrl);
// Log Redis connection status
this.redisClient.on('connect', () => this.logger.log('Connected to Redis.'));
this.redisClient.on('error', (err) => this.logger.error(`Redis Error:
${err.message}`));
}
/**
* @method explainConcept
* @description Generates an explanation for a given concept, utilizing caching
and a fallback mechanism.
* @param {string} concept - The educational concept to explain.
* @param {string} subject - The subject area of the concept (e.g., 'Math',
'Arabic', 'Science').
* @param {number} gradeLevel - The grade level of the student (1-12).
* @param {string} [language='ar'] - The target language for the explanation
(e.g., 'ar' for Arabic, 'he' for Hebrew, 'en' for English).
* @returns {Promise<ExplanationResponse>} An object containing the
explanation, and flags indicating if it came from cache or fallback.
* @throws {InternalServerErrorException} If an unexpected error occurs during
explanation generation or retrieval.
* @throws {ServiceUnavailableException} If both OpenAI API and fallback
mechanisms fail.
*/
async explainConcept(
concept: string,
subject: string,
gradeLevel: number,
language: string = 'ar',
): Promise<ExplanationResponse> {
const cacheKey =
`explanation:${language}:${subject}:${gradeLevel}:${concept}`;
this.logger.log(`Attempting to explain concept: '${concept}' for grade
${gradeLevel} in ${subject} (${language}).`);
// 1. Attempt to retrieve from Redis cache
try {
const cachedExplanation = await this.redisClient.get(cacheKey);
if (cachedExplanation) {
this.logger.log(`Explanation for '${concept}' found in cache.`);
return { explanation: cachedExplanation, fromCache: true, fromFallback:
false };
}
} catch (cacheError) {
this.logger.warn(`Failed to retrieve from Redis cache for '${concept}':

${cacheError.message}`);
// Continue to OpenAI if cache fails, but log the error
}
// 2. Attempt to generate explanation using OpenAI GPT-4o-mini
let aiExplanation: string | null = null;
try {
this.logger.log(`Calling OpenAI GPT-4o-mini for concept: '${concept}'.`);
const chatCompletion = await this.openai.chat.completions.create({
model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
messages: [
{
role: 'system',
content: this.getSystemPrompt(subject, gradeLevel, language),
},
{
role: 'user',

content: `‫اشرح لي مفهوم‬: ${concept} ‫بالتفصيل وبشكل مبسط ومناسب لطالب‬

‫ الصف‬${gradeLevel} ‫ في مادة‬${subject}.`,
},
],
temperature: 0.7,
max_tokens: 500,
top_p: 1,
frequency_penalty: 0,
presence_penalty: 0,
});

aiExplanation = chatCompletion.choices[0]?.message?.content || null;
if (aiExplanation) {
this.logger.log(`Successfully generated AI explanation for
'${concept}'.`);
// Store in Redis cache with TTL
try {
await this.redisClient.setex(cacheKey, this.REDIS_TTL_SECONDS,
aiExplanation);
this.logger.log(`Explanation for '${concept}' stored in Redis cache.`);
} catch (cacheSetError) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to set Redis cache for '${concept}':
${cacheSetError.message}`);
// Do not throw, continue with the explanation even if caching fails
}
return { explanation: aiExplanation, fromCache: false, fromFallback:
false };
} else {
this.logger.warn(`OpenAI returned an empty explanation for
'${concept}'.`);
}

} catch (openaiError: any) {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI API call failed for '${concept}':
${openaiError.message}`);
// Specific error handling for OpenAI API failures
if (openaiError instanceof OpenAI.APIError) {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI API Error Details: Status
${openaiError.status}, Code ${openaiError.code}, Type ${openaiError.type}`);
// Handle specific API errors like rate limits, invalid requests, etc.
// For production, consider implementing retry mechanisms with
exponential backoff.
} else if (openaiError.name === 'AbortError') {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI API call timed out for '${concept}'.`);
} else {
this.logger.error(`An unexpected error occurred during OpenAI API call
for '${concept}': ${openaiError.message}`);
}
}
// 3. Fallback to pre-written explanations from the database
try {
this.logger.log(`Attempting to retrieve fallback explanation for
'${concept}'.`);
const fallbackExplanation = await
this.prisma.preWrittenExplanation.findFirst({
where: {
concept: { equals: concept, mode: 'insensitive' }, // Case-insensitive
search
subject: { equals: subject, mode: 'insensitive' },
gradeLevel: gradeLevel,
language: language,
},
select: { content: true },
});
if (fallbackExplanation) {
this.logger.log(`Fallback explanation for '${concept}' found in
database.`);
return { explanation: fallbackExplanation.content, fromCache: false,
fromFallback: true };
}
} catch (dbError) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to retrieve fallback explanation from database
for '${concept}': ${dbError.message}`);
}
// If all attempts fail
this.logger.error(`Failed to provide explanation for '${concept}'. All
mechanisms (cache, AI, fallback) failed.`);
throw new ServiceUnavailableException(`Failed to retrieve explanation for

'${concept}'. Please try again later.`);
}

explainConcept method

This asynchronous method is the primary entry point for requesting explanations. It implements
the core logic:
1. Cache Lookup: It first attempts to retrieve the explanation from Redis using a unique
cacheKey generated from the concept, subject, grade level, and language. If found, it

returns the cached explanation immediately, significantly reducing latency and API costs.

2. OpenAI API Call: If the explanation is not in the cache, it constructs a system prompt
tailored to the student’s grade level, subject, and target language. It then calls the GPT-4omini model with the user’s concept. The system prompt ensures the AI generates
explanations that are appropriate for the target audience (Israeli Arab students, specific
grade level, specific subject, and language).
System Prompt Template: The getSystemPrompt method dynamically generates
the system prompt. For Arabic, it translates to: “‫أنت معلم ذكي ومساعد لطالب‬

‫ مهمتك هي شرح المفاهيم التعليمية‬.‫ وتحديدًا للطالب العرب‬،‫المدارس في إسرائيل‬
‫ مع التركيز على تبسيط المعلومات لتناسب مستوى فهم طالب الصف‬،‫بوضوح ودقة‬
[gradeLevel] ‫[ في مادة‬subject]. ،‫ سهلة الفهم‬،‫يجب أن تكون الشروحات شاملة‬

‫ وإذا كان لا بد‬،‫ تجنب المصطلحات المعقدة قدر الإمكان‬.‫وتستخدم أمثلة واقعية إن أمكن‬

‫ يجب أن تكون الإجابة‬.‫ فاشرحها بوضوح‬،‫[ من استخدامها‬languageInstruction] ‫فقط‬.” This
ensures the AI adopts the persona of a helpful teacher and tailors its response to the
specific context.
User Prompt: The user prompt is ‫اشرح لي مفهوم‬: ${concept} ‫بالتفصيل وبشكل‬

‫ مبسط ومناسب لطالب الصف‬${gradeLevel} ‫ في مادة‬${subject}. (Explain to me

the concept:

conceptindetailandinasimplif iedmannersuitablef orstudentsof grade
{gradeLevel} in subject ${subject}.)
3. Cache Storage: If a new explanation is successfully generated by OpenAI, it is stored in
Redis with a 30-day TTL (Time-To-Live) to serve future requests.
4. Fallback Mechanism: If the OpenAI API call fails (e.g., due to network issues, API limits,
or internal errors) or returns an empty response, the service attempts to retrieve a prewritten explanation from the PostgreSQL database via Prisma. This ensures a baseline
level of service even when external AI dependencies are unavailable.
5. Error Handling: Comprehensive error handling is implemented for both Redis and OpenAI
API interactions. Specific OpenAI.APIError types are caught to log detailed error
information. If all attempts (cache, AI, fallback) fail, a ServiceUnavailableException is
thrown.

Number, example: 7 })

type: String, required: false, enum: ['ar', 'he', 'en'], example: 'ar' })
@ApiResponse({ status: 200, description: 'Successfully retrieved explanation.'
})
@ApiResponse({ status: 400, description: 'Invalid or missing parameters.' })
@ApiResponse({ status: 500, description: 'Internal server error or service
unavailable.' })
async getExplanation(
@Query('concept') concept: string,
@Query('subject') subject: string,
@Query('gradeLevel') gradeLevel: number,

@Query('language') language: string = 'ar',
): Promise<{ explanation: string, fromCache: boolean, fromFallback: boolean }>
{
if (!concept || !subject || !gradeLevel) {
throw new BadRequestException('Concept, subject, and gradeLevel are
required query parameters.');
}
const parsedGradeLevel = parseInt(gradeLevel as any, 10);
if (isNaN(parsedGradeLevel) || parsedGradeLevel < 1 || parsedGradeLevel > 12)
{
throw new BadRequestException('gradeLevel must be a number between 1 and
12.');
}
if (!['ar', 'he', 'en'].includes(language.toLowerCase())) {
throw new BadRequestException('Language must be one of: ar, he, en.');
}
try {
this.logger.log(`Received request for explanation: concept='${concept}',
subject='${subject}', gradeLevel=${parsedGradeLevel}, language='${language}'`);
const result = await this.explanationService.explainConcept(concept,
subject, parsedGradeLevel, language.toLowerCase());
return result;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Error in getExplanation for concept '${concept}':
${error.message}`, error.stack);
// Re-throw specific exceptions or wrap generic errors
if (error instanceof BadRequestException || error instanceof
InternalServerErrorException) {
throw error;
}
throw new InternalServerErrorException('Failed to retrieve explanation due
to an unexpected error.');
}
}
}

F.3.6 Redis Caching Implementation
The caching mechanism is integrated directly into the ExplanationService .
Cache Key Generation: A unique key is generated for each explanation request using
explanation:${language}:${subject}:${gradeLevel}:${concept} . This ensures

that different requests (e.g., same concept but different grade level) have distinct cache
entries.
ioredis Client: The ioredis library is used for connecting to Redis. It’s initialized in the

constructor of ExplanationService using the REDIS_URL environment variable.
setex Command: When an explanation is successfully generated by OpenAI, it’s stored

using redisClient.setex(cacheKey, this.REDIS_TTL_SECONDS, aiExplanation) .
The setex command sets the key’s value and an expiration time (TTL) in seconds. Our
TTL is set to 30 days, balancing freshness with performance and cost savings.
Error Handling: Redis operations are wrapped in try-catch blocks. If Redis is
unavailable or an operation fails, the system logs a warning and proceeds to the next step
(OpenAI API call or fallback) without crashing, ensuring resilience.

F.3.7 Fallback Mechanism (Pre-written explanations)
The fallback mechanism is crucial for maintaining service availability when external AI services
are unreachable or fail.
Database Storage: Pre-written explanations are stored in the PostgreSQL database. The
PrismaService is used to interact with the PreWrittenExplanation model.

findFirst Query: If AI generation fails, the explainConcept method queries the
PreWrittenExplanation

table using

prisma.preWrittenExplanation.findFirst

with where clauses matching concept , subject , gradeLevel , and language . Caseinsensitive search ( mode: 'insensitive' ) is used for concept and subject to
increase matching flexibility.
Data Model: The PreWrittenExplanation model in the Prisma schema would look like
this:
File Path: prisma/schema.prisma
model PreWrittenExplanation {
id

String

concept

String

subject

String

@id @default(uuid())

gradeLevel Int
language

String

content

String

createdAt

DateTime @default(now())

updatedAt

DateTime @updatedAt

@db.Text

@@unique([concept, subject, gradeLevel, language])
@@index([concept, subject, gradeLevel, language])
}

id : Unique identifier for the explanation.
concept : The specific concept being explained (e.g., “Gravity”).
subject : The subject area (e.g., “Science”).
gradeLevel : The target grade level.
language : The language of the explanation.
content : The actual pre-written explanation text.
@@unique : Ensures no duplicate entries for the same concept, subject, grade level,

and language combination.
@@index : Improves query performance for these fields.

F.3.8 Error Handling
Error handling in ExplanationService is multi-layered:
OpenAI API Errors: The try-catch block around the
openai.chat.completions.create call specifically catches OpenAI.APIError

instances. This allows for logging detailed error information (status, code, type) provided
by the OpenAI API. In a production environment, this is where retry logic with exponential
backoff would be implemented for transient errors.
Redis Errors: try-catch blocks around redisClient.get and redisClient.setex
handle potential Redis connection or operation failures. These errors are logged as
warnings, and the system gracefully degrades by attempting the next mechanism (AI or
fallback) instead of failing immediately.
Database Errors: Errors during prisma.preWrittenExplanation.findFirst are
caught and logged, preventing the application from crashing due to database issues.
Service Unavailable: If all mechanisms (cache, AI, fallback) fail to provide an explanation,
a ServiceUnavailableException is thrown, indicating that the service cannot fulfill the
request at that moment.
Configuration Errors: Missing OPENAI_API_KEY or REDIS_URL environment variables
are caught during service initialization, leading to InternalServerErrorException to
prevent the application from starting with critical missing configurations.

F.4 WhisperService
F.4.1 Overview
The WhisperService is responsible for processing audio inputs, primarily for transcribing
spoken content into text. This is crucial for interactive learning features where students might
speak their answers or questions. It utilizes OpenAI’s Whisper model for transcription and
includes specialized logic for Arabic text normalization (removing tashkeel/diacritics) and
calculating Levenshtein distance for similarity comparisons, which can be used for evaluating
spoken responses.

F.4.2 Dependencies
To implement the WhisperService , the following key dependencies are required:
@nestjs/common : Core NestJS utilities.
@nestjs/config : For managing environment variables and configuration.
openai : The official OpenAI Node.js client library.
node-fetch or axios : For handling file uploads to OpenAI (if not using a local file path

directly).

These dependencies should be installed via npm or yarn :

npm install @nestjs/common @nestjs/config openai node-fetch

This is the core service for audio transcription and text processing utilities.
File Path: src/whisper/whisper.service.ts

import { Injectable, Logger, InternalServerErrorException, BadRequestException }
from '@nestjs/common';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
@Injectable()
export class WhisperService {
private readonly openai: OpenAI;
private readonly logger = new Logger(WhisperService.name);
constructor(private readonly configService: ConfigService) {
const openaiApiKey = this.configService.get<string>('OPENAI_API_KEY');
if (!openaiApiKey) {
this.logger.error('OPENAI_API_KEY is not defined in environment
variables.');
throw new InternalServerErrorException('OpenAI API key is missing.');
}
this.openai = new OpenAI({
apiKey: openaiApiKey,
});
}
/**
* @method transcribeAudio
* @description Transcribes an audio file into text using OpenAI's Whisper
model.
* @param {string} audioFilePath - The absolute path to the audio file on the
local filesystem.
* @param {string} [language='ar'] - The language of the audio (e.g., 'ar',
'he', 'en'). This helps Whisper improve accuracy.
* @returns {Promise<string>} The transcribed text.
* @throws {BadRequestException} If the audio file does not exist or is
inaccessible.
* @throws {InternalServerErrorException} If the OpenAI API call fails or
returns an empty transcription.
*/
async transcribeAudio(audioFilePath: string, language: string = 'ar'):
Promise<string> {
this.logger.log(`Attempting to transcribe audio file: ${audioFilePath} in
language: ${language}`);
if (!fs.existsSync(audioFilePath)) {
this.logger.error(`Audio file not found at path: ${audioFilePath}`);
throw new BadRequestException(`Audio file not found: ${audioFilePath}`);
}

try {
// OpenAI's Whisper API expects a file-like object. fs.createReadStream is
suitable.
const transcription = await this.openai.audio.transcriptions.create({
file: fs.createReadStream(audioFilePath),
model: 'whisper-1',
language: language, // Provide language hint for better accuracy
response_format: 'text',
});
if (!transcription) {
this.logger.warn(`Whisper API returned an empty transcription for file:
${audioFilePath}`);
throw new InternalServerErrorException('Whisper API returned an empty
transcription.');
}
this.logger.log(`Successfully transcribed audio. Text length:
${transcription.length}`);
return transcription;
} catch (openaiError: any) {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI Whisper API call failed for ${audioFilePath}:
${openaiError.message}`);
if (openaiError instanceof OpenAI.APIError) {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI API Error Details: Status
${openaiError.status}, Code ${openaiError.code}, Type ${openaiError.type}`);
} else if (openaiError.name === 'AbortError') {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI Whisper API call timed out for
'${audioFilePath}'.`);
}
throw new InternalServerErrorException(`Failed to transcribe audio:
${openaiError.message}`);
}
}
/**
* @method normalizeArabicText
* @description Removes Arabic tashkeel (diacritics) from a given text string.
*

This is useful for text comparison where diacritics might cause

mismatches.
* @param {string} text - The Arabic text to normalize.
* @returns {string} The normalized Arabic text without tashkeel.
*/
normalizeArabicText(text: string): string {
// Regex to match Arabic tashkeel characters
// َ (fatha), ً (fatḥatan), ُ (ḍamma), ٌ (ḍammatan), ِ (kasra), ٍ (kasratan), ْ
(sukūn), ّ (shaddah)

[ً
const tashkeelRegex = / -ْ\u0618-‫\ؚ‬u06D6-ۜ\u06DF-ۤ\u06E7\u06E8\u06EA-ۭ]/g;
return text.replace(tashkeelRegex, '');

}
/**
* @method calculateLevenshteinDistance
* @description Calculates the Levenshtein distance between two strings.
*

The Levenshtein distance is a metric for measuring the

difference between two sequences.
*

It is the minimum number of single-character edits (insertions,

deletions or substitutions)
*

required to change one word into the other.

* @param {string} s1 - The first string.
* @param {string} s2 - The second string.
* @returns {number} The Levenshtein distance between s1 and s2.
*/
calculateLevenshteinDistance(s1: string, s2: string): number {
s1 = s1.toLowerCase();
s2 = s2.toLowerCase();
const costs: number[] = [];
for (let i = 0; i <= s1.length; i++) {
let lastValue = i;
for (let j = 0; j <= s2.length; j++) {
if (i === 0) {
costs[j] = j;
} else if (j > 0) {
let newValue = costs[j - 1];
if (s1.charAt(i - 1) !== s2.charAt(j - 1)) {
newValue = Math.min(Math.min(newValue, lastValue), costs[j]) + 1;
}
costs[j - 1] = lastValue;
lastValue = newValue;
}
}
if (i > 0) {
costs[s2.length] = lastValue;
}
}
return costs[s2.length];
}
/**
* @method calculateSimilarityPercentage
* @description Calculates the similarity percentage between two strings based
on Levenshtein distance.
* @param {string} s1 - The first string.
* @param {string} s2 - The second string.
* @returns {number} The similarity percentage (0-100).
*/
calculateSimilarityPercentage(s1: string, s2: string): number {

const maxLength = Math.max(s1.length, s2.length);
if (maxLength === 0) return 100; // Both strings are empty, considered 100%
similar
const distance = this.calculateLevenshteinDistance(s1, s2);
return ((maxLength - distance) / maxLength) * 100;
}
}

transcribeAudio method

File Handling: Takes an audioFilePath as input. It first validates if the file exists using
fs.existsSync . The OpenAI Whisper API expects a file-like object, which is provided

using fs.createReadStream(audioFilePath) .
Whisper API Call: Calls openai.audio.transcriptions.create with the audio file,
specifying whisper-1 as the model, and providing a language hint (e.g., ‘ar’, ‘he’, ‘en’)
to improve transcription accuracy. The response_format is set to ‘text’ to get a plain
string output.
Error Handling: Catches OpenAI.APIError for specific API issues and
BadRequestException if the file is not found. If the API returns an empty transcription, an
InternalServerErrorException is thrown.
normalizeArabicText method

Purpose: Arabic text often includes diacritics (tashkeel) which can vary in usage and might
cause issues when comparing text strings (e.g., a student’s spoken answer vs. a correct
answer). This method removes all common Arabic tashkeel characters.
Algorithm: Uses a regular expression

[ً -ْ
\u0618-‫\ؚ‬u06D6-ۜ\u06DF-ۤ

\u06E7\u06E8\u06EA-ۭ] to match and replace tashkeel characters with an empty string.
calculateLevenshteinDistance method

Purpose: This method computes the Levenshtein distance, a fundamental metric for string
similarity. It quantifies the minimum number of single-character edits (insertions, deletions,
or substitutions) required to change one string into the other. This is highly useful for
evaluating the accuracy of transcribed student responses against expected answers.
Algorithm: Implements the standard dynamic programming approach for Levenshtein
distance calculation. It initializes a cost array and iteratively fills it based on character
matches and mismatches. Both input strings are converted to lowercase to ensure caseinsensitive comparison.

calculateSimilarityPercentage method

Purpose: Provides a more intuitive similarity score (0-100%) based on the Levenshtein
distance. This can be directly used to grade or provide feedback on spoken answers.
Algorithm: Calculates ((maxLength - distance) / maxLength) * 100 , where
maxLength is the length of the longer string and distance is the Levenshtein distance.

Handles the edge case where both strings are empty.

*/
@Post('transcribe')
@UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor('audio', { storage: audioStorage }))
@ApiOperation({ summary: 'Transcribe an audio file using OpenAI Whisper' })
@ApiConsumes('multipart/form-data')
@ApiBody({
schema: {
type: 'object',

properties: {
audio: {
type: 'string',
format: 'binary',
description: 'Audio file to transcribe (e.g., .mp3, .wav, .m4a)',
},

type: 'string',

default: 'ar',

},
},
},

@ApiQuery({ name: 'language', description: 'The language of the audio (ar, he,
en)', type: String, required: false, enum: ['ar', 'he', 'en'], example: 'ar' })

schema: { example: { transcription: '‫هذا نص تجريبي‬.' } } })
@ApiResponse({ status: 400, description: 'Bad Request (e.g., no file uploaded,
invalid file type).' })
@ApiResponse({ status: 500, description: 'Internal Server Error (e.g.,
transcription failed).' })
async transcribeAudioFile(
@UploadedFile() file: Express.Multer.File,
@Query('language') language: string = 'ar',
): Promise<{ transcription: string }> {
if (!file) {
throw new BadRequestException('No audio file uploaded.');
}
const allowedMimeTypes = ['audio/mpeg', 'audio/wav', 'audio/mp4', 'audio/xm4a'];
if (!allowedMimeTypes.includes(file.mimetype)) {
// Clean up the invalid file
fs.unlink(file.path, (err) => {
if (err) this.logger.error(`Failed to delete invalid audio file:
${file.path}, Error: ${err.message}`);
});
throw new BadRequestException('Invalid audio file type. Only MP3, WAV, M4A
are allowed.');
}
try {
this.logger.log(`Received audio file for transcription:
${file.originalname}, path: ${file.path}`);
const transcription = await this.whisperService.transcribeAudio(file.path,
language.toLowerCase());
return { transcription };

} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Error transcribing audio file ${file.originalname}:
${error.message}`, error.stack);
throw new InternalServerErrorException('Failed to transcribe audio.');
} finally {
// Clean up the temporary audio file after transcription
fs.unlink(file.path, (err) => {
if (err) this.logger.error(`Failed to delete temporary audio file:
${file.path}, Error: ${err.message}`);
else this.logger.log(`Temporary audio file deleted: ${file.path}`);
});
}
}

F.5.1 Overview
The

HomeworkService

information from these images, extract relevant data, and validate it. The service employs an
asynchronous processing model, allowing students to submit homework and receive status
updates without waiting for immediate AI processing. AWS S3 is used for secure and scalable
storage of homework images.

joi or class-validator : For robust JSON schema validation.

These dependencies should be installed via npm or yarn :

@prisma/client joi

private readonly homeworkSchema = Joi.object<ParsedHomeworkResult>({

studentName: Joi.string().required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫اسم الطالب‬

‫مطلوب‬.' }),

subject: Joi.string().required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫المادة مطلوبة‬.'

}),
gradeLevel: Joi.number().integer().min(1).max(12).required().messages({
'any.required': '‫مستوى الصف مطلوب‬.', 'number.min': '1 ‫مستوى الصف يجب أن يكون بين‬
12 ‫و‬.', 'number.max': '12 ‫ و‬1 ‫مستوى الصف يجب أن يكون بين‬.' }),

assignmentTitle: Joi.string().required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫عنوان‬
‫الواجب مطلوب‬.' }),
questions: Joi.array().items(Joi.object({
question: Joi.string().required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫السؤال مطلوب‬.'
}),
studentAnswer: Joi.string().required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫إجابة‬

‫الطالب مطلوبة‬.' }),

isCorrect: Joi.boolean().allow(null),

})).min(1).required().messages({ 'any.required': '‫يجب أن يحتوي الواجب على سؤال‬

overallFeedback: Joi.string().allow(null, ''),

constructor(
private readonly configService: ConfigService,
private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
) {
const openaiApiKey = this.configService.get<string>('OPENAI_API_KEY');
if (!openaiApiKey) {
this.logger.error('OPENAI_API_KEY is not defined in environment
variables.');
throw new InternalServerErrorException('OpenAI API key is missing.');
}
this.openai = new OpenAI({
apiKey: openaiApiKey,
});
this.S3_BUCKET_NAME = this.configService.get<string>('AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME');
const awsRegion = this.configService.get<string>('AWS_REGION');
const awsAccessKeyId = this.configService.get<string>('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID');
const awsSecretAccessKey = this.configService.get<string>
('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY');
if (!this.S3_BUCKET_NAME || !awsRegion || !awsAccessKeyId ||
!awsSecretAccessKey) {
this.logger.error('Missing AWS S3 configuration in environment
variables.');
throw new InternalServerErrorException('AWS S3 configuration is
incomplete.');
}

this.s3Client = new S3Client({
region: awsRegion,
credentials: {
accessKeyId: awsAccessKeyId,
secretAccessKey: awsSecretAccessKey,
},
});
}
/**
* @method uploadImageToS3
* @description Uploads an image file to AWS S3.
* @param {Buffer} fileBuffer - The buffer of the image file.
* @param {string} fileName - The desired file name in S3.
* @param {string} mimetype - The MIME type of the file.
* @returns {Promise<string>} The S3 URL of the uploaded image.
* @throws {InternalServerErrorException} If the S3 upload fails.
*/
async uploadImageToS3(fileBuffer: Buffer, fileName: string, mimetype: string):
Promise<string> {
const uploadParams = {
Bucket: this.S3_BUCKET_NAME,
Key: `homework-submissions/${fileName}`,
Body: fileBuffer,
ContentType: mimetype,
ACL: 'private', // Keep files private by default, access via signed URLs or
backend
};
try {
const command = new PutObjectCommand(uploadParams);
await this.s3Client.send(command);
const s3Url =
`https://${this.S3_BUCKET_NAME}.s3.${this.configService.get<string>
('AWS_REGION')}.amazonaws.com/${uploadParams.Key}`;
this.logger.log(`Image uploaded to S3: ${s3Url}`);
return s3Url;
} catch (error) {
this.logger.error(`Failed to upload image to S3: ${error.message}`,
error.stack);
throw new InternalServerErrorException('Failed to upload homework image to
storage.');
}
}
/**
* @method processHomework
* @description Initiates asynchronous processing of a homework submission.

*

Uploads the image to S3, creates a Homework record, and

triggers AI processing.
* @param {string} userId - The ID of the user submitting the homework.
* @param {Buffer} imageBuffer - The buffer of the homework image file.
* @param {string} imageFileName - The original file name of the image.
* @param {string} imageMimeType - The MIME type of the image.
* @returns {Promise<{ homeworkId: string, status: HomeworkStatus }>} The ID
and initial status of the created homework record.
* @throws {InternalServerErrorException} If S3 upload or database record
creation fails.
*/
async processHomework(
userId: string,
imageBuffer: Buffer,
imageFileName: string,
imageMimeType: string,
): Promise<{ homeworkId: string, status: HomeworkStatus }> {
this.logger.log(`Initiating homework processing for user: ${userId}`);
// 1. Upload image to S3
const s3Key = `${Date.now()}-${imageFileName}`;
const imageUrl = await this.uploadImageToS3(imageBuffer, s3Key,
imageMimeType);
// 2. Create initial Homework record in DB with PENDING status
const homeworkRecord = await this.prisma.homeworkSubmission.create({
data: {
userId: userId,
imageUrl: imageUrl,
status: HomeworkStatus.PENDING,
originalFileName: imageFileName,
mimeType: imageMimeType,
},
});
this.logger.log(`Homework record created with ID: ${homeworkRecord.id}.
Status: ${homeworkRecord.status}`);
// 3. Asynchronously trigger AI processing (without awaiting it)
this.processHomeworkWithAI(homeworkRecord.id, imageUrl)
.catch(error => this.logger.error(`Asynchronous AI processing failed for
homework ${homeworkRecord.id}: ${error.message}`, error.stack));
return { homeworkId: homeworkRecord.id, status: homeworkRecord.status };
}
/**
* @private
* @method processHomeworkWithAI

* @description Internal method to handle the AI processing of homework. This
runs asynchronously.
* @param {string} homeworkId - The ID of the homework submission record.
* @param {string} imageUrl - The S3 URL of the homework image.
* @throws {InternalServerErrorException} If AI processing or database update
fails.
*/
private async processHomeworkWithAI(homeworkId: string, imageUrl: string):
Promise<void> {
this.logger.log(`Starting AI processing for homework ID: ${homeworkId}`);
let parsedResult: ParsedHomeworkResult | null = null;
try {
// Update status to PROCESSING
await this.prisma.homeworkSubmission.update({
where: { id: homeworkId },
data: { status: HomeworkStatus.PROCESSING },
});
// Call GPT-4o Vision API
const chatCompletion = await this.openai.chat.completions.create({
model: 'gpt-4o-mini', // GPT-4o-mini also supports vision, but GPT-4o is
better for complex vision tasks
messages: [
{
role: 'system',
content: this.getHomeworkSystemPrompt(),
},
{
role: 'user',
content: [

{ type: 'text', text: '‫حلل هذه الصورة لواجب منزلي واستخرج المعلومات‬

‫ المطلوبة بصيغة‬JSON.' },

{ type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: imageUrl, detail: 'high' }
},
],
},
],
max_tokens: 1500,
response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, // Request JSON output
});
const aiResponseContent = chatCompletion.choices[0]?.message?.content;
if (!aiResponseContent) {
this.logger.warn(`GPT-4o Vision returned an empty response for homework
${homeworkId}.`);
throw new InternalServerErrorException('AI processing returned an empty
response.');

}
this.logger.log(`Raw AI response for homework ${homeworkId}:
${aiResponseContent.substring(0, 200)}...`);
// Validate and clean JSON output
parsedResult = this.validateAndCleanJson(aiResponseContent);
// Update homework record with parsed data and COMPLETED status
await this.prisma.homeworkSubmission.update({
where: { id: homeworkId },
data: {
status: HomeworkStatus.COMPLETED,
parsedData: parsedResult, // Store the structured JSON data
processingLog: 'Successfully processed by AI.',
},
});
this.logger.log(`Homework ${homeworkId} successfully processed and
updated.`);
} catch (error: any) {
this.logger.error(`AI processing failed for homework ${homeworkId}:
${error.message}`, error.stack);
// Update status to FAILED
await this.prisma.homeworkSubmission.update({
where: { id: homeworkId },
data: {
status: HomeworkStatus.FAILED,
processingLog: `AI processing failed: ${error.message.substring(0,
500)}`,
},
});
if (error instanceof OpenAI.APIError) {
this.logger.error(`OpenAI API Error Details for homework ${homeworkId}:
Status ${error.status}, Code ${error.code}, Type ${error.type}`);
}
// Re-throw to ensure the catch block in processHomework catches it for
logging
throw error;
}
}
