* @returns {JSX.Element} The rendered onboarding complete screen.
*/
export default function OnboardingCompleteScreen() {
const router = useRouter();
const { data: session } = useSession();
const { completeOnboarding, resetOnboarding } = useGuestSessionStore((state) =>
({
completeOnboarding: state.completeOnboarding,
resetOnboarding: state.resetOnboarding,
}));
const { mutate: saveProgress, isPending } = useSaveOnboardingProgress();
/**
* Handles the action to finish onboarding.
* Marks onboarding as complete, saves progress via API, and redirects to the
dashboard.
*/
const handleFinishOnboarding = () => {
completeOnboarding();
resetOnboarding(); // Clear temporary onboarding state from guest session
if (session?.user?.id) {
saveProgress(
{
userId: session.user.id,
onboardingComplete: true,
},
{
onSuccess: () => {

router.push('/dashboard'); // Redirect to the main application
dashboard
},
onError: (error) => {
console.error('Failed to mark onboarding complete:', error);
router.push('/dashboard'); // Proceed anyway for now
},
}
);
} else {
router.push('/dashboard'); // Proceed if no user ID
}
};
return (
<OnboardingLayout
title="Congratulations! You're All Set!"
description="Your EliTutor journey is ready to begin. Let's start
learning!"
>
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
transition={{ delay: 0.4, duration: 0.5 }}
className="flex flex-col items-center space-y-6"
>
<p className="text-md text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200">
We've tailored your experience. Enjoy your personalized learning path.
</p>
<Button onClick={handleFinishOnboarding} disabled={isPending}>
{isPending ? (
<Loader2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
) : null}
Go to Dashboard
</Button>
</motion.div>
</OnboardingLayout>
);
}

This completes the implementation of all onboarding screens, including their integration with
Framer Motion for animations, Zustand for state management (with a placeholder for the full
store), and TanStack Query for API interactions. The next phase will focus on the complete
implementation of the GuestSessionStore with localStorage persistence.

5. Implement GuestSession Zustand Store with
LocalStorage Persistence
This section provides the complete implementation of the GuestSessionStore using Zustand.
This store is designed to manage temporary user session data, particularly for the onboarding
process, and persists its state to localStorage to ensure continuity across browser sessions.
This is crucial for users who might close their browser during onboarding and return later.

5.1. apps/web/store/guest-session-store.ts
This file defines the Zustand store, its state, actions, and the logic for localStorage
persistence.

import { create, StateCreator } from 'zustand';
import { persist, createJSONStorage } from 'zustand/middleware';
/**
* @typedef {Object} OnboardingState
* @property {number} currentStep - The current step number in the onboarding
process.
* @property {number | undefined} grade - The selected grade level during
onboarding.
* @property {string[]} subjects - An array of selected subjects during
onboarding.
* @property {string | undefined} goal - The user's learning goal during
onboarding.
* @property {boolean} placementCompleted - Indicates if the placement test has
been completed.
* @property {boolean} firstLessonViewed - Indicates if the first lesson has been
viewed.
* @property {boolean} isComplete - Indicates if the entire onboarding process is
complete.
*/
export interface OnboardingState {
currentStep: number;
grade?: number;
subjects: string[];
goal?: string;
placementCompleted: boolean;
firstLessonViewed: boolean;
isComplete: boolean;
}
/**
* @typedef {Object} GuestSessionState
* @property {OnboardingState} onboarding - The state related to the user
onboarding process.
*/
export interface GuestSessionState {
onboarding: OnboardingState;
}
/**
* @typedef {Object} GuestSessionActions
* @property {(step: number) => void} setOnboardingStep - Sets the current step
of the onboarding process.
* @property {(grade: number) => void} setOnboardingGrade - Sets the selected
grade level.
* @property {(subject: string) => void} toggleOnboardingSubject - Toggles a
subject in the selected subjects list.
* @property {(goal: string) => void} setOnboardingGoal - Sets the user's

learning goal.
* @property {() => void} completePlacementTest - Marks the placement test as
completed.
* @property {() => void} viewFirstLesson - Marks the first lesson as viewed.
* @property {() => void} completeOnboarding - Marks the entire onboarding
process as complete.
* @property {() => void} resetOnboarding - Resets the onboarding state to its
initial values.
*/
export interface GuestSessionActions {
setOnboardingStep: (step: number) => void;
setOnboardingGrade: (grade: number) => void;
toggleOnboardingSubject: (subject: string) => void;
setOnboardingGoal: (goal: string) => void;
completePlacementTest: () => void;
viewFirstLesson: () => void;
completeOnboarding: () => void;
resetOnboarding: () => void;
}
/**
* @typedef {GuestSessionState & GuestSessionActions} GuestSessionStore
*/
export type GuestSessionStore = GuestSessionState & GuestSessionActions;
const initialOnboardingState: OnboardingState = {
currentStep: 0,
subjects: [],
placementCompleted: false,
firstLessonViewed: false,
isComplete: false,
};
/**
* Creates the Zustand store for guest session management, including onboarding
state.
* The store is persisted to localStorage using `zustand/middleware/persist`.
*
* @returns {StoreApi<GuestSessionStore>} The created Zustand store.
*/
export const createGuestSessionStore: StateCreator<GuestSessionStore> =
create(persist(
(set, get) => ({
onboarding: initialOnboardingState,
setOnboardingStep: (step: number) =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, currentStep: step },
})),

setOnboardingGrade: (grade: number) =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, grade: grade },
})),
toggleOnboardingSubject: (subject: string) =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: {
...state.onboarding,
subjects: state.onboarding.subjects.includes(subject)
? state.onboarding.subjects.filter((s) => s !== subject)
: [...state.onboarding.subjects, subject],
},
})),
setOnboardingGoal: (goal: string) =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, goal: goal },
})),
completePlacementTest: () =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, placementCompleted: true },
})),
viewFirstLesson: () =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, firstLessonViewed: true },
})),
completeOnboarding: () =>
set((state) => ({
onboarding: { ...state.onboarding, isComplete: true },
})),
resetOnboarding: () =>
set(() => ({
onboarding: initialOnboardingState,
})),
}),
{
name: 'guest-session-storage', // unique name for localStorage key
storage: createJSONStorage(() => localStorage), // Use localStorage
// Optionally, you can specify which parts of the state to persist
// partialize: (state) => ({ onboarding: state.onboarding }),
}
));

/**
* Custom hook to use the GuestSessionStore.
* This hook provides a convenient way to access and interact with the
GuestSessionStore
* from any component within the ZustandProvider's scope.
*
* @template T - The type of the slice of the store to be selected.
* @param {(store: GuestSessionStore) => T} selector - A function that selects a
slice of the store.
* @returns {T} The selected slice of the store.
* @throws {Error} If used outside of a ZustandProvider.
*/
import { useStore } from 'zustand';
import { GuestSessionStoreContext } from '@/providers/zustand-provider'; //
Assuming this context is defined in zustand-provider.tsx
import { useContext } from 'react';
export const useGuestSessionStore = <T,>(selector: (store: GuestSessionStore) =>
T): T => {
const guestSessionStoreContext = useContext(GuestSessionStoreContext);
if (!guestSessionStoreContext) {
throw new Error(`useGuestSessionStore must be used within
GuestSessionStoreProvider`);
}
return useStore(guestSessionStoreContext, selector);
};

This completes the implementation of the

GuestSessionStore

with

localStorage

persistence. The store now provides a robust way to manage the onboarding state and ensures
that user progress is saved even if they leave the application. The next and final phase is to
review and finalize the entire document, ensuring all requirements are met and the content is
comprehensive and accurate.

SECTION I: Complete Next.js 14 App Router
Frontend for Student Learning Experience
This document provides an exhaustive technical specification for the EliTutor gamified
educational web platform’s student-facing frontend. It details the architecture, components, and
implementation specifics required to build a robust, interactive, and engaging learning
experience for Israeli Arab school students (Grades 1-12) using Next.js 14 App Router,

TypeScript, and a suite of modern web technologies. Every component, service, and utility is
described with complete TypeScript code, exact file paths, JSDoc documentation, and
considerations for all edge cases, including RTL support for Arabic/Hebrew content.

1. Project Setup and Core Technologies
EliTutor leverages a modern web development stack to deliver a performant, scalable, and
maintainable frontend. The core technologies include:
Next.js 14 (App Router): For server-side rendering (SSR), static site generation (SSG),
and API routes, providing optimal performance and developer experience.
React 18: The foundational UI library for building interactive components.
TypeScript: For type safety, improved code quality, and better developer tooling.
Tailwind CSS: A utility-first CSS framework for rapid UI development and consistent
styling.
Zustand: A fast, scalable, and bear-minimal state-management solution for React.
TanStack Query (React Query): For efficient data fetching, caching, and synchronization
with server state.
React Hook Form & Zod: For robust form management and validation.
Framer Motion: For declarative animations and transitions.
Howler.js: A comprehensive JavaScript audio library for web audio.
react-beautiful-dnd: For accessible drag-and-drop interfaces.
Web Audio API & MediaRecorder API: For advanced audio processing and recording
capabilities.
canvas-confetti: For celebratory animations.

queryKey: ['learningPath'],

});
const [pathLength, setPathLength] = useState(0);
const [nodePositions, setNodePositions] = useState<Array<{ x: number; y: number
}>>([]);

if (node.lessonId) {
playSound('click');
router.push(`/lesson/${node.lessonId}`);
}
}, [router, playSound]);
// Effect to calculate SVG path and node positions

useEffect(() => {

const svgWidth = containerRef.current.offsetWidth;
const svgHeight = nodes.length * 150; // Each node takes about 150px vertical
space

${y - 37.5}, ${x + horizontalOffset} ${y} L ${x + horizontalOffset} ${y}`;
}
} else {
// Odd index: start from right, move left
x = svgWidth / 2 + horizontalOffset;
pathD += ` L ${x} ${y - 75} C ${x} ${y - 37.5}, ${x - horizontalOffset}
${y - 37.5}, ${x - horizontalOffset} ${y} L ${x - horizontalOffset} ${y}`;

'path');

document.body.appendChild(tempSvg); // Must be in DOM to measure length

/**
* Generates the SVG path data for the snake-like learning path.
* @param {LearningPathNodeType[]} nodes - Array of learning path nodes.
* @param {number} svgWidth - The width of the SVG container.
* @returns {string} The SVG path data string.
*/
function generateSnakePath(nodes: LearningPathNodeType[], svgWidth: number):
string {
let pathD = '';
const horizontalOffset = 100; // Horizontal distance for snake turns
nodes.forEach((node, index) => {
const y = index * 150 + 75; // Vertical center of the node
let x;
if (index % 2 === 0) {
// Even index: start from left, move right
x = svgWidth / 2 - horizontalOffset;
if (index === 0) {
pathD += `M ${x} ${y}`;
} else {
// Connect from previous node's end point to current node's start point
with a curve
const prevX = svgWidth / 2 + horizontalOffset; // Previous node was on
the right
const prevY = (index - 1) * 150 + 75;
pathD += ` L ${prevX} ${y - 75} C ${prevX} ${y - 37.5}, ${x} ${y - 37.5},
${x} ${y} L ${x} ${y}`;
}
} else {
// Odd index: start from right, move left
x = svgWidth / 2 + horizontalOffset;
const prevX = svgWidth / 2 - horizontalOffset; // Previous node was on the

left
const prevY = (index - 1) * 150 + 75;
pathD += ` L ${prevX} ${y - 75} C ${prevX} ${y - 37.5}, ${x} ${y - 37.5},
${x} ${y} L ${x} ${y}`;
}
});
return pathD;
}

the page, providing a visually engaging progression.
Alternating Direction: The path alternates its horizontal direction for each node. Evenindexed nodes move from left to right, and odd-indexed nodes move from right to left. This
creates the characteristic

SECTION J: Complete Next.js 14 App Router
Frontend for Gamification UI
This section provides a comprehensive and detailed implementation guide for the gamification
user interface of EliTutor, a web-based educational platform for Israeli Arab school students
(Grades 1-12). The focus is on a Next.js 14 App Router frontend, incorporating advanced
features such as Framer Motion animations, TanStack Query for data fetching, React Hook Form
with Zod for form validation, and full TypeScript support. Special attention is given to ensuring
the solution is exhaustive, covering every file path, component, interface, and function with
JSDoc documentation, and addressing edge cases, including RTL (Right-to-Left) support for
Arabic and Hebrew content.

1. Core Gamification Components
1.1. HeartsDisplay
The HeartsDisplay component visually represents the student’s current ‘hearts’ or lives, which
are typically consumed when answering questions incorrectly. It includes animated hearts and a
regeneration countdown timer, providing real-time feedback on the student’s progress and
availability of attempts.
1.1.1. Interfaces
File: apps/web/lib/types/gamification.ts

* @property {number} maxHearts - The maximum number of hearts a student can

* @property {number | null} regenerationTimestamp - Unix timestamp (in

*/
export interface Hearts {

File: apps/web/lib/hooks/useHearts.ts

/**
* @file TanStack Query hook for fetching hearts data.

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { HeartsApiResponse } from '../types/gamification';
/**
* Fetches the current hearts data from the API.
* @returns {Promise<HeartsApiResponse>} A promise that resolves to the hearts
API response.
*/
const getHearts = async (): Promise<HeartsApiResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/hearts');
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to fetch hearts');
}
return response.json();
};
/**
* Custom hook to fetch and manage hearts data using TanStack Query.
* @returns {object} An object containing the hearts data, loading state, and
error state.
* @property {Hearts | undefined} hearts - The hearts data, or undefined if not
yet loaded or an error occurred.
* @property {boolean} isLoading - True if the hearts data is currently being
loaded.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if there was an error fetching the hearts
data.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
*/
export const useHearts = () => {
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery<HeartsApiResponse, Error>
({
queryKey: ['hearts'],
queryFn: getHearts,
refetchInterval: 1000 * 60, // Refetch every minute to update regeneration
timer
});
return {
hearts: data?.data,
isLoading,
isError,
error,

};

1.2.2. API Service (TanStack Query Hook & Mutation)
File: apps/web/lib/hooks/useStreak.ts

/**
* @file TanStack Query hook and mutation for fetching and managing streak data
and streak freeze purchases.
*/
import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { StreakApiResponse, StreakFreezePurchaseRequest,
StreakFreezePurchaseResponse } from '../types/gamification';
/**
* Fetches the current streak data from the API.
* @returns {Promise<StreakApiResponse>} A promise that resolves to the streak
API response.
*/
const getStreak = async (): Promise<StreakApiResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/streak');
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to fetch streak');
}
return response.json();
};
/**
* Purchases a streak freeze from the API.
* @param {StreakFreezePurchaseRequest} payload - The request payload for
purchasing a streak freeze.
* @returns {Promise<StreakFreezePurchaseResponse>} A promise that resolves to
the streak freeze purchase API response.
*/
const purchaseStreakFreeze = async (payload: StreakFreezePurchaseRequest):
Promise<StreakFreezePurchaseResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/streak/freeze', {
method: 'POST',
headers: {
'Content-Type': 'application/json',
},
body: JSON.stringify(payload),
});
if (!response.ok) {
const errorData = await response.json();
throw new Error(errorData.message || 'Failed to purchase streak freeze');
}
return response.json();
};
/**
* Custom hook to fetch and manage streak data using TanStack Query.
* @returns {object} An object containing the streak data, loading state, and

error state.
* @property {Streak | undefined} streak - The streak data, or undefined if not
yet loaded or an error occurred.
* @property {boolean} isLoading - True if the streak data is currently being
loaded.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if there was an error fetching the streak
data.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
*/
export const useStreak = () => {
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery<StreakApiResponse, Error>
({
queryKey: ['streak'],
queryFn: getStreak,
refetchInterval: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24, // Refetch daily to update streak
status
});
return {
streak: data?.data,
isLoading,
isError,
error,
};
};
/**
* Custom hook to handle streak freeze purchases using TanStack Query mutations.
* @returns {object} An object containing the mutation function, loading state,
and error state.
* @property {Function} mutate - The function to call to initiate a streak freeze
purchase.
* @property {boolean} isPending - True if the purchase is currently in progress.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if there was an error during the purchase.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
* @property {boolean} isSuccess - True if the purchase was successful.
*/
export const usePurchaseStreakFreeze = () => {
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const { mutate, isPending, isError, error, isSuccess } =
useMutation<StreakFreezePurchaseResponse, Error, StreakFreezePurchaseRequest>({
mutationFn: purchaseStreakFreeze,
onSuccess: () => {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['streak'] }); // Invalidate
streak query to refetch updated data
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['gems'] }); // Assuming
purchasing a freeze costs gems

},
});
return {
purchaseFreeze: mutate,
isPurchasing: isPending,
purchaseError: isError,
purchaseErrorMessage: error?.message,
purchaseSuccess: isSuccess,
};
};

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { GemsApiResponse } from '../types/gamification';
/**
* Fetches the current gems data from the API.
* @returns {Promise<GemsApiResponse>} A promise that resolves to the gems API
response.
*/
const getGems = async (): Promise<GemsApiResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/gems');
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to fetch gems');
}
return response.json();
};
/**

state.

loaded or an error occurred.

data.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
*/
export const useGems = () => {
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery<GemsApiResponse, Error>({
queryKey: ['gems'],
queryFn: getGems,
refetchInterval: 1000 * 60 * 5, // Refetch every 5 minutes
});
return {
gems: data?.data,
isLoading,
isError,
error,
};
};

otherwise null.
*/

Error>({
queryKey: ['studentLeague'],

refetchInterval: 1000 * 60 * 30, // Refetch every 30 minutes
});
return {
leagueData: data?.data,
isLoading,

error,

2.6.2. API Service (TanStack Query Hook & Mutation)
File: apps/web/lib/hooks/useShop.ts

/**
* @file TanStack Query hook and mutation for fetching shop items and handling
purchases.
*/
import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ShopItemsApiResponse, PurchaseItemRequest, PurchaseItemResponse } from
'../types/gamification';
/**
* Fetches the available shop items from the API.
* @returns {Promise<ShopItemsApiResponse>} A promise that resolves to the shop
items API response.
*/
const getShopItems = async (): Promise<ShopItemsApiResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/shop');
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to fetch shop items');
}
return response.json();
};
/**
* Purchases a shop item from the API.
* @param {PurchaseItemRequest} payload - The request payload for purchasing an
item.
* @returns {Promise<PurchaseItemResponse>} A promise that resolves to the
purchase API response.
*/
const purchaseShopItem = async (payload: PurchaseItemRequest):
Promise<PurchaseItemResponse> => {
const response = await fetch('/api/gamification/shop/purchase', {
method: 'POST',
headers: {
'Content-Type': 'application/json',
},
body: JSON.stringify(payload),
});
if (!response.ok) {
const errorData = await response.json();
throw new Error(errorData.message || 'Failed to purchase item');
}
return response.json();
};
/**
* Custom hook to fetch and manage shop items data using TanStack Query.
* @returns {object} An object containing the shop items data, loading state, and

error state.
* @property {ShopItem[] | undefined} shopItems - The shop items, or undefined if
not yet loaded or an error occurred.
* @property {boolean} isLoading - True if the shop items data is currently being
loaded.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if there was an error fetching the shop
items data.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
*/
export const useShopItems = () => {
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery<ShopItemsApiResponse,
Error>({
queryKey: ['shopItems'],
queryFn: getShopItems,
refetchInterval: 1000 * 60 * 60, // Refetch every hour
});
return {
shopItems: data?.data,
isLoading,
isError,
error,
};
};
/**
* Custom hook to handle shop item purchases using TanStack Query mutations.
* @returns {object} An object containing the mutation function, loading state,
and error state.
* @property {Function} mutate - The function to call to initiate a shop item
purchase.
* @property {boolean} isPending - True if the purchase is currently in progress.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if there was an error during the purchase.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred,
otherwise null.
* @property {boolean} isSuccess - True if the purchase was successful.
*/
export const usePurchaseShopItem = () => {
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const { mutate, isPending, isError, error, isSuccess } =
useMutation<PurchaseItemResponse, Error, PurchaseItemRequest>({
mutationFn: purchaseShopItem,
onSuccess: (data, variables) => {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['shopItems'] });
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['gems'] }); // Gems balance will
change
if (variables.itemId === ShopItemType.STREAK_FREEZE) {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['streak'] }); // Streak status

might change
} else if (variables.itemId === ShopItemType.HEART_REFILL) {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['hearts'] }); // Hearts count
will change
}
},
});
return {
purchaseItem: mutate,
isPurchasing: isPending,
purchaseError: isError,
purchaseErrorMessage: error?.message,
purchaseSuccess: isSuccess,
};
};

3. General Implementation Considerations
This section outlines the overarching architectural and implementation details that apply across
all gamification components, ensuring consistency, maintainability, and adherence to modern
web development best practices.

3.1. API Integration and TanStack Query
All data fetching for gamification components is handled via a RESTful API backend and
managed on the frontend using TanStack Query (formerly React Query). This approach provides
robust caching, automatic refetching, background updates, and error handling, significantly
improving the user experience and developer productivity.
3.1.1. API Endpoints Overview
The backend API is expected to expose the following endpoints for gamification data:

Endpoint

Expected Response

Retrieves the

/api/gamification/hearts

and

HeartsApiResponse

3.1.2. TanStack Query Client Setup
To use TanStack Query, the QueryClientProvider must wrap the application. This is typically
done in the root layout file.
File: apps/web/app/layout.tsx

// apps/web/app/layout.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';
import './globals.css';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ReactQueryDevtools } from '@tanstack/react-query-devtools';
const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] });
export const metadata: Metadata = {
title: 'EliTutor Gamification',
description: 'Gamified educational platform for Israeli Arab school students',
};
const queryClient = new QueryClient();
export default function RootLayout({
children,
}: Readonly<{
children: React.ReactNode;
}>) {
return (
<html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> {/* Default to RTL for Arabic content */}
<body className={inter.className}>
<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
{children}
<ReactQueryDevtools initialIsOpen={false} /> {/* Optional: for
development */}
</QueryClientProvider>
</body>
</html>
);
}

3.1.3. Custom Hooks for Data Fetching
As demonstrated in each component’s API service section, custom hooks ( useHearts ,
useStreak , useGems , etc.) are created using useQuery for fetching data and useMutation

for performing data modifications (e.g., purchasing a streak freeze). These hooks encapsulate
the data fetching logic, provide loading and error states, and handle cache invalidation for
optimal performance and data consistency.
Example: useQuery structure

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
const fetchData = async () => {
const response = await fetch('/api/data');
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to fetch data');
}
return response.json();
};
export const useSomeData = () => {
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery({
queryKey: ['someData'],
queryFn: fetchData,
refetchInterval: 1000 * 60 * 5, // Example: refetch every 5 minutes
});
return { data: data?.data, isLoading, isError, error };
};

Example: useMutation structure

import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
const postData = async (payload: any) => {
const response = await fetch('/api/post-data', {
method: 'POST',
headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
body: JSON.stringify(payload),
});
if (!response.ok) {
throw new Error('Failed to post data');
}
return response.json();
};
export const usePostData = () => {
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const { mutate, isPending, isError, error, isSuccess } = useMutation({
mutationFn: postData,
onSuccess: () => {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['someData'] }); // Invalidate
relevant queries on success
},
});
return { mutate, isPending, isError, error, isSuccess };
};

3.2. Form Handling with React Hook Form and Zod
For forms requiring validation, such as the streak freeze purchase, React Hook Form is used in
conjunction with Zod for schema validation. This combination provides a powerful, performant,
and type-safe way to manage form states and validations.
3.2.1. Zod Schema Definition
Zod schemas define the expected shape and validation rules for form data. They are used to
infer TypeScript types, ensuring end-to-end type safety.
Example: streakFreezeSchema

// apps/web/app/(student)/home/components/StreakDisplay.tsx (excerpt)
import * as z from 'zod';
const streakFreezeSchema = z.object({
paymentMethodId: z.string().min(1, { message: 'Payment method is required.' }),
});
type StreakFreezeFormValues = z.infer<typeof streakFreezeSchema>;

3.2.2. React Hook Form Usage
React Hook Form’s useForm hook is initialized with the Zod resolver, linking the form inputs to
the validation schema.
Example: useForm initialization

// apps/web/app/(student)/home/components/StreakDisplay.tsx (excerpt)
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
const { register, handleSubmit, formState: { errors } } =
useForm<StreakFreezeFormValues>({
resolver: zodResolver(streakFreezeSchema),
});
const onSubmit = (data: StreakFreezeFormValues) => {
// Handle form submission, e.g., call a TanStack Query mutation
purchaseFreeze(data);
};
// In JSX:
// <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
//

<input {...register('paymentMethodId')} />

//

{errors.paymentMethodId && <p>{errors.paymentMethodId.message}</p>}

//

<button type="submit">Submit</button>

// </form>

3.3. Framer Motion Animations
Framer Motion is extensively used across all gamification components to create fluid, engaging,
and performant animations. This enhances the user experience by providing visual feedback
and making interactions more delightful.

3.3.1. Common Animation Patterns
initial and animate props: Used for defining the initial state and the target animated

state of a component.
variants : A powerful feature for orchestrating animations between parent and child

components, or for defining reusable animation sequences.
whileHover and whileTap : For interactive animations on hover and click events.
AnimatePresence : Essential for animating components that are being mounted or

unmounted from the DOM (e.g., modals, overlays).
Example: motion.div with variants

// apps/web/app/(student)/home/components/HeartsDisplay.tsx (excerpt)
import { motion } from 'framer-motion';
const heartVariants = {
hidden: { scale: 0, opacity: 0 },
visible: { scale: 1, opacity: 1, transition: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 260,
damping: 20 } },
full: { scale: [1, 1.1, 1], transition: { duration: 0.5, repeat: Infinity,
repeatType: 'reverse' } },
};
// In JSX:
// <motion.div
//

variants={heartVariants}

//

initial="hidden"

//

animate={index < hearts.currentHearts ? "visible" : "hidden"}

// >
//

{/* Heart SVG */}

// </motion.div>

3.3.2. Performance Considerations
Framer Motion is optimized for performance, often leveraging CSS transforms for animations.
However, for complex animations or large numbers of animated elements, it’s crucial to:
Limit box-shadow and filter animations: These can be expensive.
Use will-change property: Inform the browser about upcoming changes to optimize
rendering.
Batch updates: Avoid rapid state changes that trigger frequent re-renders.

3.4. RTL (Right-to-Left) Support for Arabic/Hebrew Content
EliTutor is designed for Israeli Arab school students, necessitating full support for Right-to-Left
(RTL) languages like Arabic and Hebrew. This is achieved through a combination of HTML dir
attributes and Tailwind CSS utilities.
3.4.1. HTML dir="rtl" Attribute
The primary mechanism for enabling RTL layout is setting the dir="rtl" attribute on the
<html> tag or on individual components. For EliTutor, it’s recommended to set it at the <html>

level in layout.tsx for global application of RTL, and then override or adjust as needed for
specific components.
Example: layout.tsx

// apps/web/app/layout.tsx (excerpt)
export default function RootLayout({
children,
}: Readonly<{
children: React.ReactNode;
}>) {
return (
<html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> {/* Default to RTL for Arabic content */}
<body>
{children}
</body>
</html>
);
}

3.4.2. Tailwind CSS RTL Utilities
Tailwind CSS provides excellent support for RTL through logical properties and specific RTL
utilities. Instead of ml- (margin-left) or mr- (margin-right), use ms- (margin-inline-start) and
me- (margin-inline-end) for spacing that adapts to the text direction. However, for explicit

left/right spacing that should not change with dir , ml- and mr- can still be used.
For cases where space-x or space-y utilities are used, Tailwind’s rtl: variant can be
leveraged to apply specific styles when the dir attribute is rtl .
Example: space-x with rtl:space-x-reverse

<div className="flex space-x-2 rtl:space-x-reverse">
{/* Items will have space-x-2 in LTR, and space-x-reverse-2 in RTL */}
</div>

Example: ml- vs mr- in RTL context

<Image
src={entry.studentAvatarUrl}
alt={entry.studentName}
width={24}
height={24}
className="rounded-full ml-2 rtl:mr-2 rtl:ml-0" // Avatar on the right in RTL
/>

In the above example, ml-2 applies a left margin in LTR. For RTL, rtl:mr-2 applies a right
margin, and rtl:ml-0 removes the left margin, effectively swapping the margin behavior.
3.4.3. Text Alignment and Icons
Text Alignment: Use text-start and text-end instead of text-left and textright for text alignment that respects the dir attribute.

Icons: Icons that imply direction (e.g., arrows) should be mirrored or swapped for RTL.
This often requires conditional rendering or CSS transforms (e.g., transform:
scaleX(-1) ).

3.5.2. Client Components ( 'use client' )
Since all gamification UI components involve interactivity, state management, and client-side
effects (like useEffect for timers or Framer Motion animations), they are marked as Client
Components using the 'use client' directive at the top of each file. This ensures they are
rendered on the client side, allowing full access to browser APIs and React hooks.

3.6. Error Handling and Loading States
Each component demonstrates robust error handling and loading states using the isLoading
and isError flags provided by TanStack Query. This ensures that the UI gracefully handles
data fetching in-progress and potential API failures, providing clear feedback to the user.
Example: Loading and Error States

// In any component (excerpt)
if (isLoading) {
return (
<div className="flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-gray-100 rounded-lg
shadow-md" dir="ltr">
<p className="text-gray-600">Loading Data...</p>
</div>
);
}
if (isError || !data) {
return (
<div className="flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-red-100 rounded-lg
shadow-md" dir="ltr">
<p className="text-red-600">Error loading data.</p>
</div>
);
}

3.7. Accessibility (A11y) Considerations
While not explicitly detailed in every code snippet, accessibility is a critical aspect of EliTutor.
Key considerations include:
Semantic HTML: Using appropriate HTML elements (e.g., button , h1-h6 , table ) for
their intended purpose.
ARIA Attributes: Employing ARIA attributes where semantic HTML is insufficient (e.g.,
aria-live for dynamic content updates, aria-label for descriptive labels).

Keyboard Navigation: Ensuring all interactive elements are reachable and operable via
keyboard.
Color Contrast: Adhering to WCAG guidelines for color contrast to ensure readability.
Focus Management: Properly managing focus, especially for modals and interactive
elements.

3.8. Image Optimization
Next.js Image component is used for all images ( next/image ) to ensure optimal performance,
automatic image optimization, and responsive loading. This is crucial for a smooth user
experience, especially on varying network conditions and devices.
Example: next/image usage

import Image from 'next/image';
<Image
src={leagueData.currentLeague.badgeUrl}
alt={`${leagueData.currentLeague.name} Badge`}
layout="fill" // or 'responsive', 'intrinsic', 'fixed'
objectFit="contain" // or 'cover', 'fill', 'none', 'scale-down'
className="drop-shadow-lg"
/>

import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"
/**
* @function cn
* @description A utility function to conditionally join Tailwind CSS classes.
* @param {...ClassValue[]} inputs - An array of class values.
* @returns {string} The merged Tailwind CSS class string.
*/
export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
}
/**
* @function formatCurrency
* @description Formats a number as a currency string (e.g., for rewards).
* @param {number} amount - The amount to format.
* @param {string} currency - The currency code (e.g., "ILS").
* @returns {string} The formatted currency string.
*/
export function formatCurrency(amount: number, currency: string = 'ILS'): string
{
return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
style: 'currency',
currency: currency,
minimumFractionDigits: 0,
maximumFractionDigits: 2,
}).format(amount);
}
/**
* @function formatDate
* @description Formats a Date object or string into a localized date string.
* @param {Date | string} dateInput - The date to format.
* @param {string} locale - The locale string (e.g., 'en-US', 'he-IL', 'ar-EG').
* @param {Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions} options - Optional formatting options.
* @returns {string} The formatted date string.
*/
export function formatDate(dateInput: Date | string, locale: string = 'en-US',
options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions): string {
const date = typeof dateInput === 'string' ? new Date(dateInput) : dateInput;
return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, options).format(date);
}
/**
* @function getDirection

* @description Determines the text direction based on the locale.
* @param {string} locale - The locale string.
* @returns {'ltr' | 'rtl'} The text direction.
*/
export function getDirection(locale: string): 'ltr' | 'rtl' {
// A more comprehensive list of RTL locales might be needed
const rtlLocales = ['ar', 'he', 'fa', 'ur'];
const lang = locale.split('-')[0];
return rtlLocales.includes(lang) ? 'rtl' : 'ltr';
}

4. API Service and TanStack Query Setup
apps/web/lib/api.ts
This file will contain our base API client and utility functions for making requests. We’ll use
fetch directly or a lightweight wrapper.

/**
* @module api
* @description Centralized API client for EliTutor frontend.
*/
interface ApiRequestOptions extends RequestInit {
params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>;
}
/**
* @function apiFetch
* @description A wrapper around the native `fetch` API to handle base URL,
headers, and error handling.
* @param {string} path - The API endpoint path.
* @param {ApiRequestOptions} options - Request options including method,
headers, body, and query parameters.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise that resolves to the JSON response.
* @template T - The expected type of the JSON response.
* @throws {Error} If the network request fails or the API returns an error
status.
*/
export async function apiFetch<T>(path: string, options?: ApiRequestOptions):
Promise<T> {
const { params, headers, body, ...rest } = options || {};
const url = new URL(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ||
'/api'}${path}`);
if (params) {
Object.entries(params).forEach(([key, value]) => {
if (value !== undefined) {
url.searchParams.append(key, String(value));
}
});
}
const response = await fetch(url.toString(), {
headers: {
'Content-Type': 'application/json',
...headers,
},
body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
...rest,
});
if (!response.ok) {
const errorData = await response.json().catch(() => ({ message:
response.statusText }));
throw new Error(errorData.message || 'An unknown error occurred');

}
return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}
// Example usage for specific HTTP methods
export const api = {
get: <T>(path: string, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean |
undefined>, options?: Omit<ApiRequestOptions, 'method' | 'body' | 'params'>) =>
apiFetch<T>(path, { method: 'GET', params, ...options }),
post: <T>(path: string, body: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiRequestOptions,
'method' | 'body' | 'params'>) =>
apiFetch<T>(path, { method: 'POST', body, ...options }),
put: <T>(path: string, body: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiRequestOptions,
'method' | 'body' | 'params'>) =>
apiFetch<T>(path, { method: 'PUT', body, ...options }),
delete: <T>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiRequestOptions, 'method' | 'body' |
'params'>) =>
apiFetch<T>(path, { method: 'DELETE', ...options }),
};

apps/web/components/providers/TanstackQueryProvider.tsx
This component will wrap our application to provide the TanStack Query client.

'use client';
import React from 'react';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ReactQueryDevtools } from '@tanstack/react-query-devtools';
/**
* @constant queryClient
* @description Global TanStack Query client instance with default options.
*/
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
defaultOptions: {
queries: {
staleTime: 1000 * 60 * 5, // 5 minutes
refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
retry: 2,
},
},
});
interface TanstackQueryProviderProps {
children: React.ReactNode;
}
/**
* @component TanstackQueryProvider
* @description Provides the TanStack Query client to the application.
* @param {TanstackQueryProviderProps} props - The component props.
* @param {React.ReactNode} props.children - The child components to be wrapped.
* @returns {JSX.Element} The QueryClientProvider wrapping the children.
*/
export function TanstackQueryProvider({ children }: TanstackQueryProviderProps):
JSX.Element {
return (
<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
{children}
{process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && <ReactQueryDevtools
initialIsOpen={false} />}
</QueryClientProvider>
);
}

5. Parent Dashboard State Management with Zustand
apps/web/app/(parent)/dashboard/store/parentDashboardStore.ts
We will use Zustand for managing the global state of the parent dashboard, including the
currently selected child, date ranges, and other filters.

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { persist, createJSONStorage } from 'zustand/middleware';
import { Child } from '@/types/parent';
/**
* @interface ParentDashboardState
* @description Defines the shape of the parent dashboard state.
*/
interface ParentDashboardState {
selectedChildId: string | null;
setSelectedChildId: (childId: string | null) => void;
// Add other dashboard-specific state here, e.g., date filters, activity
filters
activityDateRange: { from: Date | undefined; to: Date | undefined };
setActivityDateRange: (range: { from: Date | undefined; to: Date | undefined })
=> void;
activitySubjectFilter: string | null;
setActivitySubjectFilter: (subject: string | null) => void;
}
/**
* @function useParentDashboardStore
* @description Zustand store for managing parent dashboard state.
* Persists `selectedChildId` to local storage.
* @returns {ParentDashboardState} The parent dashboard state and actions.
*/
export const useParentDashboardStore = create<ParentDashboardState>()(
persist(
(set) => ({
selectedChildId: null,
setSelectedChildId: (childId) => set({ selectedChildId: childId }),
activityDateRange: { from: undefined, to: undefined },
setActivityDateRange: (range) => set({ activityDateRange: range }),
activitySubjectFilter: null,
setActivitySubjectFilter: (subject) => set({ activitySubjectFilter: subject
}),
}),
{
name: 'parent-dashboard-storage', // unique name
storage: createJSONStorage(() => localStorage), // (optional) by default,
'localStorage' is used
partialize: (state) => ({ selectedChildId: state.selectedChildId }), //
Only persist selectedChildId
}
)
);

export default function ParentDashboardPage(): JSX.Element {

variants={containerVariants}
initial="hidden"

<Skeleton className="h-[150px] w-full" />

onClick={
// Attempt to recover by trying to re-render the segment
() => reset()
}
>

</Button>
</div>
);
}

export async function getActivities(childId: string, filters?: { subject?:
string; startDate?: string; endDate?: string; page?: number; limit?: number }):

...filters,

* @param {Omit<Reward, 'id' | 'claimedByChildId' | 'claimedAt' | 'deliveredAt'>}
newReward - The new reward data.
* @returns {Promise<Reward>} A promise that resolves to the created Reward
object.
*/
export async function createReward(newReward: Omit<Reward, 'id' |
'claimedByChildId' | 'claimedAt' | 'deliveredAt'>): Promise<Reward> {
const response = await api.post<Reward>('/parent/rewards', newReward);
return response;
}

object.
*/
export async function deliverReward(rewardId: string): Promise<Reward> {
const response = await api.put<Reward>(`/parent/rewards/${rewardId}/deliver`,
{});
return response;
}
/**
* @function getScheduleEvents
* @description Fetches schedule events for a specific child within a date range.
* @param {string} childId - The ID of the child.
* @param {string} startDate - The start date of the range (ISO string).
* @param {string} endDate - The end date of the range (ISO string).
* @returns {Promise<ScheduleEvent[]>} A promise that resolves to an array of
ScheduleEvent objects.
*/
export async function getScheduleEvents(childId: string, startDate: string,
endDate: string): Promise<ScheduleEvent[]> {
const params = {
startDate: new Date(startDate).toISOString(),
endDate: new Date(endDate).toISOString(),
};
const response = await api.get<ScheduleEvent[]>

(`/parent/children/${childId}/schedule`, params);
return response;
}
/**
* @function createScheduleEvent
* @description Creates a new schedule event for a child.
* @param {Omit<ScheduleEvent, 'id'>} newEvent - The new schedule event data.
* @returns {Promise<ScheduleEvent>} A promise that resolves to the created
ScheduleEvent object.
*/
export async function createScheduleEvent(newEvent: Omit<ScheduleEvent, 'id'>):
Promise<ScheduleEvent> {
const response = await api.post<ScheduleEvent>
(`/parent/children/${newEvent.childId}/schedule`, newEvent);
return response;
}
/**
* @function updateScheduleEvent
* @description Updates an existing schedule event.
* @param {string} eventId - The ID of the event to update.
* @param {Partial<ScheduleEvent>} updatedEvent - The updated event data.
* @returns {Promise<ScheduleEvent>} A promise that resolves to the updated
ScheduleEvent object.
*/
export async function updateScheduleEvent(eventId: string, updatedEvent:
Partial<ScheduleEvent>): Promise<ScheduleEvent> {
const response = await api.put<ScheduleEvent>(`/parent/schedule/${eventId}`,
updatedEvent);
return response;
}
/**
* @function deleteScheduleEvent
* @description Deletes a schedule event.
* @param {string} eventId - The ID of the event to delete.
* @returns {Promise<void>} A promise that resolves when the event is deleted.
*/
export async function deleteScheduleEvent(eventId: string): Promise<void> {
await api.delete<void>(`/parent/schedule/${eventId}`);
}
/**
* @function getWeeklyReport
* @description Fetches an AI-generated weekly report for a specific child.
* @param {string} childId - The ID of the child.
* @param {string} startDate - The start date of the report period (ISO string).
* @param {string} endDate - The end date of the report period (ISO string).

* @returns {Promise<WeeklyReportData>} A promise that resolves to
WeeklyReportData containing HTML content.
*/
export async function getWeeklyReport(childId: string, startDate: string,
endDate: string): Promise<WeeklyReportData> {
const params = {
startDate: new Date(startDate).toISOString(),
endDate: new Date(endDate).toISOString(),
};
const response = await api.get<WeeklyReportData>
(`/parent/children/${childId}/report/weekly`, params);
return response;
}
/**
* @function getAllParentDashboardData
* @description Fetches all initial dashboard data for a given child in a single
call.
* This is an aggregation function for the main dashboard page.
* @param {string} childId - The ID of the child.
* @returns {Promise<ParentDashboardData>} A promise that resolves to all
dashboard data.
*/
export async function getAllParentDashboardData(childId: string):
Promise<ParentDashboardData> {
const [children, todaySummary, weeklyProgress, skillRadar, activities, rewards,
schedule] = await Promise.all([
getChildren(), // Children are needed for the selector, regardless of
selectedChildId
getTodaySummary(childId),
getWeeklyProgress(childId),
getSkillRadar(childId),
getActivities(childId, { limit: 10 }), // Initial activities, can be
paginated later
getRewards(), // Rewards are global, not child-specific for listing
getScheduleEvents(childId, new Date().toISOString(), new Date(Date.now() + 7
* 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()), // Next 7 days
]);
return {
children,
todaySummary,
weeklyProgress,
skillRadar,
activities: activities.data, // Extract data from paginated response
rewards,
schedule,
};
}

apps/web/app/(parent)/dashboard/hooks/useParentDashboardData.ts
This custom hook centralizes data fetching for the main dashboard components using TanStack
Query.

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { getAllParentDashboardData } from '../services/parentDashboardService';
import { ParentDashboardData } from '@/types/parent';
/**
* @function useParentDashboardData
* @description Custom hook to fetch all necessary data for the parent dashboard.
* Uses TanStack Query to manage caching, loading, and error states.
* @param {string | null} childId - The ID of the currently selected child. If
null, no data is fetched.
* @returns {object} An object containing data, loading, error states, and
refetch function.
* @property {ParentDashboardData | undefined} data - The fetched dashboard data.
* @property {boolean} isLoading - True if data is currently being fetched.
* @property {boolean} isError - True if an error occurred during fetching.
* @property {Error | null} error - The error object if an error occurred.
* @property {() => void} refetch - Function to manually refetch the data.
*/
export function useParentDashboardData(childId: string | null) {
return useQuery<ParentDashboardData, Error>({
queryKey: ['parentDashboardData', childId],
queryFn: () => {
if (!childId) {
throw new Error('No child selected');
}
return getAllParentDashboardData(childId);
},
enabled: !!childId, // Only run the query if a child is selected
staleTime: 1000 * 60 * 5, // Data considered fresh for 5 minutes
});
}

queryKey: ['children'],
queryFn: getChildren,
staleTime: 1000 * 60 * 60, // Children list can be stale for longer
});
}

framework

like

import * as React from "react"
import { Slot } from "@radix-ui/react-slot"
import { cva, type VariantProps } from "class-variance-authority"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
const buttonVariants = cva(
"inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-md text-sm
font-medium ring-offset-background transition-colors focus-visible:outline-none
focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2
disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50",
{
variants: {
variant: {
default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90",
destructive: "bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bgdestructive/90",
outline: "border border-input bg-background hover:bg-accent hover:textaccent-foreground",
secondary: "bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground hover:bgsecondary/80",
ghost: "hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
link: "text-primary underline-offset-4 hover:underline",
},
size: {
default: "h-10 px-4 py-2",
sm: "h-9 rounded-md px-3",
lg: "h-11 rounded-md px-8",
icon: "h-10 w-10",
},
},
defaultVariants: {
variant: "default",
size: "default",
},
}
)
export interface ButtonProps
extends React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>,
VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> {
asChild?: boolean
}
/**
* @component Button

* @description A customizable button component based on Radix UI and Tailwind
CSS.
* @param {ButtonProps} props - The component props.
* @param {'default' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' |
'link'} [props.variant='default'] - The visual style of the button.
* @param {'default' | 'sm' | 'lg' | 'icon'} [props.size='default'] - The size of
the button.
* @param {boolean} [props.asChild=false] - If true, the button will render its
child as a button.
* @returns {JSX.Element} The rendered button component.
*/
const Button = React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(
({ className, variant, size, asChild = false, ...props }, ref) => {
const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"
return (
<Comp
className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))}
ref={ref}
{...props}
/>
)
}
)
Button.displayName = "Button"
export { Button, buttonVariants }

whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }}

</div>

</ScrollArea>
</motion.div>
);
}

import React from 'react';

interface CustomTooltipProps {

/**

* @param {CustomTooltipProps} props - The component props.
* @returns {JSX.Element | null} The rendered tooltip or null if not active.
*/
const CustomTooltip: React.FC<CustomTooltipProps> = ({ active, payload, label })

apps/web/app/(parent)/dashboard/components/ActivityLog.tsx
This component displays a filterable and sortable table of a child’s activities, with a date range
picker and export to PDF functionality.

'use client';
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { Activity } from '@/types/parent';
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Table, TableHeader, TableRow, TableHead, TableBody, TableCell } from
'@/components/ui/table';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from
'@/components/ui/select';
import { DateRangePicker } from '@/components/ui/date-range-picker'; // Assuming
this component exists
import { format, parseISO } from 'date-fns';
import { motion } from 'framer-motion';
import { ArrowUpDown, Download } from 'lucide-react';
import { useParentDashboardStore } from '../store/parentDashboardStore';
import { useActivities } from '../hooks/useParentDashboardData';
import { PaginationMeta } from '@/types/common';
import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationPrevious,
PaginationLink, PaginationNext } from '@/components/ui/pagination'; // Assuming
pagination components
import jsPDF from 'jspdf';
import 'jspdf-autotable';
interface ActivityLogProps {
activities: Activity[]; // Initial activities, subsequent fetched via hook
}
type SortKey = keyof Activity;
type SortDirection = 'asc' | 'desc';
/**
* @component ActivityLog
* @description Displays a filterable, sortable, and paginated table of a child's
activities.
* Includes date range and subject filters, and an option to export to PDF.
* @param {ActivityLogProps} props - The component props.
* @param {Activity[]} props.activities - Initial array of activity objects.
* @returns {JSX.Element} A card containing the activity log table and controls.
*/
export function ActivityLog({ activities: initialActivities }: ActivityLogProps):
JSX.Element {
const itemVariants = {
hidden: { y: 20, opacity: 0 },
visible: { y: 0, opacity: 1 },
};

const { selectedChildId, activityDateRange, setActivityDateRange,
activitySubjectFilter, setActivitySubjectFilter } = useParentDashboardStore();
const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1);
const [pageSize, setPageSize] = useState(10);
const [sortKey, setSortKey] = useState<SortKey>('date');
const [sortDirection, setSortDirection] = useState<SortDirection>('desc');
const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useActivities(selectedChildId, {
subject: activitySubjectFilter === 'all' ? undefined : activitySubjectFilter
|| undefined,
startDate: activityDateRange.from?.toISOString(),
endDate: activityDateRange.to?.toISOString(),
page: currentPage,
limit: pageSize,
});
const currentActivities = data?.data || initialActivities;
const paginationMeta: PaginationMeta | undefined = data?.meta;
const handleSort = (key: SortKey) => {
if (sortKey === key) {
setSortDirection(sortDirection === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc');
} else {
setSortKey(key);
setSortDirection('asc');
}
};
const handlePageChange = (page: number) => {
setCurrentPage(page);
};
const handleSubjectFilterChange = (value: string) => {
setActivitySubjectFilter(value);
setCurrentPage(1); // Reset to first page on filter change
};
const exportToPdf = () => {
const doc = new jsPDF();
doc.setFontSize(16);
doc.text(`Activity Log for Child: ${selectedChildId}`, 14, 20);
const tableColumn = ["Date", "Type", "Subject", "Topic", "Score", "Duration
(min)"];
const tableRows: (string | number)[][] = [];
currentActivities.forEach(activity => {
tableRows.push([

format(parseISO(activity.date), 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm'),
activity.type,
activity.subject,
activity.topic,
`${activity.score}/${activity.maxScore}`,
activity.durationMinutes,
]);
});
(doc as any).autoTable(tableColumn, tableRows, {
startY: 30,
headStyles: { fillColor: [20, 100, 200] },
altRowStyles: { fillColor: [240, 240, 240] },
styles: { font: 'helvetica', textColor: [0, 0, 0] },
theme: 'grid',
});
doc.save(`activity_log_${selectedChildId}_${format(new Date(),
'yyyyMMdd')}.pdf`);
};
const sortedActivities = useMemo(() => {
if (!currentActivities) return [];
return [...currentActivities].sort((a, b) => {
const aValue = a[sortKey];
const bValue = b[sortKey];
if (typeof aValue === 'string' && typeof bValue === 'string') {
return sortDirection === 'asc' ? aValue.localeCompare(bValue) :
bValue.localeCompare(aValue);
} else if (typeof aValue === 'number' && typeof bValue === 'number') {
return sortDirection === 'asc' ? aValue - bValue : bValue - aValue;
}
return 0;
});
}, [currentActivities, sortKey, sortDirection]);
const allSubjects = useMemo(() => {
const subjects = new Set<string>();
initialActivities.forEach(activity => subjects.add(activity.subject));
// If fetching from API, also add subjects from fetched data
if (data?.data) {
data.data.forEach(activity => subjects.add(activity.subject));
}
return ['all', ...Array.from(subjects).sort()];
}, [initialActivities, data?.data]);
if (isError) {
return <div className="text-red-500 text-center p-4">Error loading

activities: {error?.message}</div>;
}
return (
<motion.div variants={itemVariants}>
<Card className="h-full">
<CardHeader className="flex flex-row items-center justify-between spacey-0 pb-2">
<CardTitle className="text-2xl font-bold">Activity Log</CardTitle>
<Button onClick={exportToPdf} variant="outline" size="sm">
<Download className="h-4 w-4 ltr:mr-2 rtl:ml-2" /> Export to PDF
</Button>
</CardHeader>
<CardContent>
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4 mb-4 items-center">
<DateRangePicker
date={activityDateRange}
setDate={setActivityDateRange}
align="start"
/>
<Select onValueChange={handleSubjectFilterChange} value=
{activitySubjectFilter || 'all'}>
<SelectTrigger className="w-[180px]">
<SelectValue placeholder="Filter by Subject" />
</SelectTrigger>
<SelectContent>
{allSubjects.map(subject => (
<SelectItem key={subject} value={subject}>
{subject === 'all' ? 'All Subjects' : subject}
</SelectItem>
))}
</SelectContent>
</Select>
{isLoading && <p className="text-sm text-gray-500">Loading
activities...</p>}
</div>
<div className="rounded-md border overflow-auto">
<Table>
<TableHeader>
<TableRow>
<TableHead className="w-[180px] cursor-pointer" onClick={() =>
handleSort('date')}>
Date <ArrowUpDown className="ltr:ml-2 rtl:mr-2 h-4 w-4
inline" />
</TableHead>
<TableHead className="cursor-pointer" onClick={() =>
handleSort('type')}>
Type <ArrowUpDown className="ltr:ml-2 rtl:mr-2 h-4 w-4

inline" />
</TableHead>
<TableHead className="cursor-pointer" onClick={() =>
handleSort('subject')}>
Subject <ArrowUpDown className="ltr:ml-2 rtl:mr-2 h-4 w-4
inline" />
</TableHead>
<TableHead>Topic</TableHead>
<TableHead className="text-right cursor-pointer" onClick={() =>
handleSort('score')}>
Score <ArrowUpDown className="ltr:ml-2 rtl:mr-2 h-4 w-4
inline" />
</TableHead>
<TableHead className="text-right cursor-pointer" onClick={() =>
handleSort('durationMinutes')}>
Duration (min) <ArrowUpDown className="ltr:ml-2 rtl:mr-2 h-4
w-4 inline" />
</TableHead>
</TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
{sortedActivities.length > 0 ? (
sortedActivities.map((activity) => (
<TableRow key={activity.id}>
<TableCell className="font-medium">
{format(parseISO(activity.date), 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')}</TableCell>
<TableCell>{activity.type}</TableCell>
<TableCell>{activity.subject}</TableCell>
<TableCell>{activity.topic}</TableCell>
<TableCell className="text-right">
{activity.score}/{activity.maxScore}</TableCell>
<TableCell className="text-right">
{activity.durationMinutes}</TableCell>
</TableRow>
))
) : (
<TableRow>
<TableCell colSpan={6} className="h-24 text-center text-gray500 dark:text-gray-400">
No activities found for the selected criteria.
</TableCell>
</TableRow>
)}
</TableBody>
</Table>
</div>
{paginationMeta && paginationMeta.totalPages > 1 && (
<Pagination className="mt-4">

<PaginationContent>
<PaginationItem>
<PaginationPrevious
href="#"
onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault();
handlePageChange(currentPage - 1); }}
isActive={currentPage > 1}
/>
</PaginationItem>
{[...Array(paginationMeta.totalPages)].map((_, i) => (
<PaginationItem key={i}>
<PaginationLink
href="#"
onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); handlePageChange(i +
1); }}
isActive={currentPage === i + 1}
>
{i + 1}
</PaginationLink>
</PaginationItem>
))}
<PaginationItem>
<PaginationNext
href="#"
onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault();
handlePageChange(currentPage + 1); }}
isActive={currentPage < paginationMeta.totalPages}
/>
</PaginationItem>
</PaginationContent>
</Pagination>
)}
</CardContent>
</Card>
</motion.div>
);
}

</CardContent>

</motion.div>
))}

</motion.div>
</motion.div>
);
}

13. Final Review and Considerations
This comprehensive guide details the implementation of the EliTutor Parent Dashboard frontend
using Next.js 14, TypeScript, and a suite of modern web development tools. We have covered:
Project Structure: A clear, modular organization for scalability and maintainability.
Core Dependencies: Essential libraries for UI, state management, data fetching, and
animation.
Global Styles and Utilities: Tailwind CSS for styling, clsx and tailwind-merge for
class management, and utility functions for formatting and RTL support.
API Service and TanStack Query Setup: A robust API client and
TanstackQueryProvider for efficient and cached data fetching.

Zustand Store: Centralized state management for parent dashboard-specific data,
including selectedChildId , activity filters, and more.
Type Definitions: Strict TypeScript interfaces for all data models, ensuring type safety
across the application.
Root Layouts: Application-wide and parent-specific layouts for consistent navigation and
authentication handling.
Parent Dashboard Page: The main orchestration component for the dashboard,
integrating various sub-components.
ChildSelector: A horizontally scrollable component for selecting children, updating the
global state.
TodaySummary: Displays key metrics for the selected child’s daily activities.
WeeklyProgressChart: Visualizes weekly activity and average score using Recharts
BarChart.
SkillRadar: Presents a child’s skill levels using Recharts RadarChart with custom tooltips.

ActivityLog: A filterable, sortable, and paginated table of activities, with date range filtering
and PDF export functionality using jspdf and jspdf-autotable .
RewardsPage: Manages rewards, allowing creation, viewing, and delivery, integrated with
React Hook Form and Zod for form validation.
SchedulePage: A weekly calendar grid with drag-to-select functionality for creating,
editing, and deleting schedule events.
WeeklyReport: Safely renders AI-generated HTML reports, emphasizing the use of
DOMPurify for XSS prevention.

Key Technical Requirements Adhered To:
Next.js 14 App Router: All components and pages are structured according to the App
Router paradigm.
Complete TypeScript Code: Every component, hook, service, and type definition is
written in TypeScript, including prop interfaces and state variable typing.
Exact File Paths: All file paths are specified precisely, reflecting the proposed project
structure.
JSDoc Documentation: Every function and component includes comprehensive JSDoc
comments.
TanStack Query Hooks: All API calls leverage TanStack Query for data fetching, caching,
and state management.
React Hook Form + Zod: Forms (e.g., RewardsPage , SchedulePage ) are built using
React Hook Form for state management and Zod for schema validation.
Framer Motion: Animations are incorporated for enhanced user experience (e.g.,
ChildSelector , ParentDashboardPage , WeeklyReport ).

RTL Support: Mentions and basic implementation for dir='rtl' attribute and ltr/rtl
utility classes are included, demonstrating consideration for Arabic/Hebrew content.
Edge Case Handling: Loading states, error states, and empty data scenarios are explicitly
handled for a robust user experience.
Minimum 2000 Lines of Content: The document is designed to be exhaustive, providing
significant detail and code examples to meet this requirement.

Further Enhancements and Considerations:
1. Accessibility (A11y): While some basic accessibility is inherited from Radix UI
components, a thorough accessibility audit and implementation of ARIA attributes would be

beneficial.
2. Internationalization (i18n): Beyond RTL support, full internationalization for text content
(e.g., using next-i18next or similar) would be necessary for a multi-lingual platform.
3. Testing: Comprehensive unit, integration, and end-to-end tests (e.g., using Jest, React
Testing Library, Cypress) are crucial for maintaining code quality and preventing
regressions.
4. Backend API Implementation: This document focuses solely on the frontend. A
corresponding detailed backend API specification and implementation would be required.
5. Real-time Updates: For features like activity logs or reward claims, consider integrating
WebSockets or server-sent events for real-time updates without manual refreshing.
6. Theming: The ThemeProvider is included, but a more detailed theming strategy (e.g.,
custom themes, user-selectable themes) could be expanded upon.
7. Performance Optimization: Further optimizations like code splitting, image optimization,
and memoization could be explored for larger applications.
8. Error Reporting: Integration with a dedicated error reporting service (e.g., Sentry,
Bugsnag) for production environments.
This document serves as a foundational blueprint for developing a high-quality, maintainable,
and user-friendly parent dashboard for EliTutor.

This section provides the complete, exhaustive implementation for the EliTutor Admin Panel
frontend and its associated UI Component Library. It adheres strictly to Next.js 14 App Router
conventions, utilizes Tailwind CSS for styling, Framer Motion for animations, and TanStack
Query for data fetching. All components are fully typed with TypeScript and documented with
JSDoc.

1. Project Structure and Configuration
The project is structured as a monorepo using Turborepo and pnpm workspaces to separate the
web application from the reusable UI component library.

File: apps/web/lib/api.ts

import axios from 'axios';
const API_BASE_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL || '/api';
export const api = axios.create({
baseURL: API_BASE_URL,
withCredentials: true,
headers: {
'Content-Type': 'application/json',
},
});
export const handleApiError = (error: unknown): string => {
if (axios.isAxiosError(error)) {
if (error.response) {
if (typeof error.response.data === 'object' && 'message' in
error.response.data) {
return error.response.data.message as string;
}
return `Error: ${error.response.status} - ${error.response.statusText}`;
} else if (error.request) {
return 'No response received from server. Please check your network
connection.';
} else {
return `Request setup error: ${error.message}`;
}
}
return error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'An unexpected error
occurred.';
};
export const fetchData = async <T>(url: string, params?: Record<string, any>):
Promise<T> => {
const response = await api.get<T>(url, { params });
return response.data;
};
export const postData = async <T, R>(url: string, data: T): Promise<R> => {
const response = await api.post<R>(url, data);
return response.data;
};
export const putData = async <T, R>(url: string, data: T): Promise<R> => {
const response = await api.put<R>(url, data);
return response.data;
};
export const deleteData = async <R>(url: string): Promise<R> => {

const response = await api.delete<R>(url);
return response.data;
};

import { Slot } from "@radix-ui/react-slot"
import { cva, type VariantProps } from "class-variance-authority"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
import { Loader2 } from "lucide-react"
const buttonVariants = cva(
"inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-md text-sm
font-medium ring-offset-background transition-colors focus-visible:outline-none
focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2
disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50",
{
variants: {
variant: {
default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90",
destructive: "bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bgdestructive/90",
outline: "border border-input bg-background hover:bg-accent hover:textaccent-foreground",
secondary: "bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground hover:bgsecondary/80",
ghost: "hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
link: "text-primary underline-offset-4 hover:underline",
danger: "bg-danger-500 text-white hover:bg-danger-600",
},
size: {
default: "h-10 px-4 py-2",
sm: "h-9 rounded-md px-3",
lg: "h-11 rounded-md px-8",
icon: "h-10 w-10",
},
},
defaultVariants: {
variant: "default",
size: "default",
},
}
)
export interface ButtonProps
extends React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>,
VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> {
asChild?: boolean
isLoading?: boolean
}
const Button = React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(
({ className, variant, size, asChild = false, isLoading, children, ...props },

ref) => {
const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"
return (
<Comp
className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))}
ref={ref}
disabled={isLoading || props.disabled}
{...props}
>
{isLoading && <Loader2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />}
{children}
</Comp>
)
}
)
Button.displayName = "Button"
export { Button, buttonVariants }

import * as React from "react"
import { createPortal } from "react-dom"
import { X } from "lucide-react"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
import { Button } from "./button"
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "framer-motion"
export interface ModalProps {
isOpen: boolean;
onClose: () => void;
title?: string;
children: React.ReactNode;
className?: string;
}
export function Modal({ isOpen, onClose, title, children, className }:
ModalProps) {
const [mounted, setMounted] = React.useState(false);
React.useEffect(() => {
setMounted(true);
if (isOpen) {
document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
} else {
document.body.style.overflow = 'unset';
}
return () => {
document.body.style.overflow = 'unset';
};
}, [isOpen]);
if (!mounted) return null;
return createPortal(
<AnimatePresence>
{isOpen && (
<div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center">
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
onClick={onClose}
className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm"
/>
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95, y: 20 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1, y: 0 }}
exit={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95, y: 20 }}

className={cn(
"relative z-50 w-full max-w-lg rounded-lg bg-background p-6 shadowlg",
className
)}
>
<div className="flex items-center justify-between mb-4">
{title && <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold">{title}</h2>}
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={onClose} className="h8 w-8 rounded-full">
<X className="h-4 w-4" />
<span className="sr-only">Close</span>
</Button>
</div>
<div>{children}</div>
</motion.div>
</div>
)}
</AnimatePresence>,
document.body
);
}

import * as React from "react"
import {
ColumnDef,
flexRender,
getCoreRowModel,
useReactTable,
getPaginationRowModel,
SortingState,
getSortedRowModel,
ColumnFiltersState,
getFilteredRowModel,
} from "@tanstack/react-table"
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from
"./table"
import { Button } from "./button"
import { Input } from "./input"
interface DataTableProps<TData, TValue> {
columns: ColumnDef<TData, TValue>[]
data: TData[]
searchKey?: string
}
export function DataTable<TData, TValue>({ columns, data, searchKey }:
DataTableProps<TData, TValue>) {
const [sorting, setSorting] = React.useState<SortingState>([])
const [columnFilters, setColumnFilters] = React.useState<ColumnFiltersState>
([])
const table = useReactTable({
data,
columns,
getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(),
getPaginationRowModel: getPaginationRowModel(),
onSortingChange: setSorting,
getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
onColumnFiltersChange: setColumnFilters,
getFilteredRowModel: getFilteredRowModel(),
state: {
sorting,
columnFilters,
},
})
return (
<div>
{searchKey && (
<div className="flex items-center py-4">

<Input
placeholder={`Search ${searchKey}...`}
value={(table.getColumn(searchKey)?.getFilterValue() as string) ??
""}
onChange={(event) =>
table.getColumn(searchKey)?.setFilterValue(event.target.value)}
className="max-w-sm"
/>
</div>
)}
<div className="rounded-md border">
<Table>
<TableHeader>
{table.getHeaderGroups().map((headerGroup) => (
<TableRow key={headerGroup.id}>
{headerGroup.headers.map((header) => {
return (
<TableHead key={header.id}>
{header.isPlaceholder ? null :
flexRender(header.column.columnDef.header, header.getContext())}
</TableHead>
)
})}
</TableRow>
))}
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
{table.getRowModel().rows?.length ? (
table.getRowModel().rows.map((row) => (
<TableRow key={row.id} data-state={row.getIsSelected() &&
"selected"}>
{row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
<TableCell key={cell.id}>
{flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell, cell.getContext())}
</TableCell>
))}
</TableRow>
))
) : (
<TableRow>
<TableCell colSpan={columns.length} className="h-24 text-center">
No results.
</TableCell>
</TableRow>
)}
</TableBody>
</Table>
</div>
<div className="flex items-center justify-end space-x-2 py-4">

<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => table.previousPage()}
disabled={!table.getCanPreviousPage()}>
Previous
</Button>
<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => table.nextPage()}
disabled={!table.getCanNextPage()}>
Next
</Button>
</div>
</div>
)
}

import { Tree, NodeRendererProps } from "react-arborist"
import { Subject, Section, Unit, Level, Lesson, Question } from "@/types"
import { Folder, FileText, HelpCircle, Edit, Trash2, GripVertical } from "lucidereact"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { SubjectModal } from "./subject-modal"
import { SectionModal } from "./section-modal"
import { UnitModal } from "./unit-modal"
import { LevelModal } from "./level-modal"
import { LessonModal } from "./lesson-modal"
import { QuestionModal } from "./question-modal"
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { deleteData, putData } from "@/lib/api"
import { toast } from "sonner"
type TreeNodeData = Subject | Section | Unit | Level | Lesson | Question;
interface CurriculumTreeProps {
data: Subject[];
}
export function CurriculumTree({ data }: CurriculumTreeProps) {
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const [treeData, setTreeData] = React.useState<any[]>([]);
React.useEffect(() => {
const transformData = (items: any[], type: string): any[] => {
return items.map(item => {
let children = [];
if (type === 'subject') children = transformData(item.sections || [],
'section');
else if (type === 'section') children = transformData(item.units || [],
'unit');
else if (type === 'unit') children = transformData(item.levels || [],
'level');
else if (type === 'level') children = transformData(item.lessons || [],
'lesson');
else if (type === 'lesson') children = transformData(item.questions ||
[], 'question');
return {
id: item.id,
name: item.title,
type: type,
originalData: item,
children: children.length > 0 ? children : undefined,
};

});
};
setTreeData(transformData(data, 'subject'));
}, [data]);
const onMove = useMutation({
mutationFn: async (args: { dragIds: string[], parentId: string | null, index:
number }) => {
return putData('/admin/curriculum/reorder', args);
},
onSuccess: () => {
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['curriculumSubjects'] });
toast.success('Reordered successfully');
},
onError: () => {
toast.error('Failed to reorder');
}
});
return (
<div className="h-[600px] w-full">
<Tree
data={treeData}
width="100%"
height={600}
indent={24}
rowHeight={40}
onMove={(args) => onMove.mutate(args)}

SECTION M: Complete Testing Strategy, DevOps, and
Deployment Configuration

SECTION M: Complete Testing Strategy,
DevOps, and Deployment Configuration
This section provides an exhaustive and detailed blueprint for establishing a robust testing
strategy, implementing a streamlined DevOps pipeline, and configuring the deployment
environment for EliTutor. The goal is to ensure high code quality, system reliability, and efficient
delivery of features to Israeli Arab school students (Grades 1-12) using a gamified educational
web platform. Every aspect, from unit tests for core gamification mechanics to end-to-end user

flows, CI/CD pipelines, local development setups, deployment configurations, database
backups, and comprehensive monitoring, is covered with meticulous attention to detail, including
complete TypeScript code, exact file paths, and handling of edge cases.

1. Introduction
EliTutor is a browser-only gamified educational web platform designed to engage students
through interactive learning experiences. The platform’s success hinges on its stability,
performance, and the seamless functioning of its gamification elements. This document outlines
the technical specifications for achieving these goals through a multi-faceted approach
encompassing rigorous testing, automated deployment, and proactive monitoring. The
architecture assumes a monorepo structure, with apps/web for the frontend, apps/api for the
backend, and packages/gamification for shared gamification logic.

2. Testing Strategy
A comprehensive testing strategy is paramount for EliTutor, covering unit tests for critical
business logic and end-to-end tests for core user journeys. This ensures that individual
components function correctly and that the integrated system delivers the intended user
experience.

2.1. Unit Testing with Jest (Gamification Services)
Unit tests will be implemented using Jest, focusing on the core gamification services housed
within packages/gamification . Each service will have a dedicated test file, ensuring
comprehensive coverage of all functions, edge cases, and state transitions. We aim for a
minimum of 20 test cases per service to guarantee robustness.
2.1.1. Hearts Service
The Hearts service manages a student’s available lives or attempts within the platform. Losing
all hearts might result in a temporary lockout or a penalty. The service must handle heart
deductions, additions, and reset mechanisms accurately.
