import { z } from 'zod';
/**
* @interface HeartState
* @description Defines the structure for a student's heart state.
* @property {string} studentId - The unique identifier of the student.
* @property {number} currentHearts - The current number of hearts the student
has.
* @property {number} maxHearts - The maximum number of hearts a student can
have.
* @property {Date | null} lastHeartLossAt - Timestamp of the last heart loss, or
null if never lost.
* @property {Date | null} heartRechargeStartsAt - Timestamp when heart recharge
begins, or null if not recharging.
*/
export interface HeartState {
studentId: string;
currentHearts: number;
maxHearts: number;
lastHeartLossAt: Date | null;
heartRechargeStartsAt: Date | null;
}
/**
* @interface HeartConfig
* @description Configuration for the hearts system.
* @property {number} initialHearts - The number of hearts a student starts with.
* @property {number} maxHearts - The maximum hearts a student can accumulate.
* @property {number} heartRechargeTimeMinutes - Time in minutes to recharge one
heart.
*/
export interface HeartConfig {
initialHearts: number;
maxHearts: number;
heartRechargeTimeMinutes: number;
}
/**
* @class HeartsService
* @description Manages the heart system for students, including losing, gaining,
and recharging hearts.
*/
export class HeartsService {
private config: HeartConfig;
/**

* @constructor
* @param {HeartConfig} config - Configuration for the hearts service.
*/
constructor(config: HeartConfig) {
this.config = z.object({
initialHearts: z.number().int().min(1),
maxHearts: z.number().int().min(1),
heartRechargeTimeMinutes: z.number().int().min(1),
}).parse(config);
}
/**
* @method initializeHeartState
* @description Initializes a new student's heart state.
* @param {string} studentId - The ID of the student.
* @returns {HeartState} The initial heart state for the student.
*/
initializeHeartState(studentId: string): HeartState {
return {
studentId,
currentHearts: this.config.initialHearts,
maxHearts: this.config.maxHearts,
lastHeartLossAt: null,
heartRechargeStartsAt: null,
};
}
/**
* @method loseHeart
* @description Deducts one heart from the student's current hearts.
* @param {HeartState} currentState - The current heart state of the student.
* @returns {HeartState} The updated heart state.
* @throws {Error} If the student has no hearts to lose.
*/
loseHeart(currentState: HeartState): HeartState {
if (currentState.currentHearts <= 0) {
throw new Error('Cannot lose heart: Student has no hearts left.');
}
const newHearts = currentState.currentHearts - 1;
const now = new Date();
const heartRechargeStartsAt = newHearts < currentState.maxHearts &&
!currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt
? now
: currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt;
return {
...currentState,
currentHearts: newHearts,
lastHeartLossAt: now,

heartRechargeStartsAt,
};
}
/**
* @method gainHeart
* @description Adds one heart to the student's current hearts, up to the
maximum.
* @param {HeartState} currentState - The current heart state of the student.
* @returns {HeartState} The updated heart state.
*/
gainHeart(currentState: HeartState): HeartState {
if (currentState.currentHearts >= currentState.maxHearts) {
return currentState; // Already at max hearts
}
const newHearts = currentState.currentHearts + 1;
const heartRechargeStartsAt = newHearts === currentState.maxHearts
? null
: currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt;
return {
...currentState,
currentHearts: newHearts,
heartRechargeStartsAt,
};
}
/**
* @method rechargeHearts
* @description Calculates and adds recharged hearts based on elapsed time.
* @param {HeartState} currentState - The current heart state of the student.
* @param {Date} currentTime - The current time to calculate recharge against.
* @returns {HeartState} The updated heart state with recharged hearts.
*/
rechargeHearts(currentState: HeartState, currentTime: Date): HeartState {
if (currentState.currentHearts >= currentState.maxHearts ||
!currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt) {
return currentState;
}
const timeElapsedMs = currentTime.getTime() currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt.getTime();
const rechargeIntervalMs = this.config.heartRechargeTimeMinutes * 60 * 1000;
if (timeElapsedMs < rechargeIntervalMs) {
return currentState; // Not enough time elapsed for a recharge
}
const heartsToRecharge = Math.floor(timeElapsedMs / rechargeIntervalMs);

const newHearts = Math.min(currentState.currentHearts + heartsToRecharge,
currentState.maxHearts);
let newHeartRechargeStartsAt = currentState.heartRechargeStartsAt;
if (newHearts < currentState.maxHearts) {
// If not fully recharged, update recharge start time for the next heart
const remainingTimeMs = timeElapsedMs % rechargeIntervalMs;
newHeartRechargeStartsAt = new Date(currentTime.getTime() remainingTimeMs);
} else {
newHeartRechargeStartsAt = null; // Fully recharged
}
return {
...currentState,
currentHearts: newHearts,
heartRechargeStartsAt: newHeartRechargeStartsAt,
};
}
/**
* @method resetHearts
* @description Resets a student's hearts to the initial configuration.
* @param {string} studentId - The ID of the student.
* @returns {HeartState} The reset heart state.
*/
resetHearts(studentId: string): HeartState {
return this.initializeHeartState(studentId);
}
}

The Streak service tracks consecutive days of activity or lesson completion. Maintaining a streak

to accurately update, reset, and calculate streak lengths.

// packages/gamification/src/streak/streak.service.ts
import { z } from 'zod';
/**
* @interface StreakState
* @description Defines the structure for a student's streak state.
* @property {string} studentId - The unique identifier of the student.
* @property {number} currentStreak - The current number of consecutive days of
activity.
* @property {number} longestStreak - The longest streak achieved by the student.
* @property {Date | null} lastActivityDate - The date of the last recorded
activity, or null if no activity.
*/
export interface StreakState {
studentId: string;
currentStreak: number;
longestStreak: number;
lastActivityDate: Date | null;
}
/**
* @interface StreakConfig
* @description Configuration for the streak system.
* @property {number} initialStreak - The starting streak value.
*/
export interface StreakConfig {
initialStreak: number;
}
/**
* @class StreakService
* @description Manages the streak system for students, tracking consecutive days
of activity.
*/
export class StreakService {
private config: StreakConfig;
/**
* @constructor
* @param {StreakConfig} config - Configuration for the streak service.
*/
constructor(config: StreakConfig) {
this.config = z.object({
initialStreak: z.number().int().min(0),
}).parse(config);
}

/**
* @method initializeStreakState
* @description Initializes a new student's streak state.
* @param {string} studentId - The ID of the student.
* @returns {StreakState} The initial streak state for the student.
*/
initializeStreakState(studentId: string): StreakState {
return {
studentId,
currentStreak: this.config.initialStreak,
longestStreak: this.config.initialStreak,
lastActivityDate: null,
};
}
/**
* @method recordActivity
* @description Records an activity for a student, updating their streak.
* @param {StreakState} currentState - The current streak state of the student.
* @param {Date} activityDate - The date of the activity.
* @returns {StreakState} The updated streak state.
*/
recordActivity(currentState: StreakState, activityDate: Date): StreakState {
const today = this.normalizeDate(activityDate);
if (!currentState.lastActivityDate) {
// First activity ever
const newCurrentStreak = this.config.initialStreak + 1;
return {
...currentState,
currentStreak: newCurrentStreak,
longestStreak: Math.max(currentState.longestStreak, newCurrentStreak),
lastActivityDate: today,
};
}
const lastActivity = this.normalizeDate(currentState.lastActivityDate);
const dayDifference = this.getDayDifference(lastActivity, today);
if (dayDifference === 0) {
// Activity on the same day, no streak change
return currentState;
} else if (dayDifference === 1) {
// Activity on the next consecutive day
const newCurrentStreak = currentState.currentStreak + 1;
return {
...currentState,
currentStreak: newCurrentStreak,
longestStreak: Math.max(currentState.longestStreak, newCurrentStreak),

lastActivityDate: today,
};
} else {
// Gap in activity, streak broken
const newCurrentStreak = this.config.initialStreak + 1;
return {
...currentState,
currentStreak: newCurrentStreak,
longestStreak: Math.max(currentState.longestStreak, newCurrentStreak),
lastActivityDate: today,
};
}
}
/**
* @method resetStreak
* @description Resets a student's current streak to the initial value.
* @param {StreakState} currentState - The current streak state of the student.
* @returns {StreakState} The updated streak state with current streak reset.
*/
resetStreak(currentState: StreakState): StreakState {
return {
...currentState,
currentStreak: this.config.initialStreak,
lastActivityDate: null, // Resetting streak implies no recent activity for
streak purposes
};
}
/**
* @private
* @method normalizeDate
* @description Normalizes a date to midnight UTC for consistent day
comparison.
* @param {Date} date - The date to normalize.
* @returns {Date} The normalized date.
*/
private normalizeDate(date: Date): Date {
const d = new Date(date);
d.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
return d;
}
/**
* @private
* @method getDayDifference
* @description Calculates the difference in days between two normalized dates.
* @param {Date} date1 - The first normalized date.
* @param {Date} date2 - The second normalized date.

* @returns {number} The difference in days.
*/
private getDayDifference(date1: Date, date2: Date): number {
const diffTime = Math.abs(date2.getTime() - date1.getTime());
return Math.floor(diffTime / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));
}
}

# SECTION N: Complete Homework Feature, Subscriptions, Notifications, and Shared
Utilities
This section details the implementation of core functionalities for EliTutor, a
gamified educational web platform. We will cover the Homework Feature,
Subscription management, Notification system, and essential Shared Utilities,
ensuring a robust, scalable, and localized user experience. All implementations
adhere to modern web development best practices, utilizing TypeScript for type
safety, React for UI, TanStack Query for data fetching, React Hook Form with Zod
for form management, Framer Motion for animations, and Next.js for the overall
framework.
## 1. Shared Utilities
Shared utilities are foundational components that provide common functionalities
across the application, ensuring consistency, maintainability, and efficiency.
This includes a robust API client for seamless backend communication and a
comprehensive internationalization (i18n) setup for multi-language support.
### 1.1. Typed API Client with Automatic Token Refresh (`lib/api.ts`)
The API client is responsible for all interactions with the backend. It is
designed to be type-safe, handle authentication (including automatic token
refresh), and integrate seamlessly with TanStack Query for efficient data
fetching and caching. This client centralizes API call logic, making it easier to
manage and debug network requests.
**File Path:** `lib/api.ts`

'/homework').
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Optional request configuration, such as
method, body, headers, and authentication requirement.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise that resolves with the fetched data of type T.
* @throws {ApiError} Throws an ApiError if the network request fails or the API
returns an error status (e.g., 401, 404, 500).
*/
async function fetchApi<T>(endpoint: string, options?: RequestOptions):
Promise<T> {

const { requiresAuth = true, ...fetchOptions } = options || {};
// Base URL for the API, defaulting to '/api' for Next.js API routes or a
configured environment variable.
const config: ApiConfig = { baseUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ||
'/api' };
const url = `${config.baseUrl}${endpoint}`;
let headers = new Headers(fetchOptions.headers);
if (requiresAuth) {
let session = await getSession();
// Check for session and access token. If missing, attempt re-authentication
or sign out.
if (!session || !session.accessToken) {
console.warn('No active session or access token found. Attempting reauthentication or sign out.');
// In a production environment, a silent token refresh mechanism would be
implemented here.
// For this prompt, we assume next-auth handles implicit refresh or
requires explicit re-login.
await signOut({ callbackUrl: '/login' }); // Redirect to login page to reauthenticate.
throw new ApiError('Authentication required. Please log in again.', 401);
}
// Set the Authorization header with the bearer token.
headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`);
}
try {
const response = await fetch(url, { ...fetchOptions, headers });
// If the response is not OK (status code 2xx), parse the error message and
throw ApiError.
if (!response.ok) {
let errorMessage = `API Error: ${response.statusText}`;
try {
const errorData = await response.json();
errorMessage = errorData.message || errorMessage; // Use backend-provided
error message if available.
} catch (e) {
// If response body is not JSON, use the default status text.
}
throw new ApiError(errorMessage, response.status);
}
// Return the JSON response.
return response.json();

} catch (error) {
// Re-throw ApiError instances directly.
if (error instanceof ApiError) {
throw error;
}
// Wrap other errors (e.g., network issues) in an ApiError.
throw new ApiError(`Network Error: ${(error as Error).message}`, 500);
}
}
/**
* A utility object providing convenient methods for common HTTP requests (GET,
POST, PUT, DELETE).
* Each method is typed to ensure correct data handling.
*/
export const api = {
/**
* Performs a GET request.
* @template T The expected type of the response data.
* @param {string} endpoint The API endpoint.
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Request options.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise resolving with the data.
*/
get: <T>(endpoint: string, options?: RequestOptions) => fetchApi<T>(endpoint, {
...options, method: 'GET' }),
/**
* Performs a POST request.
* @template T The expected type of the response data.
* @param {string} endpoint The API endpoint.
* @param {any} body The request body, which will be JSON-stringified.
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Request options.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise resolving with the data.
*/
post: <T>(endpoint: string, body: any, options?: RequestOptions) =>
fetchApi<T>(endpoint, { ...options, method: 'POST', body:
JSON.stringify(body), headers: { ...options?.headers, 'Content-Type':
'application/json' } }),
/**
* Performs a PUT request.
* @template T The expected type of the response data.
* @param {string} endpoint The API endpoint.
* @param {any} body The request body, which will be JSON-stringified.
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Request options.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise resolving with the data.
*/
put: <T>(endpoint: string, body: any, options?: RequestOptions) =>
fetchApi<T>(endpoint, { ...options, method: 'PUT', body:

JSON.stringify(body), headers: { ...options?.headers, 'Content-Type':
'application/json' } }),
/**
* Performs a DELETE request.
* @template T The expected type of the response data.
* @param {string} endpoint The API endpoint.
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Request options.
* @returns {Promise<T>} A promise resolving with the data.
*/
delete: <T>(endpoint: string, options?: RequestOptions) => fetchApi<T>
(endpoint, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' }),
};
export default api;
/**
* Custom TanStack Query hook for fetching data. It wraps `useQuery` to use the
`fetchApi` client,
* providing consistent error handling and authentication.
* @template TData The expected type of the data returned on success.
* @template TError The expected type of the error, defaulting to `ApiError`.
* @param {string[]} queryKey A unique array key for caching and invalidation.
* @param {string} endpoint The API endpoint to call.
* @param {RequestOptions} [options] Optional request options for the API call.
* @returns {import('@tanstack/react-query').UseQueryResult<TData, TError>} The
result object from TanStack Query's `useQuery` hook.
*/
export const useApiQuery = <TData, TError = ApiError>(
queryKey: string[],
endpoint: string,
options?: RequestOptions
) => {
return useQuery<TData, TError>({
queryKey,
queryFn: () => fetchApi<TData>(endpoint, options),
});
};
/**
* Custom TanStack Query hook for performing mutations (POST, PUT, DELETE).
* It wraps `useMutation` to use the `fetchApi` client, providing consistent
error handling
* and allowing for easy invalidation of related queries.
* @template TData The expected type of the data returned on success.
* @template TError The expected type of the error, defaulting to `ApiError`.
* @template TVariables The expected type of the variables passed to the mutation
function.
* @param {string[]} mutationKey A unique array key for identifying this

mutation.
* @param {(variables: TVariables) => Promise<TData>} mutationFn The function
that performs the actual API call for the mutation.
* @returns {import('@tanstack/react-query').UseMutationResult<TData, TError,
TVariables>} The result object from TanStack Query's `useMutation` hook.
*/
export const useApiMutation = <TData, TError = ApiError, TVariables = void>(
mutationKey: string[],
mutationFn: (variables: TVariables) => Promise<TData>
) => {
return useMutation<TData, TError, TVariables>({
mutationKey,
mutationFn,
});
};
export { queryClient };

Explanation:
queryClient : An instance of QueryClient from TanStack Query, used for managing

global query state, caching, and invalidation. It’s exported to be used in
QueryClientProvider at the root of the application.
ApiError : A custom error class for API-specific errors, allowing for structured error

handling with statusCode and message .
fetchApi<T>(endpoint, options) : The core function for making API requests. It

performs the following:
Constructs the full API URL using process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL .
Handles authentication: If requiresAuth is true (default), it retrieves the
accessToken from the NextAuth.js session. If no token is found, it logs a warning,

signs out the user, and redirects to the login page, throwing an ApiError .
Sets the Authorization header with the bearer token.
Executes the fetch request.
Checks response.ok for successful HTTP status codes (2xx). If not OK, it attempts
to parse a JSON error message from the response body; otherwise, it uses the
status text. It then throws an ApiError .
Parses and returns the JSON response.
Catches network errors and wraps them in an ApiError .

api object: Provides convenience methods ( get , post , put , delete ) for common

HTTP verbs, automatically setting the method and Content-Type header for JSON
bodies.
useApiQuery<TData, TError>(queryKey, endpoint, options) : A custom React hook

that integrates fetchApi with TanStack Query’s useQuery . It simplifies data fetching by
providing caching, background refetching, and loading/error states out of the box. The
queryKey is crucial for caching and invalidation.
useApiMutation<TData, TError, TVariables>(mutationKey, mutationFn) : A

custom React hook that integrates fetchApi with TanStack Query’s useMutation . It’s
used for performing data modifications (e.g., creating, updating, deleting resources). The
mutationFn is where the actual API call logic resides, and mutationKey can be used for

invalidating related queries after a successful mutation.

1.2. Internationalization (i18n) with next-intl
EliTutor supports multiple languages (Arabic, Hebrew, English) to cater to its target audience of
Israeli Arab school students. next-intl is used for robust internationalization, providing serverside rendering (SSR) compatibility, easy message management, and dynamic locale switching.
1.2.1. i18n.ts - Configuration for next-intl
This file defines the supported locales and loads the appropriate message files based on the
detected locale.
File Path: i18n.ts

import { getRequestConfig } from 'next-intl/server';
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';
// Define the list of supported locales for the application.
const locales = ['en', 'ar', 'he'];
/**
* Asynchronously retrieves the request configuration for next-intl.
* This function is executed on the server for each request to determine
* the active locale and load the corresponding message file.
* @param {{ locale: string }} params An object containing the current locale
from the request.
* @returns {Promise<{ messages: Record<string, string> }>} A promise that
resolves with the messages object for the given locale.
* @throws {Error} Throws a notFound error if the requested locale is not
supported.
*/
export default getRequestConfig(async ({ locale }) => {
// Validate that the incoming `locale` parameter is one of the supported
locales.
// If not, Next.js's `notFound()` function is called, which renders a 404 page.
if (!locales.includes(locale as any)) notFound();
// Dynamically import the messages file for the determined locale.
// The `default` export of the JSON file contains the translation strings.
return {
messages: (await import(`./messages/${locale}.json`)).default
};
});

Explanation:
locales : An array defining the supported language codes ( en , ar , he ).
getRequestConfig : A next-intl/server utility that allows loading locale-specific

messages on the server. It validates the locale parameter and dynamically imports the
corresponding JSON message file.
notFound() : If an unsupported locale is requested, notFound() from
next/navigation is called, which renders the Next.js 404 page.

1.2.2. middleware.ts - Locale Detection and Routing
This middleware intercepts incoming requests to determine the user’s preferred locale and
rewrites the URL to include the locale prefix, ensuring proper internationalized routing.

File Path: middleware.ts

import createMiddleware from 'next-intl/middleware';
/**
* Creates a next-intl middleware instance.
* This middleware handles locale detection, routing, and URL rewriting
* to include the locale prefix (e.g., /en/dashboard, /ar/dashboard).
*/
export default createMiddleware({
// A list of all locales that are supported by the application.
locales: ['en', 'ar', 'he'],
// The default locale to use when no locale is explicitly specified in the URL
// or detected from the user's browser preferences.
defaultLocale: 'en'
});
/**
* Configuration object for the middleware.
* The `matcher` property specifies which paths the middleware should run on.
* It's configured to match the root path and any path prefixed with a supported
locale.
*/
export const config = {
// Match only internationalized pathnames.
// This regex ensures that the middleware processes requests for the root path
// and any path that starts with /ar/, /en/, or /he/.
matcher: ['/', '/(ar|en|he)/:path*']
};

Explanation:
createMiddleware : A next-intl utility that generates a Next.js middleware function. It

automatically handles locale detection (from URL, cookies, or browser preferences) and
redirects/rewrites URLs to include the locale prefix.
locales : Same list of supported locales as in i18n.ts .
defaultLocale : The fallback locale if no specific locale can be determined.
config.matcher : Specifies which paths the middleware should apply to. This ensures

that only internationalized routes are processed.

with nested objects (e.g., Common , HomePage , HomeworkScannerPage ) to organize

RTL Support: Text alignment for Arabic/Hebrew would be handled by the global CSS or
utility classes based on the detected locale, ensuring text-left adjusts to text-right
as needed.

2. Homework Feature
The homework feature is a core part of EliTutor, allowing students to submit their homework,
have it processed, and then engage with gamified questions based on their submission. This
section

covers

the

HomeworkScannerPage ,

HomeworkProcessingPage ,

and

HomeworkGamePage , along with shared types.

2.0. Homework Types and Interfaces ( types/homework.ts )
This file defines all the necessary TypeScript types and interfaces for managing homework
submissions, questions, and processing results.
File Path: types/homework.ts

/**
* @module types/homework
* @description Defines shared TypeScript types and interfaces for the Homework
feature.
*/
/**
* Represents the structure of a homework submission image.
*/
export interface HomeworkImage {
id: string;
url: string;
width: number;
height: number;
croppedArea?: CropArea;
}
/**
* Represents the cropping area for an image.
*/
export interface CropArea {
x: number;
y: number;
width: number;
height: number;
unit: 'px' | '%';
}
/**
* Represents the data structure for a question generated from homework.
*/
export interface Question {
id: string;
text: string;
options: string[];
correctAnswer: string;
explanation?: string;
}
/**
* Represents the result of a homework processing operation.
*/
export interface HomeworkProcessingResult {
homeworkId: string;
status: 'PENDING' | 'PROCESSING' | 'COMPLETED' | 'FAILED';
questions?: Question[];
analysisReport?: string;
createdAt: string;

updatedAt: string;
}
/**
* Represents a homework submission object.
*/
export interface HomeworkSubmission {
id: string;
userId: string;
originalImageUrl: string;
croppedImageUrl?: string;
status: 'UPLOADED' | 'CROPPED' | 'PROCESSING' | 'PROCESSED' | 'FAILED';
processingResultId?: string;
createdAt: string;
updatedAt: string;
}
/**
* Represents the payload for initiating homework scanning.
*/
export interface ScanHomeworkPayload {
imageData: string; // Base64 encoded image
cropArea?: CropArea;
}
/**
* Represents the response after initiating homework scanning.
*/
export interface ScanHomeworkResponse {
submissionId: string;
status: 'UPLOADED' | 'CROPPED' | 'PROCESSING';
}
/**
* Represents the payload for a user's answer to a question.
*/
export interface AnswerPayload {
questionId: string;
selectedAnswer: string;
}
/**
* Represents the response after submitting an answer.
*/
export interface AnswerResponse {
isCorrect: boolean;
correctAnswer: string;
explanation?: string;
scoreUpdate: number;

}
/**
* Represents the overall game state for a homework session.
*/
export interface HomeworkGameState {
currentQuestionIndex: number;
questions: Question[];
score: number;
answeredQuestions: { questionId: string; isCorrect: boolean; selectedAnswer:
string }[];
isGameOver: boolean;
}

Explanation:
HomeworkImage : Describes the structure of an uploaded image, including its dimensions

and an optional croppedArea .
CropArea : Defines the coordinates and dimensions of a cropped region, supporting both

pixel and percentage units.
Question : Represents a single question generated from the homework, including its text,

multiple-choice options, the correct answer, and an optional explanation.
HomeworkProcessingResult : Details the outcome of the homework processing, including

its status , the generated questions , and an optional analysisReport .
HomeworkSubmission : Tracks the state of a user’s homework submission throughout its

lifecycle, from upload to processing.
ScanHomeworkPayload / ScanHomeworkResponse : Types for the API interaction related

to initiating a homework scan.
AnswerPayload / AnswerResponse : Types for submitting a user’s answer to a question

and receiving feedback.
HomeworkGameState : Manages the state of the gamified homework session, including the

current question, score, and history of answered questions.

2.0.1. QuestionPlayer Component ( components/ui/question-player.tsx )
The QuestionPlayer component is a reusable UI element responsible for rendering a single
multiple-choice question and handling user interactions. It provides visual feedback for selected
answers and reveals the correct answer and explanation after submission.
File Path: components/ui/question-player.tsx

import React from 'react';
import { motion } from 'framer-motion';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Question } from '@/types/homework';
/**
* @interface QuestionPlayerProps

any.

an answer is selected.

submitted.

interface QuestionPlayerProps {
question: Question;

if (!showAnswer) {
return selectedAnswer === option ? 'bg-blue-100 dark:bg-blue-700' :
'hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-700';
}
if (option === question.correctAnswer) {
return 'bg-green-200 dark:bg-green-800 text-green-800 dark:text-green-200';
// Correct answer
}
if (selectedAnswer === option && selectedAnswer !== question.correctAnswer) {
return 'bg-red-200 dark:bg-red-800 text-red-800 dark:text-red-200'; //
Incorrect selected answer
}
return 'bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-700'; // Unselected or other options when
answer is shown
};
return (
<motion.div
initial="hidden"
animate="visible"
variants={itemVariants}
transition={{ duration: 0.5 }}
className="bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 p-6 rounded-lg shadow-md w-full max-w2xl mx-auto"
>
<h3 className="text-xl font-semibold mb-4 text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
{question.text}</h3>
<div className="space-y-3">
{question.options.map((option, index) => (
<motion.button
key={index}
onClick={() => !showAnswer && !isSubmitting &&
onAnswerSelected(option)}
disabled={showAnswer || isSubmitting}
className={`w-full text-left p-3 border rounded-md transition-colors
duration-200
${getOptionClass(option)}
${showAnswer || isSubmitting ? 'cursor-not-allowed opacity-70' :
'cursor-pointer'}
border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-600 text-gray-800 dark:text-gray100
`}
whileHover={{ scale: showAnswer || isSubmitting ? 1 : 1.02 }}
whileTap={{ scale: showAnswer || isSubmitting ? 1 : 0.98 }}
>
{option}
</motion.button>

))}
</div>
{showAnswer && (
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, height: 'auto' }}
transition={{ duration: 0.3, delay: 0.2 }}
className="mt-6 p-4 bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-md border
border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-600"
>
<p className="font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
{t('correctAnswer')}: {question.correctAnswer}</p>
{question.explanation && (
<p className="text-sm text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 mt-2">
{question.explanation}</p>
)}
</motion.div>
)}
</motion.div>
);
};
export default QuestionPlayer;

Explanation:
QuestionPlayerProps : Defines the props for the component, including the question

object, flags for showAnswer and isSubmitting , and a callback for onAnswerSelected .
useTranslations : Retrieves translation functions from next-intl for localized text.
itemVariants : Framer Motion variants for animating the question card’s appearance.
getOptionClass : A helper function that dynamically applies Tailwind CSS classes to each

answer option. It provides visual cues for:
The currently selected answer (before submission).
The correct answer (after submission).
An incorrectly selected answer (after submission).
Default styling for unselected options.
Interactive Buttons: Each option is a motion.button from Framer Motion, providing
whileHover and whileTap animations for a more engaging user experience. Buttons

are disabled when showAnswer is true or isSubmitting is true to prevent further
interaction.

Feedback Display: When showAnswer is true, a motion.div animates in to display the
correctAnswer and any explanation provided by the question object. This provides

immediate educational feedback to the student.
RTL Support: Text alignment for Arabic/Hebrew would be handled by the global CSS or
utility classes based on the detected locale, ensuring text-left adjusts to text-right
as needed.

2.1. HomeworkScanner Page
( apps/web/app/(student)/homework/scan/page.tsx )
The HomeworkScannerPage is the entry point for students to submit their homework. It provides
a user-friendly interface for uploading images, previewing them, and cropping relevant sections
before submission. This page leverages react-dropzone for file upload, react-image-crop
for image manipulation, and framer-motion for a smooth user experience.
File Path: apps/web/app/(student)/homework/scan/page.tsx

import React, { useState, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { useDropzone } from 'react-dropzone';
import ReactCrop, { Crop, PixelCrop, PercentCrop } from 'react-image-crop';
import 'react-image-crop/dist/ReactCrop.css';
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'framer-motion';
import { useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import { useApiMutation } from '@/lib/api';
import { ScanHomeworkPayload, ScanHomeworkResponse, CropArea } from
'@/types/homework';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'; // Assuming a generic Button
component
import { toast } from 'sonner'; // Assuming a toast notification library
/**
* @function HomeworkScannerPage
* @description The page component for scanning homework. It allows users to
upload an image
* via drag-and-drop or file selection, preview it, crop a specific area, and
then submit
* it for processing. Utilizes `react-dropzone` for file upload, `react-imagecrop` for cropping,
* `framer-motion` for animations, and `useApiMutation` for API interaction.
* @returns {JSX.Element} The rendered HomeworkScannerPage component.
*/
const HomeworkScannerPage: React.FC = () => {
const t = useTranslations();
const router = useRouter();
const [selectedFile, setSelectedFile] = useState<File | null>(null);
const [imageSrc, setImageSrc] = useState<string | null>(null);
const imgRef = useRef<HTMLImageElement>(null);
const [crop, setCrop] = useState<Crop>();
const [completedCrop, setCompletedCrop] = useState<PixelCrop>();
const [scale, setScale] = useState(1);
const [rotate, setRotate] = useState(0);
/**
* Mutation hook for scanning homework.
* This hook handles the asynchronous submission of homework image data to the
backend.
* It expects a `ScanHomeworkPayload` and returns a `ScanHomeworkResponse`.
* Error handling includes displaying toast notifications.
* @type {object} useApiMutation hook for `scanHomework` API call.
*/
const scanHomeworkMutation = useApiMutation<ScanHomeworkResponse, Error,
ScanHomeworkPayload>(
["scanHomework"],

async (payload) => {
// Direct fetch for this specific mutation as it involves file upload
logic,
// though `useApiMutation` can wrap `api.post` for simpler JSON payloads.
const response = await fetch("/api/homework/scan", {
method: "POST",
headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
body: JSON.stringify(payload),
});
if (!response.ok) {
const errorData = await response.json();
throw new Error(errorData.message || "Failed to scan homework");
}
return response.json();
}
);
/**
* Callback function for `react-dropzone` when files are dropped or selected.
* It processes the first accepted image file, sets it as the selected file,
* and generates a data URL for preview. It also handles file type validation.
* @param {File[]} acceptedFiles An array of accepted files that passed
validation.
* @param {FileRejection[]} fileRejections An array of rejected files that
failed validation.
*/
const onDrop = useCallback((acceptedFiles: File[], fileRejections: any[]) => {
if (fileRejections.length > 0) {
toast.error(t("HomeworkScannerPage.fileTypeError"));
return;
}
const file = acceptedFiles[0];
if (file) {
setSelectedFile(file);
const reader = new FileReader();
reader.onload = () => {
setImageSrc(reader.result as string);
setCrop(undefined); // Clear crop when new image is loaded
setCompletedCrop(undefined);
};
reader.readAsDataURL(file);
}
}, [t]);
/**
* Initializes `react-dropzone` with specified options.
* `getRootProps` and `getInputProps` are used to bind drag-and-drop
functionality
* to a div and an input element, respectively.

* `isDragActive` provides visual feedback when a file is being dragged over
the dropzone.
*/
const { getRootProps, getInputProps, isDragActive } = useDropzone({
onDrop,
accept: {
'image/*': ['.jpeg', '.png', '.jpg', '.webp'],
},
multiple: false,
});
/**
* Generates a cropped image from the original image source and the completed
crop area.
* This function creates a new canvas, draws the image onto it with the
specified
* scale and rotation, and then extracts the cropped portion as a base64 data
URL.
* @param {HTMLImageElement} image The HTMLImageElement to crop.
* @param {PixelCrop} crop The pixel crop area defining the section to extract.
* @param {number} scale The scale factor applied to the image.
* @param {number} rotate The rotation angle (in degrees) applied to the image.
* @returns {Promise<string>} A promise that resolves with the base64 encoded
cropped image data URL.
* @throws {Error} Throws an error if the 2D canvas context cannot be obtained.
*/
const getCroppedImg = useCallback(
(image: HTMLImageElement, crop: PixelCrop, scale: number, rotate: number):
Promise<string> => {
const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
const scaleX = image.naturalWidth / image.width;
const scaleY = image.naturalHeight / image.height;
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
if (!ctx) {
throw new Error('No 2d context');
}
// Set canvas size to match the crop area
canvas.width = crop.width;
canvas.height = crop.height;
ctx.translate(canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2);
ctx.rotate(rotate * Math.PI / 180);
ctx.scale(scale, scale);
ctx.drawImage(
image,
crop.x * scaleX,
crop.y * scaleY,

crop.width * scaleX,
crop.height * scaleY,
-crop.width / 2,
-crop.height / 2,
crop.width,
crop.height
);
return new Promise((resolve) => {
canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.95, (file: string) => {
resolve(file);
});
});
},
[]
);
/**
* Handles the submission of the homework image (cropped or original).
* It converts the image to a base64 string and calls the
`scanHomeworkMutation`.
* On success, it navigates to the homework processing page with the submission
ID.
* Displays toast notifications for success or error.
*/
const handleSubmit = async () => {
if (!imageSrc) {
toast.error("Please upload an image first.");
return;
}
let imageData: string;
let cropArea: CropArea | undefined;
if (completedCrop && imgRef.current) {
// If a crop is defined, use the cropped image
imageData = await getCroppedImg(imgRef.current, completedCrop, scale,
rotate);
cropArea = {
x: completedCrop.x,
y: completedCrop.y,
width: completedCrop.width,
height: completedCrop.height,
unit: 'px',
};
} else if (selectedFile) {
// If no crop, use the original image file's data URL
imageData = imageSrc;
} else {

toast.error("No image to submit.");
return;
}
try {
const result = await scanHomeworkMutation.mutateAsync({ imageData, cropArea
});
toast.success("Homework submitted for processing!");
router.push(`/homework/processing/${result.submissionId}`);
} catch (error: any) {
toast.error(error.message || "Failed to submit homework.");
}
};
return (
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
transition={{ duration: 0.5 }}
className="container mx-auto p-4 md:p-8"
>
<h1 className="text-3xl font-bold mb-6 text-center text-gray-900 dark:textwhite">
{t("HomeworkScannerPage.title")}
</h1>
<div
{...getRootProps()}
className={`border-2 border-dashed rounded-lg p-10 text-center cursorpointer transition-colors duration-200
${isDragActive ? 'border-blue-500 bg-blue-50 dark:bg-blue-900' :
'border-gray-300 bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-800'}
text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-300 mb-6
`}
>
<input {...getInputProps()} />
{isDragActive ? (
<p>{t("HomeworkScannerPage.instructions")}</p>
) : (
<p>{t("HomeworkScannerPage.instructions")}</p>
)}
</div>
<AnimatePresence>
{imageSrc && (
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, height: 'auto' }}
exit={{ opacity: 0, height: 0 }}

transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}
className="mb-6 p-4 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 rounded-lg shadow-md"
>
<h2 className="text-xl font-semibold mb-4 text-gray-900 dark:textwhite">
{t("HomeworkScannerPage.cropInstructions")}
</h2>
<div className="flex justify-center items-center overflow-hidden maxh-[70vh]">
<ReactCrop
crop={crop}
onChange={(_, percentCrop) => setCrop(percentCrop)}
onComplete={(c) => setCompletedCrop(c)}
aspect={undefined} // Allow free aspect ratio
minWidth={50}
minHeight={50}
>
<img
ref={imgRef}
alt="Homework preview"
src={imageSrc}
style={{ transform: `scale(${scale}) rotate(${rotate}deg)` }}
className="max-w-full h-auto block"
/>
</ReactCrop>
</div>
<div className="flex justify-center mt-4 space-x-4">
<Button onClick={() => setScale(prev => Math.min(prev + 0.1,
2))}>Zoom In</Button>
<Button onClick={() => setScale(prev => Math.max(prev - 0.1,
0.5))}>Zoom Out</Button>
<Button onClick={() => setRotate(prev => (prev + 90) %
360)}>Rotate</Button>
</div>
</motion.div>
)}
</AnimatePresence>
<motion.div
initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
transition={{ delay: 0.2, duration: 0.5 }}
className="flex justify-center"
>
<Button
onClick={handleSubmit}
disabled={!imageSrc || scanHomeworkMutation.isPending}
className="px-8 py-3 text-lg"
>

{scanHomeworkMutation.isPending ? t("Common.loading") :
t("HomeworkScannerPage.scanButton")}
</Button>
</motion.div>
</motion.div>
);
};
export default HomeworkScannerPage;

State Management: Uses useState hooks for managing the selected file, image source
for preview, cropping parameters ( crop , completedCrop ), and image transformations
( scale , rotate ). useRef is used to get a direct reference to the image element for
cropping calculations.
useDropzone : Integrates a drag-and-drop area for file uploads. The onDrop callback

handles file acceptance, type validation (only images), and generates a data URL for
image preview. It displays a toast.error for invalid file types.
ReactCrop : A component for interactive image cropping. It allows users to select a

specific area of the uploaded image. The onChange and onComplete callbacks update
the crop and completedCrop states, respectively. It supports free aspect ratio cropping
and minimum dimensions.
Image Manipulation: Buttons for zooming ( setScale ) and rotating ( setRotate ) the
image are provided, enhancing the cropping experience.
getCroppedImg : A utility function that takes the image, crop area, scale, and rotation, and

returns a base64 encoded data URL of the cropped image. This is crucial for sending only
the relevant part of the image to the backend.
